findings.title: Discarding an untracked file reports success and deletes nothing (includeUntracked never sent)
findings.evidence: src/bridges/commands.ts:191-197 sends `{args:{repo, paths, opts}}` with opts defaulted to `{}`; src/stores/workingCopy.ts:52-61 calls it with no options; the only caller is App.vue:918. src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:269-273 hits `if status.contains(Status::WT_NEW) && !tracked { if opts.include_untracked { to_delete.push(..) } continue; }` — with include_untracked=false the path is skipped and the function returns Ok(()) having written nothing; src-tauri/src/domain/working_copy.rs:519-529 declares `include_untracked: false` by default, and src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:412-415 returns `changed(cx)` (a fresh delta still containing the file). App.vue:919 then pushes the success toast for `ok === true`.
findings.repro: 1. In any repo create an untracked file (`echo hi > scratch.txt`). 2. Working copy tab → the file appears in the 未跟踪 section; hover the row and click the ↩ discard button (WorkingCopyFileList.vue:159-167; the detail bar's 放弃 button is shown for every non-staged, non-unmerged entry, WorkingCopyFileDetail.vue:105-113). 3. Confirm the dialogue whose zh-CN copy says 「这会永久放弃此文件中的改动，无法撤销。」. 4. Observe the toast 「已放弃该文件的改动。」 while the row is still listed and the file is still on disk. The same happens through the detail bar's 放弃 button.
findings.expected: The untracked file is deleted (or the command refuses loudly so no success toast is shown).
findings.actual: The engine skips the path (`include_untracked` defaults to false), returns Ok, and the UI shows the success toast 「已放弃该文件的改动。」 / "Discarded the file's changes." while the file and its row remain.
findings.fix: The store/composable must pass the delete intent: `wcPathsDiscard(repo, paths, { includeUntracked: <any selected row is untracked>, confirmToken: "confirmed" })` after the confirmation dialogue (the engine already enforces the token at index.rs:222-233). Additionally, make the engine refuse when the selection is untracked-only and include_untracked is false, instead of silently doing nothing (a `paths_discarded` count or an ErrorPayload naming the untracked paths).
findings.testIdea: src/stores/workingCopy.test.ts: mock `commands.wcPathsDiscard`, call `discard(repo, ["scratch.txt"])` with an untracked entry, assert the invoke payload's `opts.includeUntracked === true` and `opts.confirmToken` is non-empty. Rust side (src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs tests): `discard_paths(&repo, &["scratch.txt"], &DiscardOptions::default())` must either delete the file or return `Err` — assert `!dir.join("scratch.txt").exists() || result.is_err()`.

notes:
NOT REFUTED — reproduced end to end; only the severity is wrong (major, not blocker).

1. Real git baseline (scratch repo /tmp/verify-WC-01/repo). `git checkout -- scratch.txt` and `git restore --worktree -- scratch.txt` on an untracked path both fail loudly (exit 1, "pathspec did not match any file(s) known to git"); only `git clean -f scratch.txt` deletes (exit 0, file gone). The reference tool refuses rather than silently succeeding. Also confirmed `git ls-files --error-unmatch scratch2.txt` → exit 1, i.e. the untracked path has no index entry — exactly what `status::lookup(&index, path, 0).is_some()` returns None for.

2. Wire payload walk (built and ran /tmp/verify-WC-01/serde-check, a standalone serde project copying the two structs verbatim from the snapshot). Feeding the exact JSON /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/bridges/commands.ts:196 emits when opts is omitted — {"args":{"repo":"/tmp/repo","paths":["scratch.txt"],"opts":{}}} — deserializes *successfully* into `DiscardOptions { include_untracked: false, confirm_token: None }` (`#[serde(default, rename_all="camelCase")]` + `#[derive(Default)]`, and `opts: DiscardOptions` also carries `#[serde(default)]` at src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:383). No serde error, no unknown-key rejection — a silent default. The same run confirms the proposed payload parses: {"includeUntracked":true,"confirmToken":"confirmed"} → include_untracked=true, confirm_token=Some("confirmed").

3. Engine computation for that opts value. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:268-273: status for scratch.txt is WT_NEW (status_map at :945-960 sets include_untracked(true); entry_rows/workdir_code at status.rs:306-309 map WT_NEW → FileStatus::Untracked with staged=false), `tracked = false`, so the branch is `if opts.include_untracked { to_delete.push(..) } continue;` — with false, nothing is pushed and the loop continues. to_delete/to_head/to_index are all empty, both checkout blocks are `!is_empty()`-guarded, and the function returns Ok(()) at :304 having written nothing. A no-op returning success.

4. Nothing intercepts it. validate_paths (src-tauri/src/validation/working_copy.rs:20-43) rejects only empty paths and parent-dir escapes; WcPathsDiscard::validate (commands/working_copy.rs:398-410) rejects only conflicted paths. AppState::run (src-tauri/src/state.rs:56-97) is resolve→enqueue→validate→execute, with policy/snapshot hooks still "later", and never rewrites args. So execute runs discard_paths with include_untracked=false, then `changed(cx)` (:412-415 → :668-677) re-reads status — the untracked entry is still present, delta_of keeps it (code = Some(Untracked)), store.apply re-renders the row, discard returns true, and App.vue:919 pushes the success toast.

5. The affordance is genuinely reachable for untracked rows. WorkingCopyPane.vue:244 passes `:allow-discard="section.id !== 'conflicted' && section.id !== 'staged'"` and the untracked section id is 'untracked' (:105, :138-142); untracked entries have staged=false, so WorkingCopyFileList.vue:159-167 renders the ↩ button. WorkingCopyFileDetail.vue:105-113 gates only on `!stagedFor(entry) && entry.code !== 'unmerged'`, also true for untracked. Both emit discard(path) → App.vue:907 discardEntry → dialogue → useWorkingCopy.ts:43-47 → store.discard(id,[path]) → commands.wcPathsDiscard(repo, paths) with opts defaulted to `{}`. A repo-wide grep for includeUntracked finds it declared in src/bridges/bindings.ts:442 and set by no caller anywhere.

6. Intent is unambiguous: docs/03-command-surface.md:112 lists `include_untracked` in the command surface, and the engine doc comment (index.rs:209-213) says untracked paths *are* deleted, "the last only with include_untracked and an explicit confirmation token". The UI already collects that confirmation (the zh-CN dialogue is the "cannot be undone" copy) and then discards it. The engine's own test at index.rs:1402-1443 covers untracked+no-token (Err) and untracked+token (deleted) but never the default+untracked case the UI actually sends — which is why this survived.

Why major, not blocker: the failure direction is safe. Nothing is deleted that the user did not intend, no state is corrupted, and the app does not break — the file stays on disk and the row stays listed. What is wrong is the contract: a destructive verb, gated behind a scary confirmation the user answered, reports "已放弃该文件的改动。" / "Discarded the file's changes." while doing nothing. That is a false success plus a feature that is 100% non-functional for an entire row class (every untracked file, via both the row button and the detail-bar button) — real, user-visible and trust-breaking, but not data loss. Blocker is normally reserved for data loss, corruption, crash or security.

Traced end-to-end and confirmed empirically. UI: WorkingCopyPane.vue:244 grants allow-discard to the untracked section, WorkingCopyFileList.vue:160 renders the row button for non-staged entries, WorkingCopyFileDetail.vue:106 renders the bar button for any non-staged, non-unmerged entry — untracked satisfies all. Chain: App.vue:918 -> useWorkingCopy.discard (composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:43-47) -> store.discard (stores/workingCopy.ts:52-61) -> commands.wcPathsDiscard (bridges/commands.ts:191-197) with opts defaulting to {}; includeUntracked/confirmToken are never sent. Engine: domain/working_copy.rs:519-529 defaults include_untracked=false; engine/index.rs:269-273 does `if status.contains(Status::WT_NEW) && !tracked { if opts.include_untracked { to_delete.push(..) } continue; }`, so nothing is queued (to_head/to_index are also empty since WT_NEW is in neither index_bits() nor workdir_bits(), index.rs:926-940) and the fn returns Ok(()) having written nothing. commands/working_copy.rs:412-415 then returns changed(cx), which re-loads status (working_copy.rs:668-677) and yields a delta still containing the file; the store applies it and returns true, so App.vue:919 pushes the success toast. I verified this by adding a probe test in a copy at /tmp/verify-WC-01/repo: discard_paths(&repo, &["scratch.txt"], &DiscardOptions::default()) passed while asserting result.is_ok() AND the file still exists. The only inaccuracy in the finding is its call-chain description (it omits the useWorkingCopy composable between App.vue and the store), which does not change the outcome. No guard, default, other caller, catalogue entry, refresh, or handler rescues the behaviour, and the shipped test at index.rs:1403 only covers the include_untracked=true branches. Severity corrected: the failure is fail-safe (nothing destroyed, no crash, no security issue) but it is a broken T0 verb plus a lying success toast, so major rather than blocker.

findings.title: wc_status_load is always called with empty opts, so assume-unchanged / ignored / untracked-dir rows can never appear and the 'clear assume-unchanged' control is unreachable
findings.evidence: src/stores/workingCopy.ts:29 — `apply(await commands.wcStatusLoad(repo))` (the `opts: WcStatusOptions = {}` default at src/bridges/commands.ts:105 means includeIgnored/includeDirs/includeNonmodified/includeAssumeUnchanged are all false). src-tauri/src/engine/status.rs:83-91 then drops every clean row (`if clean && !opts.include_nonmodified && !(opts.include_assume_unchanged && assume) { continue; }`) and never lists ignored files, so the assume-unchanged bit is unobservable. src/components/panes/WorkingCopyFileList.vue:168-176 only renders the eye-slash button for `entries[index].assumeUnchanged`, and src/App.vue:1496 is its only caller — dead code. There is no UI at all for `wc_entry_ignore` (src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:427-463; registered at lib.rs:87 but no TS wrapper in src/bridges/commands.ts), so a user who stages an ignored file gets engine/index.rs:52-58's English refusal and no way forward.
findings.repro: 1. `git update-index --assume-unchanged tracked.txt` (or set it in a previous session). 2. Switch to Meridian and open the working copy tab: the file is absent from the list and there is no toggle to show it. 3. The ↉ button that would clear the bit can therefore never be pressed. With `includeIgnored` never sent, `.gitignore`d files are likewise unreachable.
findings.expected: A 「显示未修改文件」/「显示已忽略文件」/ assume-unchanged visibility toggle (docs/04 §S6 lists badges for assume-unchanged) whose state is sent on every `wc_status_load`, so flagged files are listed and clearable.
findings.actual: A file carrying the assume-unchanged bit is completely invisible in the working-copy list (and there is no way to show ignored files or untracked directories), so the only UI affordance for the flag — the 'clear assume-unchanged' button — can never be rendered.
findings.fix: Keep a `statusOptions` ref in stores/workingCopy (includeAssumeUnchanged/includeIgnored/includeNonmodified/includeDirs, plus conflictedOnly) driven by toggles in the WorkingCopyPane toolbar, and pass it in every `wcStatusLoad(repo, opts)`. Note that `summary_of` (domain/working_copy.rs:180-193) already skips Ignored rows, so enabling includeIgnored will not corrupt the counters. Also add a `wcEntryIgnore` bridge and wire it to a context-menu item so the refuse-then-offer-ignore flow in engine/index.rs:41-58 is reachable.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/workingCopy.test.ts: set `store.statusOptions.includeAssumeUnchanged = true`, call `refresh('repo')`, assert the recorded invoke payload is `{args:{repo, opts:{includeAssumeUnchanged:true}}}`. Plus a Vue test mounting WorkingCopyPane that asserts the toolbar renders a toggle which updates the prop.

notes: CONFIRMED empirically. (1) Real git: in /tmp/verify-WC-02, after `git update-index --assume-unchanged tracked.txt` + modifying it, `git status --porcelain` shows nothing for it; only `git ls-files -v` reveals it (`h tracked.txt`). (2) Engine: src-tauri/src/engine/status.rs:69 sets include_unmodified(opts.include_nonmodified || opts.include_assume_unchanged) and :89 drops clean rows; with default opts both are false so the assume-unchanged row is dropped. The crate's own test `status_honors_ignore_and_assume_unchanged_options` (:510) asserts the row is hidden under default opts and only appears with include_assume_unchanged:true — direct in-repo proof of the mechanism. (3) Store: src/stores/workingCopy.ts:29 is the ONLY caller of wcStatusLoad and always passes no opts (grep confirms). (4) Button: WorkingCopyFileList.vue:169 renders the eye-slash only when entries[index].assumeUnchanged; sole emit site is App.vue:1496 -> clearAssumeUnchanged (App.vue:900); since the flag is never true, it is unreachable dead code. (5) wc_entry_ignore has no TS wrapper at all (grep wcEntryIgnore src/ = none) though it is registered at lib.rs:87, and engine/index.rs:51-58 refuses ignored staging in English with no UI path forward; no includeIgnored/includeDirs/includeNonmodified toggle exists (only a client-side conflictedOnly filter at WorkingCopyPane.vue:145). docs/03:104 and docs/04 S6:289 confirm the options and assume-unchanged badge are specified, so the implementation is incomplete relative to spec. Two minor imprecisions in the finding, neither affecting the verdict: the TS WcStatusOptions type (bindings.ts:214-217) declares only includeIgnored/includeDirs (the other two aren't in the TS type; Rust serde defaults them false), and conflictedOnly is already handled client-side so it need not be re-sent to the backend. Also, setAssumeUnchanged(..., true) is never called anywhere, so the bit cannot even be set from the UI — the entire assume-unchanged feature is dead, not just the clear control. Severity major is appropriate: a documented option surface and UI affordance are entirely unreachable, but there is no data loss or crash.

Re-traced line by line in /tmp/meridian-baseline; the path behaves exactly as claimed, and the guard I was hunting for does not exist anywhere.

1) Single call site, empty opts. `grep -rn "wcStatusLoad" src/` returns only two hits: the definition at src/bridges/commands.ts:105 (`wcStatusLoad(repo, opts: WcStatusOptions = {})` → `invoke("wc_status_load", { args: { repo, opts } })`) and src/stores/workingCopy.ts:29 (`apply(await commands.wcStatusLoad(repo));`). The store is the only status reader; src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:70 is the only wrapper and it forwards no opts either. No second caller, no persisted view-options state.

2) The TS binding cannot even express the needed flags. src/bridges/bindings.ts:214-217:
   `export interface WcStatusOptions { includeIgnored?: boolean; includeDirs?: boolean; }`
   There is no `includeNonmodified` / `includeAssumeUnchanged` / `conflictedOnly` on the TS side, while the Rust struct (src-tauri/src/domain/working_copy.rs:39-51) has all five. So the capability was never plumbed, not merely unset.

3) Engine drops the rows. src-tauri/src/engine/status.rs:89: `if clean && !opts.include_nonmodified && !(opts.include_assume_unchanged && assume) { continue; }`. The crate's own test (status.rs:534-552) proves the suppression even with real content changes: after writing "two\n" and `set_assume_unchanged(true)`, `load(..., default)` satisfies `assert!(hidden.iter().all(|e| e.path != "tracked.txt"))`, and only `include_assume_unchanged: true` yields the row — with `assert_eq!(row.code, None)`, i.e. a clean row.

4) The mutation path cannot smuggle it in either — this is the guard I expected to refute the finding. src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:675: `let entries = engine::status::load(cx.repo, &WorkingCopyStatusOptions::default())?;` inside `changed()`, which every stage/unstage/discard/assume-unchanged-set mutation returns, and `delta_of` (working_copy.rs:683-693) starts `.filter_map(|entry| entry.code.map(|code| EntryStatus::new(...)))` — dropping exactly the code-less assume rows. Note this `filter_map` also proves `wc_entry_assume_unchanged_set`'s own StatusDelta can never carry an assume row, so the store's `setAssumeUnchanged` → `refresh(repo)` (workingCopy.ts:104-108) cannot re-surface it either.

5) The button's only caller is App.vue:1496 `@clear-assume-unchanged`, and WorkingCopyFileList.vue:169 `v-if="entries[index].assumeUnchanged"` can never be satisfied (a `code: None` row would not survive `delta_of`, and no load ever asks for one). Corroborating dead wiring I found beyond the finding: the i18n key `workingCopy.assumeUnchanged` ("标记为未改动" / "Assume unchanged") is defined at src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/panes.ts:150 and parts/en/panes.ts:153 but referenced nowhere — so there is not even a "set" affordance, only the unreachable "clear". The composable's own comment (useWorkingCopy.ts:54-58) states the hazard: "A file carrying that bit is invisible to `git status`, so without a way to clear it a user can lose track of a file entirely" — the mitigation it describes cannot fire.

6) `wc_entry_ignore` genuinely has no TS wrapper: `grep -rn "entry_ignore|entryIgnore" src/` returns zero hits under src/, while the command exists (working_copy.rs:427-463, registered lib.rs:87). The only guard I found there is one-directional by design — src-tauri/tests/handler_completeness.rs asserts every Rust command appears in `generate_handler!`, not that every command has a TS wrapper — which is why the gap passes CI.

7) It contradicts the spec, so this is stale-ui rather than an unrequested nicety: docs/01-product-spec.md:92 `| CAP-G2-06 | T1 | Show ignored / non-modified / assume-unchanged items |`; docs/03-command-surface.md:104 lists all five opts for `wc_status_load`; docs/04-ui-spec.md:289 lists the assume-unchanged badge in the S6 file list; docs/02-architecture.md:475 puts "ignore/assume-unchanged/untrack" in the working-copy pane scope. `summary_of` (domain/working_copy.rs:180-193) already skips `FileStatus::Ignored`, so enabling includeIgnored would not corrupt the counters, as the finding states.

Not refuted. Severity major is correct: no crash and no data loss caused by the app itself, but a spec'd capability (CAP-G2-06), a documented badge, and a named action row are all unreachable, and a file hidden by the bit is invisible in the app with no in-app way to clear it — a user must drop to `git update-index --no-assume-unchanged` manually.

findings.title: Stage/unstage of a rename row addresses only the new path, so the rename is half applied
findings.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/status.rs:254-290 (finish_row) rewrites a renamed row's path to the new name and stores the old one in `old_path`. src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:682-702 (`delta_of`) maps each row into `domain::status::EntryStatus`, which has no old_path field (src-tauri/src/domain/status.rs:22-32) — the rename source is lost on the wire. src/App.vue:1493-1494 emits only `entry.path`, so `wc_stage_paths`/`wc_unstage_paths` (src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:41-77 and 92-119) see a single path. (Related: `wcStatusLoad` is typed `Promise<StatusDelta>` at src/bridges/commands.ts:105-107 while Rust returns `WorkingTreeStatus`, which is why the initial load's `oldPath` never reaches the typed UI at all.)
findings.repro: 1. Commit `old.txt`, then rename it on disk to `new.txt`; the list shows one row `new.txt` (R, old_path old.txt). 2. Click 暂存 on it. Verified with git 2.45: `git add new.txt` yields `A  new.txt` + ` D old.txt` — the old file's deletion stays unstaged, so the next commit adds a duplicate and leaves a deletion pending. 3. Undo and stage with `git add -A` (`R old.txt -> new.txt`), then click 取消暂存 on the rename row: verified `git reset HEAD -- new.txt` yields `D  old.txt` + `?? new.txt`, i.e. the UI now shows a staged deletion the user never asked for.
findings.expected: Clicking Stage on a rename row stages both sides (one Renamed row remains), and Unstage returns the file to its pre-stage state (deleted old + untracked new, exactly as `git add -A` + `git reset -A` would).
findings.actual: Only the new path is passed to git, so staging a rename produces `A new.txt` staged plus an unstaged ` D old.txt` (half the rename), and unstaging a staged rename leaves `D old.txt` staged with `?? new.txt` back on disk.
findings.fix: Carry `oldPath` on the wire: add `old_path: Option<String>` to `domain::status::EntryStatus`, fill it in `delta_of` (src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:682-702), and make the UI send both paths for a rename row (`stage → [oldPath, path]`, `unstage → [oldPath, path]`), or expand the rename inside `engine::index::{stage_paths, unstage_paths}` when a path matches a rename delta.
findings.testIdea: src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs tests: after a workdir rename, `stage_paths(&repo, &["new.txt"])` must leave both sides staged (assert `code_of("old.txt", true) == Some(Deleted)` and `code_of("new.txt", true) == Some(Added)` **or** a single Renamed row — pick one contract and assert it); frontend test in src/App.test.ts asserting the invoke payload for a rename row's Stage button contains both the old and the new path.

notes:
Reproduced concretely, both by reading the code and by running the exact library the app uses (git2 0.21 / libgit2-sys 0.18.8+1.9.7).

Code path: finish_row (engine/status.rs:254-290) sets row.path = new name and row.old_path = old name for a Renamed/Copied delta. delta_of (commands/working_copy.rs:682-702) maps each WorkingCopyEntry into domain::status::EntryStatus, which has no old_path field (domain/status.rs:22-32), so the rename source is dropped from every mutation's StatusDelta. The UI carries only a path string: App.vue:1493-1494 emits entry.path; WorkingCopyPane's `stage: [path: string]`; useWorkingCopy.stage → store.stage(id,[path]) → wcStagePaths(repo,[path]) → invoke("wc_stage_paths",{args:{repo,paths:[new.txt]}}). Engine stage_paths (engine/index.rs:41-77) then calls index.add_all(["new.txt"], DEFAULT, None).

Empirical (driver /tmp/verify-wc03/lgtest/src/main.rs), starting from a committed old.txt renamed on disk to new.txt:
- add_all(["new.txt"]) -> status "A  new.txt" + " D old.txt": exactly `git add new.txt` (verified against git 2.45 CLI in /tmp/verify-wc03/gitcli), i.e. the rename is half applied; committing would add a duplicate new.txt and leave the old.txt deletion pending.
- reset_default(HEAD, ["new.txt"]) on a fully-staged rename (R old.txt->new.txt) -> "D  old.txt" + "?? new.txt": a staged deletion the user never asked for.
- Control: add_all(["old.txt","new.txt"]) -> "R  old.txt" (fix works); reset_default(HEAD,["old.txt","new.txt"]) -> back to the workdir rename; add_all(["."]) (the stage-all button) -> "R  old.txt", which is why only the per-row/bulk stage is affected.

The related claim also checks out: Rust wc_status_load returns WorkingTreeStatus (entries: Vec<WorkingCopyEntry>, which serializes oldPath), but bridges/commands.ts:105-107 types wcStatusLoad as Promise<StatusDelta> whose EntryStatus (bindings.ts:101-107) has no oldPath, so the typed UI cannot see the rename source even on the initial load.

Severity: major is correct — a core staging operation silently produces a half-applied rename that corrupts the next commit's contents (duplicate file + pending deletion) and unstaging fabricates a staged deletion. Not a blocker (no crash, recoverable via Stage-all), not minor (silent wrong index state, user-visible data hazard).

TRACE result: the finding survives line-by-line retracing; I found no guard, default, or other caller that repairs the behaviour, and I reproduced it end-to-end.

Wire loss (Rust side): domain/status.rs:22-32 EntryStatus has {path, code, staged, assume_unchanged, view} — no old_path. commands/working_copy.rs:682-700 delta_of builds each row with `EntryStatus::new(entry.path.as_str(), code, entry.staged, entry.assume_unchanged)`, silently dropping the `WorkingCopyEntry.old_path` that engine/status.rs:260-290 finish_row sets (row.path = new name, row.old_path = Some(old)). So both mutation responses and the typed load lose the rename source.

Wire loss (TS side): bridges/commands.ts:105-107 types wcStatusLoad as Promise<StatusDelta> even though WcStatusLoad::Output is WorkingTreeStatus (domain/working_copy.rs:159-166) whose entries are WorkingCopyEntry (carries oldPath). bindings.ts:101-107 EntryStatus likewise has no oldPath. So even the initial load's runtime oldPath is unreachable to the typed UI.

UI sends one path: App.vue:1493-1494 -> composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:33-41 stage/unstage(path) -> stores/workingCopy.ts:35-45 `store.stage(id, [path])` -> wc_stage_paths/wc_unstage_paths with a single-element paths array. WorkingCopyFileList.vue:146/155 emits `entries[index].path` only; nothing anywhere in src/ reads or forwards oldPath for staging. The list is fed by load() with `.renames_index_to_workdir(true)` / `.renames_head_to_index(true)` (engine/status.rs:71-72), so a rename collapses to ONE row (verified by the existing test status_detects_workdir_renames, engine/status.rs:490-505), leaving the old path with no row of its own to stage.

Engine is per-path: index.rs:41-77 stage_paths does `index.add_all(paths, DEFAULT)`; index.rs:92-119 unstage_paths does `reset_default(HEAD, paths)`. Both act only on the names given. validation/working_copy.rs validate_paths imposes no rename expansion.

Empirical confirmation (libgit2 0.21, exact dep version, in /tmp/verify-WC-03-g2):
- After an unstaged `mv old.txt new.txt`, `add_all(["new.txt"])` -> status `new.txt INDEX_NEW` + `old.txt WT_DELETED`; committing leaves BOTH new.txt and old.txt in HEAD's tree (the "duplicate + pending deletion" the finding describes). git 2.45 CLI reproduces identically.
- After `add_all(["."])` stages the rename, `reset_default(HEAD, ["new.txt"])` -> `old.txt INDEX_DELETED` (staged deletion) + `new.txt WT_NEW` (untracked) — i.e. unstaging a staged rename leaves a staged deletion the user never asked for.

No refutation available: the only nearby "rename is two paths" comment (engine/index.rs:943-944) is about the discard status_map and actually corroborates that a rename is two paths the caller must supply; the UI supplies one. Correctly rated major (functional correctness defect in a core staging operation, producing wrong repo state), not a blocker (recoverable, no immediate committed-data loss).

findings.title: Selection is keyed by path only, so for a file with staged + unstaged changes the detail pane is stuck on the staged row
findings.evidence: src/App.vue:928-932 — `selectedEntry = workingCopy.entries.find(e => e.path === selectedPath)`, which cannot distinguish the two axes the status list deliberately emits (src-tauri/src/engine/status.rs:215-252 emits one row per axis; the sort at status.rs:96 puts the staged row first via `b.staged.cmp(&a.staged)`). The watch at src/App.vue:958-972 therefore keeps `perspectiveFor` at indexToBase, and WorkingCopyFileDetail.vue:51-53/93-113 renders 取消暂存 (and hides 放弃) for that row.
findings.repro: 1. Commit `a.txt`; 2. edit a.txt and press 暂存; 3. edit a.txt again. The list shows two rows for `a.txt` (staged M, then unstaged M). 4. Click the lower (unstaged) row: `selectedPath` is already `a.txt`, `find` returns the *staged* row, so the detail pane keeps showing the staged diff with 取消暂存 and no 放弃 button; clicking the staged row changes nothing. There is no other control to reach the unstaged row's diff or its discard.
findings.expected: Clicking a row selects that exact row, so the unstaged row shows the workdir↔index diff and offers 暂存/放弃.
findings.actual: Both rows have the same `path`, and `find` always returns the first one — the staged row — so clicking the unstaged row does nothing: you keep seeing the staged diff, the Unstage button, and no Discard button.
findings.fix: Make the selection identify the axis: keep `selectedPath` plus `selectedStaged`, and `find(e => e.path === selectedPath && e.staged === selectedStaged)`; emit both from WorkingCopyFileList's `select`. Alternatively give each row a stable id (`${path}\0${staged}`) and key the selection on that.
findings.testIdea: A component/store test (e.g. src/stores/workingCopy.test.ts or a mounted WorkingCopyPane test) with entries `[{path:'a.txt',staged:true},{path:'a.txt',staged:false}]`: selecting the unstaged row must make `selectedEntry.staged === false` and the detail bar must render the 放弃 action.

notes: Reproduced end-to-end. (1) git CLI in /tmp/verify-wc04: commit a.txt, stage an edit, edit again -> `MM a.txt`, one path on both axes with two distinct diffs (index->base vs worktree->index). (2) Engine: status.rs:215 entry_rows emits one row per axis; for INDEX_MODIFIED|WT_MODIFIED index_code() (line 292) pushes staged=true Modified and workdir_code() (line 306) pushes staged=false Modified for the same path. The engine's own test status_separates_axes_and_reports_untracked (status.rs:456) builds exactly this scenario and asserts both rows. (3) Sort status.rs:96 `a.path.cmp(&b.path).then_with(|| b.staged.cmp(&a.staged))`: for equal paths false.cmp(true)==Less, so the staged row is first. (4) Frontend: WorkingCopyFileList emits `select:[path,event]` only; pane forwards selectFile(path,event); App.vue:1491 `@select-file="selectedPath = $event"` stores a bare path. selectedEntry (App.vue:928-932) is `entries.find(e => e.path === path)` -> first match -> always the staged row. A Node simulation of the exact logic (entries sorted as the engine sorts, selectedPath="a.txt") yields selectedEntry.staged=true, perspectiveFor=indexToBase, detail bar shows Unstage and hides Discard. The watch key (App.vue:958-972) `${path}\0${staged}\0${code}` does not change, so diff.load is never re-invoked. So the claimed wrong behaviour holds concretely, and even without any prior selection: clicking the unstaged row sets selectedPath to the shared path and the detail immediately renders the staged diff. Minor overstatement only: the claim 'no other control to reach ... its discard' is false because the Modified row's hover action renders 放弃 (WorkingCopyFileList `v-if="allowDiscard && !entries[index].staged"`, Modified section passes allow-discard=true); however the workdir<->index diff is genuinely unreachable, and both rows highlight simultaneously (both match path===selectedPath) while the detail verbs act on the wrong axis. Core defect confirmed; keep major.

I re-traced the whole chain line by line in /tmp/meridian-baseline and could not find a guard, default, or alternate caller that rescues it. The finding is real, with one correction to its "actual" paragraph.

1. The backend genuinely emits two rows per path. `entry_rows` (/tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/status.rs:215-252) pushes one row per axis: `index_code(status)` → `staged=true`, `workdir_code(status)` → `staged=false`, both with the same `path`. An edit-then-stage-then-edit file has INDEX_MODIFIED|WT_MODIFIED, so both rows exist.

2. The sort puts the staged row first, deterministically. status.rs:96 `entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.path.cmp(&b.path).then_with(|| b.staged.cmp(&a.staged)))`. I ran the comparator in /tmp/verify-WC-04/sort.js: sorted order is `[{a.txt,staged:true},{a.txt,staged:false}]`.

3. The store preserves that order — `apply()` in /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/workingCopy.ts:20-24 assigns `entries.value = delta.entries` verbatim. No dedup, no regroup, no re-sort anywhere.

4. Both rows are visible, in different sections. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/panes/WorkingCopyPane.vue:96-102 splits on `entry.staged`, so the staged row lands in the Staged section and the unstaged row in the Modified section.

5. Selection carries no axis. WorkingCopyFileList.vue:56 emits `select: [path: string, event: MouseEvent]` and line 126 emits `emit('select', entries[index].path, $event)` — path only. Pane.vue:249 forwards `emit('selectFile', path, event)`, and App.vue:1491 binds `@select-file="selectedPath = $event"`, dropping the event entirely. Assigning the same string to a `ref` is a no-op for reactivity, so the computed never re-evaluates.

6. The lookup cannot distinguish the axes. App.vue:928-932 `workingCopy.entries.value.find((entry) => entry.path === path)` returns the first match = the staged row, per step 2.

7. Consequences land exactly as described. `perspectiveFor` (App.vue:947-951) sees `staged=true` → `"indexToBase"`, so the watcher at App.vue:958-972 loads the staged diff. WorkingCopyFileDetail.vue:92-100 renders 取消暂存, and its Discard button at :105-113 is gated on `!stagedFor(entry)` so it is absent.

8. No escape hatch in the diff viewer. I checked /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/diff/DiffViewer.vue: its toolbar exposes only context lines, ignoreWhitespace, fullFile, syntax, and unified/split. `direction` at :188-193 is *derived* from `doc.perspective` (via toDiffPerspective in /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/viewModels.ts:111-122), not user-selectable. There is no perspective switch.

9. Compounding: WorkingCopyFileList.vue:125 marks rows `.selected` on `entries[index].path === selectedPath`, so BOTH rows highlight at once — the UI gives the user no way to tell which one the detail pane is showing.

CORRECTION to the finding's "actual": the claim "There is no other control to reach the unstaged row's diff or its discard" is half wrong. The discard and stage verbs on the unstaged row itself DO work, because they read `entries[index].staged` per-row rather than going through `selectedEntry`. WorkingCopyFileList.vue:151-167 renders the 暂存 button on the `v-else` branch and the 放弃 button at :159-167 gated on `allowDiscard && !entries[index].staged`; Pane.vue:244 passes `:allow-discard="section.id !== 'conflicted' && section.id !== 'staged'"`, which is true for the modified section. So the user can still discard and stage the unstaged change from the row's hover actions. The defect is confined to the detail pane: wrong diff shown, and the detail bar's verbs describe the wrong axis.

Severity stays major: the core complaint — clicking the unstaged row yields the staged diff, plus both rows highlighting at once — is a real display-correctness bug in the most common partially-staged state, and there is no control to reach the correct diff. It is not data loss, and every mutating verb remains reachable, which is why I would not push it above major.

findings.title: A merge whose resolution leaves the tree equal to HEAD cannot be committed, and the merge banner that would offer it is never loaded
findings.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/commit.rs:215-228 — `let staged = engine::index::has_staged_changes(repo)?; if amend {…} else if !staged { return Err(Violation::new(ErrorCode::InvalidRequest, "No staged changes to commit")) }`, with no exemption for `RepositoryState::Merge` (which the same function explicitly *allows* at commit.rs:177-178). The composer gate `props.subject.trim() !== "" && stagedCount.value > 0` (src/components/panes/CommitComposer.vue:64-73) and App.vue:989 refuse it before the command is even issued, and the merge banner that carries the 「提交合并」 button (WorkingCopyPane.vue:200-226) is fed by `const mergeStatus = ref<MergeStatus | null>(null)` (src/App.vue:1031) — never assigned, so `wc_merge_status_load` (src/bridges/commands.ts:355-357) is dead code.
findings.repro: 1. Create a conflicting merge. 2. Resolve the conflict by taking ours (`git checkout --ours .` + stage, or the app's resolve flow) so the index tree equals HEAD's tree. 3. Verified with git 2.45: `git commit -m 'merge resolved as ours'` succeeds and writes a two-parent merge commit. 4. In Meridian the Commit button is disabled with 「先暂存改动」 and the merge banner is absent, so the only remaining exit (`resolveMerge`/`abortMerge` at App.vue:1509-1510) is also invisible — the merge cannot be completed from the UI.
findings.expected: While a merge is in progress, `git commit`'s rule applies: the commit is allowed even when the index matches HEAD (that is how a merge resolved entirely to 'ours' is finished), producing the two-parent merge commit.
findings.actual: Commit is refused with 「No staged changes to commit」 (invalid_request) because the index tree equals HEAD's tree, and the Commit button is disabled with 「先暂存改动」 — so the merge cannot be completed at all.
findings.fix: In `validate_commit`, skip the `!staged` refusal when `repo.state() == RepositoryState::Merge`; mirror that in the composer (App.vue:989 / CommitComposer.vue:64-73) by passing a `mergeInProgress` prop so the staged-count gate does not apply. Separately, wire `wcMergeStatusLoad` into the store so the banner (and its 提交合并 button) actually renders.
findings.testIdea: src-tauri/src/commands/commit.rs tests: build a conflicted merge (the `conflicting_merge` helper in src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:1534), resolve it to HEAD's content, then assert `validate_commit` returns Ok and `commit()` yields `parent_count == 2`.

notes:
CONFIRMED, not refuted. Reproduced the exact scenario with git 2.45.2 in a scratch repo (/tmp/verify-WC05/repo2): conflicting merge on master vs feature, resolved with `git checkout --ours -- . && git add .`. Afterwards `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` and `git write-tree` are identical (d66240dd...), `git diff --cached`/`git diff-tree` show 0 deltas, MERGE_HEAD is still present, and `git commit -m 'merge resolved as ours'` exits 0 and writes a two-parent commit (rev-list --parents reports 2 parents). So real git's rule — a merge in progress commits even when the index tree equals HEAD — holds.

Code path in /tmp/meridian-baseline: `has_staged_changes` (src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:756-765) does `diff_tree_to_index(head_tree, index)` and returns `deltas().len() > 0`, i.e. false here. `validate_commit` (src-tauri/src/commands/commit.rs:215-228) then hits the `else if !staged` branch and returns `Violation::new(InvalidRequest, "No staged changes to commit")`. Crucially the same function explicitly ALLOWS `RepositoryState::Merge` at commit.rs:177-178, so the merge exemption exists everywhere except this staged check. `AppState::run` (state.rs:78-79) calls `validate` and maps the Violation to an ErrorPayload before `execute`, so the engine is never reached — even though `engine::index::commit` (index.rs:571-715, parents read from MERGE_HEAD at 658-662) would in fact produce the correct two-parent commit and would NOT refuse on staged==HEAD. The engine test at index.rs:1790 only covers a merge whose tree differs, so nothing exercises the all-ours case.

Frontend also confirmed: CommitComposer.vue:64-73 gates non-amend commit on `subject.trim() !== "" && stagedCount.value > 0`; with index==HEAD staged is 0, so the button is disabled with 「先暂存改动」 and the meta+enter path is gated identically. The banner carrying the 「提交合并」 button (WorkingCopyPane.vue:200-226) is fed by `:merge="mergeStatus"` (App.vue:1472) where `const mergeStatus = ref<MergeStatus | null>(null)` (App.vue:1031) is never assigned (`grep mergeStatus.value` finds nothing), so the banner never renders and the `resolve-merge`/`abort-merge` handlers at App.vue:1509-1510 are unreachable. `wcMergeStatusLoad` (bridges/commands.ts:355) has zero callers — dead code, as claimed.

One nuance worth noting (does not refute the finding): a second, generic integration banner exists in RepositoryScreen.vue:71-81 with Continue/Abort buttons driven by `summary.state` (RepoInfo.state, an IntegrationState that includes "merge"). If it rendered, Continue → integration_continue → engine::merge::continue_merge (merge.rs:503-530), which has NO staged gate and would finish the merge. But RepoInfo.state is only ever set by repos.upsert at open/init/clone (stores/repos.ts:36-43, 56-88) and is never refreshed afterwards: useGit.refreshAll (useGit.ts:32-34) and useAppEvents (useAppEvents.ts:30-40) reload branches/workingCopy/history only, never repos. So for a merge started in-session the state stays "clean" and this banner does not appear either. The only workaround is closing and reopening the repo while the merge is in progress (repositoryOpen then reports state "merge"), which is obscure. So the finding's "the merge cannot be completed from the UI" is essentially accurate for the normal flow.

Minor inaccuracy in the finding: App.vue:989's `staged` is only used to compute `reusesMessage` for the amend branch, so it is not itself a gate for the non-amend merge commit — the real frontend gate is CommitComposer.vue:64-73. This does not change the verdict.

The claimed path holds at every link; I could not find a guard that saves the behaviour.

1. Backend refusal, no Merge exemption. commit.rs:177-178 explicitly permits Merge: `git2::RepositoryState::Clean | git2::RepositoryState::Merge => {}` with the comment "A merge in progress *is* the commit path (it produces the two-parent commit)". Yet commit.rs:215 then computes `let staged = engine::index::has_staged_changes(repo)...` and at the `else if !staged` branch returns `Violation::new(ErrorCode::InvalidRequest, "No staged changes to commit")` — with no Merge carve-out. This directly contradicts the intent stated 40 lines earlier.

2. `has_staged_changes` (engine/index.rs:756) is `repo.diff_tree_to_index(head_tree, index, None)` → `diff.deltas().len() > 0`. When the resolved index tree equals HEAD's tree the delta count is 0, so `staged == false`.

3. The git premise is real. I reproduced it in /tmp/verify-WC-05: conflict merge, `git checkout --ours` + `git add`, index tree `30b0f16...` == HEAD tree `30b0f16...`, `git diff --cached` empty, and `git commit -m` succeeds producing a two-parent commit (parent count 2). `engine::index::commit` already supports this: index.rs:661 `parent_oids.extend(read_pseudoref_oids(repo, "MERGE_HEAD"))`, so exempting the `!staged` check would yield the correct 2-parent commit.

4. `AppState::run` (state.rs:79) does call `cmd.validate(...)?` before `execute`, so the violation is really returned to the UI.

5. UI gates. CommitComposer.vue `canCommit` requires `props.subject.trim() !== "" && stagedCount.value > 0`; after an all-ours resolution the entry is clean (index==worktree==HEAD), so summary_of counts staged=0 and the button is disabled. App.vue:1031 `const mergeStatus = ref<MergeStatus | null>(null)` is never assigned anywhere (grep: only declaration at 1031 and the `:merge="mergeStatus"` pass at 1472), so the WorkingCopyPane merge banner at 200-226 (and its 提交合并 button) never renders; ports.ts:21 documents this as a pending port.

I actively hunted for the guard the auditor might have missed — the RepositoryScreen integration banner (App.vue:1459-1464, `@continue-operation` → `git.continueOperation()` → `integration_continue` → `engine::merge::continue_merge`, which creates the merge commit with NO staged check). That looked like a rescue path, but it is also dead: its `stateLabel` is driven by `props.summary?.state` (RepositoryScreen.vue), which App.vue:203-208 sources from `selectedRepo.value.state` = `RepoInfo.state`. That field is only ever written by `upsert` in stores/repos.ts:61/78/124 (open/init/clone); nothing refreshes it after a merge starts — `useGit.run`'s `refreshAll` refreshes branches/workingCopy/history only, `useAppEvents` handles `reposChanged` as a no-op `break`, and `repository_state`/`repository_refresh` are never invoked from src/. So the integration banner never appears for an in-session merge either.

Conclusion: a merge resolved so its tree equals HEAD cannot be committed — the backend refuses it and both UI exits are unreachable. The finding is correct. (It actually understates the problem: there are two dead exits, not one.) Severity major is appropriate: a valid git operation is refused and the user is fully stuck with no in-app way to finish the merge.

findings.title: Bulk stage/unstage issues one command per path, each re-reading the whole status, with no progress and no error
findings.evidence: src/components/panes/WorkingCopyPane.vue:155-159 collects the section's paths and emits them; src/App.vue:1497-1498 turns that into `paths.forEach(path => void workingCopy.stage(path))`; src/stores/workingCopy.ts:35-49 issues one `wc_stage_paths` per path; src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:668-677 (`changed`) re-runs a full `engine::status::load` and ships the entire delta back for **every** one of them. `wc_stage_all` / `wc_unstage_all` (src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:213-284, registered at lib.rs:82-83) exist and would do it in one call, but no TS wrapper exists.
findings.repro: 1. Check out a repository with a large untracked/generated tree (20k files). 2. Working copy → 未跟踪 section → 暂存所有. 3. The app issues 20,000 `wc_stage_paths` commands; each one walks the whole worktree for status and returns the full delta over IPC. The list freezes with no busy indicator, and if any single call fails the error state is overwritten by the next success (see WC-12) so the user is told nothing.
findings.expected: One command for the whole section (paths array or `wc_stage_all`), with a busy indicator and one reported error.
findings.actual: The section's 「暂存所有」/「取消暂存所有」 buttons fire one IPC command per file, and every command re-scans the entire working copy and returns the full delta — O(N) full status walks, no progress, and the UI becomes unresponsive on any real tree.
findings.fix: Add `wcStageAll`/`wcUnstageAll` wrappers in src/bridges/commands.ts and call them for the section bulk buttons (or send the whole `paths` array in one `wc_stage_paths`); wrap the call in a `busy` flag and report a single error toast.
findings.testIdea: src/App.test.ts (or a mounted WorkingCopyPane test): with 5 rows in a section, clicking the bulk button must produce exactly one invoke of `wc_stage_paths` with the 5-path array (or one `wc_stage_all`), not 5 invokes.

notes:
Traced end to end in /tmp/meridian-baseline; the behaviour is real.

CHAIN: WorkingCopyPane.vue:155-159 maps the section's entries to paths and emits bulkStage/bulkUnstage, wired at :252 as `@bulk="onBulk(section.id, section.entries)"` with `:entries="section.entries"` (:241) — the full section list, not the virtualized window. App.vue:1497-1498 then does `paths.forEach((path) => void workingCopy.stage(path))`. The actual fan-out point (which the finding misattributes to the store) is src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:33-41: `stage(path: string)` -> `store.stage(id, [path])`, `unstage(path)` -> `store.unstage(id, [path])`. Each call becomes one `wc_stage_paths` (commands.ts:109-115), and src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:668-677 `changed(cx)` re-runs `engine::status::load(...default())` and ships the full delta every time.

TWO AGGRAVATORS THE FINDING MISSED: (1) src-tauri/src/state.rs:65-67 `let _turn = self.queue.enqueue(&repo_id).await;` — all commands for a repo are SERIALIZED, so the N calls queue head-to-tail rather than overlapping: O(N^2) status walks. (2) `changed()` emits AppEvent::WorkingCopyChanged, and src/composables/useAppEvents.ts:35-39 handles it with `void workingCopy.refresh(event.payload.repo)` — so each per-path mutation triggers a SECOND full `wc_status_load`. That is ~2 complete status enumerations per file, not 1.

NO GUARD RESCUES IT: WorkingCopyStatusOptions derives Default with every flag false (src-tauri/src/domain/working_copy.rs:38-51), so `include_dirs: false` -> `recurse_untracked_dirs(true)` (engine/status.rs:68-75) — the full untracked tree is enumerated, and `load()` has no result cap. `validate_paths` (validation/working_copy.rs:20-43) checks only emptiness and path escape, not count. `wcStageAll`/`wcUnstageAll` wrappers do not exist in src/bridges/commands.ts even though the Rust commands are registered (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:82-83) and implemented (working_copy.rs:213-234, 262-284). stores/workingCopy.ts:35-49 sets no loading flag (only `refresh` at :27 does) and writes errorState on failure, which the next success overwrites. The bulk button is rendered whenever `bulkAction && entries.length > 0` (WorkingCopyFileList.vue:96) with no disabled/busy state.

EVIDENCE CORRECTION: the store (stores/workingCopy.ts:35-49) is array-capable and issues exactly ONE `wcStagePaths` per call; it is the single-path composable signature that forces N calls, not the store. This does not change the verdict.

FIX CORRECTION: the suggested `wc_stage_all`/`wc_unstage_all` substitution would be wrong. The bulk button is PER-SECTION — WorkingCopyFileList.vue:83-85 renders `workingCopy.bulkStageAll` with the section noun ("Stage all modified" / "Stage all untracked"), so `stage_all` would also stage conflicts and every other section, changing semantics. Severity stays major: real UX freeze plus silently swallowed errors, but not data loss or corruption (each call is a valid `git add` and the queue does eventually drain).

CONFIRMED empirically, and the finding understates the cost by ~2x. Every link in the claimed chain exists verbatim.

1) Pane collects the whole section. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/panes/WorkingCopyPane.vue:155-159 — `onBulk` does `list.map(e => e.path)` over the entire section and emits `bulkStage`/`bulkUnstage` with the full array. No truncation anywhere in the file.

2) App.vue fans it out per path. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:1497-1498 — `@bulk-stage="(paths) => paths.forEach((path) => void workingCopy.stage(path))"`. Fire-and-forget (`void`), N promises.

3) The composable narrows the array back to one path. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:33-36 — `stage(path)` → `store.stage(id, [path])`. The store (src/stores/workingCopy.ts:35-41) already accepts `paths: string[]` and calls `commands.wcStagePaths` — so the split happens purely in the App.vue/composable layer, exactly as claimed.

4) Each call re-walks the whole worktree AND rewrites the index. src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:209-210 `WcStagePaths::execute` → `engine::index::stage_paths(...)` then `changed(cx)`; `changed` (working_copy.rs:668-677) emits an event and calls `engine::status::load(repo, &WorkingCopyStatusOptions::default())`. That load is a full libgit2 walk: `engine/status.rs:57-77` sets `include_untracked(true)` and `recurse_untracked_dirs(!opts.include_dirs)` and calls `repo.statuses(...)`. Worse than the finding says: `engine/index.rs:41-77` also does `index.write()` on every call — an on-disk .git/index rewrite, 20k times.

5) No `wcStageAll` TS wrapper exists, while the Rust commands are registered. `grep wcStageAll src/bridges/commands.ts` → nothing; `wc_stage_all`/`wc_unstage_all` are registered at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:82-83. Confirmed.

REPRO (scratch repo /tmp/verify-WC-06/repo, real git CLI, 20k untracked files):
- `git status --porcelain` (proxy for the `changed()` walk) costs 21ms at 20k untracked and 64-67ms once they are all staged — it is O(worktree), NOT O(remaining). So the per-call cost does not decay as the bulk progresses.
- 500-file bulk: per-path pipeline (`git add <one>` + 2 full status walks) = 22.16s; one-call batch (`git add <all 500>` + 1 status walk) = 0.06s → 392x.
- Extrapolated to the finding's 20k repro: ~15 minutes vs ~2.3 seconds. The CLI measurement includes process-spawn overhead the Tauri app does not pay, but the status walks (the dominant term) are identical work, so the ratio stands.

TWO AMPLIFIERS THE FINDING MISSES (both make it worse, not better):

A) The event handler doubles every status walk. `changed()` emits `AppEvent::WorkingCopyChanged`, and /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useAppEvents.ts:36-39 reacts with `void workingCopy.refresh(event.payload.repo)` — a second `wc_status_load` per staged path. This directly violates the invariant the backend states in its own module doc at commands/working_copy.rs:14-16: "a mutation answers with the fresh StatusDelta, so the UI never issues a second wc_status_load after a stage/unstage/discard." So the real cost per bulk path is 2 full walks, not 1. (My 500-file measurement already models both walks.)

B) The 20k invokes are fully serialized, so nothing hides the latency. src-tauri/src/state.rs:56-65 — every mutating command goes through `AppState::run` → `queue.enqueue(&repo_id).await`, and queue.rs:27 is a single tokio fair mutex per repo. `queue.rs:12-13` claims read-only loads "bypass the queue", but commands/working_copy.rs:992-997 routes `wc_status_load` through `state.run` like everything else, so the 20k event-driven refreshes also queue behind the 20k stages on the same mutex. The `void` fan-out buys zero parallelism; it just builds a 20k-deep FIFO.

Also confirmed: no busy indicator. WorkingCopyFileList.vue's bulk button (lines 97-104) has no `disabled`/`busy` binding, and App.vue's only pending flag is `committing` (App.vue:944), used only for the commit composer. So the button stays live for the whole ~15-minute drain and can be re-fired, queueing another 20k commands.

Error swallowing confirmed as described: store `stage` catch sets `state.value = errorState(error)` (workingCopy.ts:38-40), and the next successful `apply()` overwrites it (line 20-24). Also, with 20k racing `apply()` calls the visible list flickers through every intermediate delta.

Severity: major is correct, not blocker. The end state is right — staging paths one at a time produces the same index as staging them at once — so this is purely a performance and feedback defect, not a correctness or data-loss one. It bites on a plausible-but-not-universal input (a large generated/untracked tree).

Unrelated to the finding: the project working tree is clean (`git status --porcelain` is empty at ~/dev/CortexOS), and all my scratch work is in /tmp/verify-WC-06 — there is nothing half-done to commit.

findings.title: A status/delta response for another repository is applied to the current one (cross-repo race)
findings.evidence: src/stores/workingCopy.ts:20-33 — `apply(delta)` writes `entries`/`summary` with no check that `delta.repo` is the selected repository, even though `StatusDelta` carries `repo` (src-tauri/src/domain/status.rs:143-149). The watcher at src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:16-22 issues `store.refresh(id)` on every selection change, and `store.commit` (workingCopy.ts:68-84) refreshes the id it captured at call time. `repositories.select(id)` (src/stores/repos.ts:36-38 via src/composables/useRepositories.ts:72-74, reached from the command palette / recents list at App.vue:526-529 and 1332) does not clear the working-copy store.
findings.repro: 1. Open a repository with a large working copy (a slow `wc_status_load`). 2. Before it answers, switch to another repository (command palette → Open, or the recents list). 3. The first repository's rows, summary and the sidebar badge (src/App.vue:239-243) are rendered under the second repository's title; clicking 暂存 then issues `wc_stage_paths` against the second repo with paths from the first (which fails with an English 「No such file」, or worse, stages same-named files in the wrong repository).
findings.expected: The store ignores any delta whose `repo` is not the currently selected repository, and the list is cleared on repository switch.
findings.actual: The working-copy store holds one global `entries` list and `refresh()` applies whatever answer arrives, so an in-flight status load for repository A can land after the user has switched to repository B; A's rows then render under B, and the next stage/unstage runs against B with A's paths.
findings.fix: Tag the store with the repo it belongs to (`const repoId = ref<RepoId|null>(null)`); in `apply(delta)` ignore `delta.repo !== repos.selectedId` (or stash the delta and expose it through a per-repo map); clear `selectedPath` and the diff on selection change.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/workingCopy.test.ts: with repo A selected, resolve `wcStatusLoad` with `{repo:'B', entries:[…]}` and assert `store.entries` stays `[]`; then resolve with `{repo:'A', …}` and assert it is applied.

notes:
Re-traced every claimed line in /tmp/meridian-baseline and reproduced the bug. The finding is correct.

STORE APPLIES UNGUARDED. src/stores/workingCopy.ts:20-24 is `function apply(delta) { entries.value = delta.entries; summary.value = delta.summary; state.value = dataState(delta.entries); }` — no reference to delta.repo. Called from refresh (line 29), stage (37), unstage (45), discard (54), and via refresh from commit (75) and setAssumeUnchanged (95). Every caller passes a RepoId the store already has and then throws it away.

THE REPO FIELD EXISTS AND IS POPULATED. bindings.ts:116-120 `interface StatusDelta { repo: RepoId; entries: EntryStatus[]; summary: StatusSummary }`; the Rust read type is WorkingTreeStatus (src-tauri/src/domain/working_copy.rs:162-166) with the same `pub repo: RepoId`, and src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:67 fills it: `WorkingTreeStatus::new(cx.repo_id.clone(), entries)`. So the guard is available on the wire and simply not taken.

NO SEQUENCING ANYWHERE. grep for requestId|generation|seq|token|latest across src/stores/*.ts: zero hits. Neither the store nor the composable tracks which request is newest.

THE RUST QUEUE DOES NOT SERIALIZE THE RACE AWAY. RepoQueueManager::enqueue (src-tauri/src/queue.rs:27-36) keys its mutex map by RepoId (`queues.entry(repo.clone()).or_default()`), so a load for repo A and a load for repo B hold *different* mutexes and execute concurrently in separate spawn_blocking tasks (state.rs:68-86). Cross-repo overlap is the expected case, not an edge case.

NOTHING CLEARS THE STORE ON SWITCH. `select` in src/stores/repos.ts only assigns selectedId and calls loadRemotes; no workingCopy reset. grep for `$reset` across src/ finds nothing. App.vue:925 `const selectedPath = ref<string|null>(null)` is never cleared on repo change. The pane is not keyed — `grep -c ":key" src/App.vue` = 0 — so no remount discards the stale list.

REACHED FROM REAL UI PATHS. src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:16-22 watches repos.selectedId and fires `void store.refresh(id)` on every change; src/App.vue:1332 (palette `repo:` prefix) and 526-529 (openRepository → repositories.select) both drive it.

THE CODEBASE ALREADY GUARDS THIS EXACT CLASS ELSEWHERE — which is why it is a defect rather than a deliberate design choice. src/composables/useAppEvents.ts:31 and :37 both read `if (event.payload.repo !== repos.selectedId) return;`, and src/App.vue:518-520 comments "Compare is repository-scoped: it must not answer for the previous repo." The event-driven refresh path is guarded; the direct refresh path is not.

REPRODUCED, NOT JUST READ. In /tmp/verify-WC-07 I drove the real store with mocked commands: refresh("repoA") and refresh("repoB") in flight, B resolved first, A resolved second → `store.entries` ends as ["a.txt"] and `summary.unstaged` = 9 while B is the selection. The pre-fix test passes on the buggy code; after applying a monotonic-token guard the "buggy" assertion fails and the corrected assertion passes, with the existing src/stores/loadState.test.ts (5 tests) still green.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE IMPACT CLAIM (makes it worse, not better). The finding says the bad stage "fails with an English 「No such file」, or worse, stages same-named files in the wrong repository." In fact the silent-wrong-stage is the *default* for tracked names and the error is the rarer branch: validation::working_copy::validate_paths (src-tauri/src/validation/working_copy.rs:20-43) only rejects absolute/parent-dir escapes, and engine::index::stage_paths (src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:41-76) checks `if tracked { continue; }` before its `!workdir.join(path).exists()` guard — so a tracked path of the same name in repo B is staged into B with no error at all. Note the wired call is `engine::index::stage_paths` (commands/working_copy.rs:208); the near-duplicate in engine/working_tree.rs:55 is dead code for this command, so it is not the one that matters.

SEVERITY: major is right. Realistic trigger (large working copy → slow wc_status_load → user switches repo mid-flight) is ordinary, and the consequence is a mutation (stage/unstage) applied to a repository the user is not looking at. Not a blocker: it needs a timing window, the most common outcome is a wrong list plus an error toast, and discard is behind a confirm dialogue.

Files: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/workingCopy.ts, /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts, /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/repos.ts, /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useAppEvents.ts, /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/queue.rs, /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs; repro at /tmp/verify-WC-07/src/stores/workingCopy.race.test.ts.

REPRODUCED empirically. I drove the real useWorkingCopyStore and the real useWorkingCopy() composable (with its selection watcher), mocking only the Tauri IPC boundary, against a pristine copy of the baseline (store md5 30e18a74... verified identical before and after the run). Resolving repo A's wc_status_load AFTER repo B's leaves repos.selectedId === "repo-b" while store.entries === ["a-owned.ts"] and store.summary.unstaged === 1: A's rows and A's sidebar badge (App.vue:239-243 workingCopyTotal reads workingCopy.summary) render under B's title. Clicking 暂存 on that stale row issues wc_stage_paths("repo-b", ["src/app.ts"]) — confirmed by mock assertion.

The backend does not prevent it: RepoQueueManager::enqueue keys its queue by RepoId (src-tauri/src/queue.rs:33), so loads for two different repos run concurrently, and AppState::run gives no cross-repo ordering. StatusDelta (domain/status.rs:143-149) and WorkingTreeStatus (domain/working_copy.rs:162-166) both carry `repo`, so the data needed to reject the delta is present — apply() at workingCopy.ts:20-24 just never reads it. The finding's evidence is accurate.

Git CLI consequences verified in two scratch repos sharing src/app.ts: (1) an A-only path against B fails, pathspec did not match any files, exit 128 — the finding's "fails" branch; (2) a same-named path that B had also modified was SILENTLY STAGED in B (exit 0, staged content was B's own edit) — the finding's "or worse" branch, confirmed. The state does not self-correct: there is no polling in the store, and the workingCopyChanged handler already filters on repo !== selectedId (useAppEvents.ts:37), so stale rows persist until an explicit refresh.

Severity major confirmed. Cross-repo mutation is the deciding factor: staging is recoverable, but the same store's discard/wc_paths_discard is Risk::Destructive and runs checkout_head/checkout_index with .force() (engine/index.rs:214-305), and commit would commit the wrong repo's index. Discard has a path-naming confirm dialog, which bounds it.

Two corrections to the finding's details. (1) The trigger window is narrower than described: it requires A's load still in flight at the switch, i.e. a genuinely slow wc_status_load — uncommon, though exactly the large-working-copy case the repro names. (2) Sibling stores share the flaw and the finding omits them: stores/history.ts:85-95 and stores/branches.ts:24-36 apply loads with no repo check or generation token, so the same switch corrupts history and branch lists. useCompare already implements the correct pattern (forRepo with a monotonic requestToken, useCompare.ts:165-175), so workingCopy is the outlier.

I validated the proposed fix on a scratch copy: with repoId tracking plus clearing entries/summary in refresh, the store retains b-owned.ts and the 108 pre-existing tests still pass (only the three bug-asserting repro assertions failed).

findings.title: A failed stage/unstage replaces the whole working-copy tab with an error, and in a bulk action the failure is never shown at all
findings.evidence: src/stores/workingCopy.ts:35-49 — `catch (error) { state.value = errorState(error) }`, with no `lastError` write (unlike discard/commit/openEntry at workingCopy.ts:53-61/69-83) and no return value. src/App.vue:1493-1494 discards the returned promise (`void workingCopy.stage(path)`), so no toast can ever be raised. src/components/panes/WorkingCopyPane.vue:163-172 hands that state to ListShell, whose error arm replaces the entire tab with `state.error.message` + a Retry button. Engine side, `ErrorClass::Index + Git2Code::Locked` maps to `ErrorCode::IndexLocked` (src-tauri/src/engine/error.rs:21) — reachable whenever another git process holds `.git/index.lock`, and `engine/index.rs:59-65` refuses with 「No such file: {path}」 when the file vanished after the list was drawn.
findings.repro: 1. In a terminal run a long `git add .` in the same repository so `.git/index.lock` exists. 2. In Meridian's working copy click 暂存 on any row: the whole tab is replaced by 「另一个 Git 进程正在使用该仓库，请关闭后重试。」 plus a Retry button — the file list, the composer and the sidebar context are all gone, and no toast explains what happened. 3. Repeat via 暂存所有 (WC-06): the failing call sets the error state, the next successful call overwrites it with data, and the user is told nothing at all.
findings.expected: A failed stage shows a toast naming the file and the reason, and leaves the list intact (the delta did not change).
findings.actual: Single-file stage/unstage failures turn the entire working-copy tab into one error message (losing the list, the composer and the detail pane), and bulk-stage failures are overwritten by the next successful delta so they are never reported anywhere.
findings.fix: Keep the list state for data errors: on failure set `lastError` and leave `state` as-is (or add a per-row error), then have App.vue report it exactly like discard/commit do (`reportError(workingCopy.lastError.value, …)`). For bulk actions, aggregate failures and report once.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/workingCopy.test.ts: make `commands.wcStagePaths` reject with an ErrorPayload; assert `store.entries` is unchanged, `store.lastError` is the payload, and `store.state.status !== 'error'`.

notes: Reproduced concretely in three independent ways. (1) Real git: with .git/index.lock present, `git add <path>` fails (exit 128). (2) libgit2, the engine's actual backend: I compiled a minimal crate against the cached git2 0.21.0 and ran the exact engine::index::stage_paths sequence (repo.index() -> add_all -> write). With the lock present, index.write() returns class=Index, code=Locked, which engine/error.rs:21 maps to ErrorCode::IndexLocked (retryable=true) — the claimed reachable path. The alternate path (file vanished) is engine/index.rs:59-65 returning InvalidRequest "No such file: {path}", also confirmed by reading. (3) The store, run under vitest with wcStagePaths rejecting: after store.stage the result is state.status="error", entries.length=1 (unchanged), lastError=null, and state.error.code="index_locked". For the bulk path (App.vue:1497 does paths.forEach(p => void workingCopy.stage(p)), i.e. N independent calls each calling apply()), a rejection sets error, then the next success calls apply() -> dataState() and wipes it: after failure status="error", after success status="data", lastError=null. So the finding's core claims all hold: the catch at workingCopy.ts:35-49 writes only `state` (no lastError, no return value), App.vue:1493-1494 discards the promise via `void` so no toast can fire, and ListShell's error arm (ListShell.vue:64-69) replaces its default slot — which in WorkingCopyPane holds the MasterDetail (file list + CommitComposer + detail pane). The single-file case is not silent (an error panel with a Retry button is shown), but it wrongly blanks the whole list/composer/detail on a mutation failure, diverging from the app's own pattern where discard/commit/setAssumeUnchanged write lastError and App.vue toasts it. The bulk case is genuinely silent. Two overstatements in the finding, neither refuting: the sidebar is a separate pane and is not lost, and the composer's typed text lives in App.vue refs so it is not destroyed (only unmounted until Retry). Also, the repro quotes the zh-CN byCode string 「另一个 Git 进程正在使用该仓库…」, but the pane renders the raw state.error.message (libgit2's English "the index is locked; …"); the localizer errorText() in i18n/index.ts has zero callers (dead code), so the localized string is never shown. That is cosmetic and does not change the defect.

Every link in the claimed chain verified verbatim in the snapshot; no guard, default, other caller, catalogue entry or handler rescues it.

STORE (workingCopy.ts:35-49) — matches the claim exactly. stage/unstage do `catch (error) { state.value = errorState(error) }` with no lastError write and no return value, unlike discard (53-61), commit (68-84) and openEntry (87-94) which each write `lastError` and return a sentinel.

CALLER (App.vue:1493-1494) — `@stage="(path) => void workingCopy.stage(path)"`, `@unstage` likewise. `workingCopy` at App.vue:127 is the composable; useWorkingCopy.ts:33-41 forwards straight to `store.stage(id, [path])` with zero error handling. `reportError` (App.vue:548) is unreachable for stage/unstage: its only workingCopy call sites are 903 (setAssumeUnchanged), 920 (discard), 1011 (commit).

RENDER — WorkingCopyPane.vue:168 passes state.error.message to ListShell; ListShell.vue:64-69 is a `v-else-if` ahead of `<slot v-else />` at line 71. The MasterDetail holding the file list, CommitComposer and WorkingCopyFileDetail (WorkingCopyPane.vue:228-296) is inside that default slot, so it is replaced.

SEARCHED FOR A RESCUING GUARD, NONE EXISTS — no watcher on workingCopy.state anywhere in src/; no window error/unhandledrejection handler (the only addEventListener in src/ is `hashchange`, router/index.ts:67); no app-wide error bus; no `wcStageAll` binding anywhere (bulk is literally `paths.forEach((path) => void workingCopy.stage(path))`, App.vue:1497, so a later success overwrites the earlier errorState); the `workingCopyChanged` refresh path in useAppEvents.ts:36-39 can never fire because the engine emits nothing matching that name (grep workingCopyChanged in src-tauri/ is empty).

REACHABILITY HOLDS — engine/error.rs:21 maps (ErrorClass::Index, Git2Code::Locked) -> ErrorCode::IndexLocked; engine/index.rs:59-65 returns InvalidRequest "No such file: {path}" when an untracked file vanished after the list was drawn. Note the test file named in the finding does not exist: there is no src/stores/workingCopy.test.ts, so this store has no coverage at all.

THREE CORRECTIONS, NONE OF WHICH RESCUE THE BEHAVIOUR — (1) The sidebar is NOT affected: it is a separate shell slot at App.vue:1410-1427, outside the pane. (2) The toolbar DOES survive: ListShell.vue:43 renders `<slot name="toolbar" />` outside the status conditional, so refresh/counts/conflict-toggle remain; what is lost is the merge banner (WorkingCopyPane.vue:200), the file list, the composer and the detail pane. "The whole tab is replaced" overstates it, and the surviving toolbar refresh is a recovery path. (3) The repro's quoted string is wrong: 「另一个 Git 进程正在使用该仓库，请关闭后重试。」 is errors.byCode.index_locked (zh-CN.ts:163), but errorText() (i18n/index.ts:159) has ZERO consumers — the pane renders state.error.message raw, i.e. the untranslated libgit2 text. That makes the real UX worse than described, not better.

SEVERITY KEPT AT MAJOR — the bulk path is a true silent failure (stage 20, one file deleted mid-flight, 19 succeed, nothing is said anywhere) and the single-file path destroys the composer and detail pane for a recoverable condition. It is not a blocker: no data is corrupted (the delta did not change), the list is restorable via the Try again button (App.vue emits refresh) or the surviving toolbar refresh, and the repo has an intact repo-lock guard (state.rs:65 enqueue).

findings.title: Diff documents are silently truncated above 40k lines and the image-diff branch is unreachable
findings.evidence: The engine sets `truncated` (src-tauri/src/engine/diff.rs:397-399, 589-625) and the domain documents that "the UI shows its large-diff warning" (src-tauri/src/domain/working_copy.rs:21-27), but the mapping in src/stores/viewModels.ts:132-164 copies only path/oldPath/perspective/rows/stats/isBinary — `truncated` is dropped, so `document.tooLarge` (src/components/contracts.ts:134) stays undefined and the gate at src/components/diff/DiffViewer.vue:317-329 never renders. The same mapping never sets `document.image`, although the viewer implements that state (DiffViewer.vue:341-357), and `wcImageDataLoad` (src/bridges/commands.ts:229-231) has no caller — a PNG therefore falls into the generic binary branch.
findings.repro: 1. Open a generated/large file (>40 000 diff lines, e.g. a minified bundle with local edits). 2. Select it in the working copy: the diff stops silently at the first ~40k lines with no banner, no count and no "show anyway" — the user reads a diff that is not the diff, and cannot tell. 3. Select `logo.png`: the viewer shows 「二进制文件」 instead of the image pair; no `` is ever produced because nothing calls `wcImageDataLoad` and `toDiffDocument` never sets `image`.
findings.expected: A truncated document surfaces the large-diff warning (with the elided size/line count) instead of showing a partial diff as if it were complete; an image file opens the image comparison.
findings.actual: A diff over `MAX_DOCUMENT_LINES` (40 000) is cut off with no warning anywhere, and image files always render the generic binary placeholder.
findings.fix: In `toDiffDocument`, map `wire.truncated` onto `tooLarge` (e.g. `{bytes: oldSize+newSize, gate: MAX_DOCUMENT_LINES}`) and map image extensions (use `engine::diff::mime_for` — exposed by `wc_image_data_load.mime`) onto `image`; then have the store fetch both sides with `wcImageDataLoad` when `image` is set so the viewer can render the pair.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/viewModels.test.ts: `toDiffDocument({truncated: true, change: {oldSize: 5, newSize: 6}, …}, "f")` must set `tooLarge`; `toDiffDocument` for `logo.png` must set `image`. Plus a DiffViewer test asserting the gate renders when `tooLarge` is set.

notes: Traced line by line in /tmp/meridian-baseline; the path behaves exactly as claimed, and two extra defects make it worse than described. 1. Engine sets the flag. src-tauri/src/engine/diff.rs:397-399 assigns `doc.truncated = truncated` from `collect_hunks`; collect_hunks (589-625) hard-caps at `budget = MAX_DOCUMENT_LINES` (= 40_000, domain/working_copy.rs:24), sets `truncated = true`, and breaks out of BOTH the line loop and the hunk loop — the returned hunk list is genuinely partial. The wire type binds it: `truncated: boolean` (bridges/bindings.ts:399). 2. The one and only mapper drops it. stores/diff.ts:41 is the sole caller of `toDiffDocument` (grep confirms: the other two "callers" are `diffCommands.loadDiff` → `useDiffDocument`, which itself has zero consumers — dead legacy port). viewModels.ts:156-163 returns an object literal containing exactly path/oldPath/perspective/rows/stats/binary. `truncated` and any image marker are absent. 3. Nothing else sets the two optional fields. `grep -rn tooLarge src/` returns only contracts.ts:134 (the type) and DiffViewer.vue:317/323/324 (the reads). `document.image` is never assigned anywhere in src/. So DiffViewer.vue:317 (`v-else-if="document.tooLarge"`) can never be true, and :341 (`v-else-if="document.image"`) can never be true. 4. The binary branch does fire for PNGs. `is_binary` (diff.rs:531-535) returns true for image deltas, and the template order is tooLarge → binary (:334) → image (:341), so `logo.png` always lands on 「二进制文件」. 5. No image data path exists. `wcImageDataLoad` (bridges/commands.ts:229-231) has zero callers; the Rust command IS registered (lib.rs:93) and `mime_for` exists (diff.rs:1184). Worse than reported: the image branch contains NO `` element at all — only two `

CONFIRMED empirically on both halves; every cited line reference checks out. BACKEND (rebuilt git2 0.21 offline against the cached crate; faithful ports of `is_binary` diff.rs:531-535, `collect_hunks` diff.rs:586-625, `pick_delta`, and `EngineDiffOptions::git2()` diff.rs:96-110). Scratch repo /tmp/verify-WC-09/scratch, run at /tmp/verify-WC-09/rustrepro: - bundle.js with a 120,000-line change (WorkingTreeToBase): engine keeps exactly 40,000 lines, `truncated = true`. additions/deletions = 60000/60000. - logo.png (valid PNG, byte-modified): `is_binary = true`; `truncated = false` (the `if !binary` guard skips collect_hunks). - Control small.txt: `truncated = false`. SERDE: `#[derive(Serialize)] #[serde(rename_all="camelCase")] pub struct DiffDocument { … pub truncated: bool, … }` (working_copy.rs:399-412) has NO skip_serializing_if on `truncated`, so `"truncated": true` is ALWAYS on the wire. The TS binding src/bridges/bindings.ts also declares `truncated: boolean` — the field is present in the mapper's input type and is dropped anyway. FRONTEND (real `toDiffDocument` from the snapshot, executed via node type-stripping): - `toDiffDocument({…, truncated: true, …}, null)` → `doc.tooLarge === undefined`, `"tooLarge" in doc === false`; `doc.rows.length = 40001` (all 40,000 partial lines). PNG wire → `binary: true`, `image: undefined`. - DiffViewer.vue v-else-if chain evaluated in source order (loading → error → !document → tooLarge(317) → binary(336) → image(341) → text): the truncated doc selects the **"text document" fallthrough**, so the partial diff renders with no banner/count; the PNG selects the **binary** branch ("二进制文件", zh-CN diff.ts:86), confirming the repro exactly. WIRING: `stores/diff.ts:41` is the only caller of `toDiffDocument` (grep: no other call sites). `wcImageDataLoad` (bridges/commands.ts:229) and `DiffPort.loadImage` (diffCommands.ts:71) have zero callers; useDiffDocument.ts only calls `port.loadDiff` and `port.applyChunk`. TWO CORROBORATING DETAILS THAT STRENGTHEN "major": 1. The stats header actively lies. Engine `additions/deletions` come from `patch.line_stats()`, which is NOT bounded by the 40,000 budget, so the UI displays "+60000/−60000" while rendering only 40,000 lines — the truncated diff looks authoritative rather than merely partial. 2. There is no workaround. `showFull` only raises context to FULL_CONTEXT_LINES=100,000 (diff.rs:33,90-94); `collect_hunks` still caps at MAX_DOCUMENT_LINES=40,000, so `truncated` is set for any >40k-line diff regardless of options. The user cannot obtain the full diff at all, and gets no signal that they haven't. MINOR INACCURACY IN THE FINDING (does not change the verdict): the finding attributes the missing `` to "nothing calls wcImageDataLoad and toDiffDocument never sets image". The second clause is the operative cause, but there is a third, independent one — the DiffViewer image branch (341-357) contains ZERO `` elements (`grep -c "` plus before/after size captions. So the branch itself is a scaffold that never shows pixels. SEVERITY: major is correct, not minor. The engine's own doc comment (working_copy.rs:21-23) states the contract "the UI shows its large-diff warning … instead of a frozen renderer"; that contract is unimplemented, the failure is fully silent (no banner, no count, no "show anyway"), the displayed stats contradict the rendered content, and no option escapes the cap. Silent display of a partial diff as if complete is a correctness/trust failure, not a cosmetic gap.

findings.title: 'Open in editor' failures are invisible, including for a deleted file
