Nothing clears or re-scopes selection on tab change. Grep for `selectedOid` in App.vue shows only 1534 and 1632 (both panes) plus 1555/1661 `selectedPath` — no reset site exists.

REPRO HOLDS in both directions. Compare→history is the worse half: the history detail pane renders whatever `history.detail` holds (CommitDetailPane.vue:63-64 gates only on `state.status === "data"`), so returning to 历史 shows a full diff/changeset for a commit chosen on the other screen, with no row highlighted if that oid is outside the loaded 250-row history page.

PARTIAL MITIGATION THE AUDITOR MISSED (does not refute, but bounds the severity): `reconcileSelection()` (stores/history.ts:65-72) drops a selection that is not in the loaded commits, and it runs from `apply()` — i.e. on `refresh()` (filter/search/sort change), but NOT on `select()` and NOT from `loadMore()`. So a compare-driven selection that is outside the history page self-heals the next time the user re-filters history. When the compare-selected commit is inside the history page (the common case — both are recent commits), it never heals and the history cursor just silently moves. This is a dirty-state bug with a partial, non-deterministic cleanup, not a corruption bug.

OVER-CLAIMED DETAIL: "a double-click and a single click are identical" is true but is NOT an extra defect. HistoryPane wires `@select` and `@activate` to the same `onHistorySelect` (App.vue:1536-1537), so identical click/dblclick is the established house pattern, not an inconsistency introduced here. Don't let the fix invent a distinct dblclick behavior.

Severity: minor is right. No crash, no data loss, no wrong git operation — the commit shown is always a real commit and the highlight always matches the detail. It is a wrong-selection/confusing-state bug ("stale-ui") whose blast radius is one stale ref in a store. It would be major only if a verb acted on `history.selectedOid` without re-reading the row; grep shows no such consumer (blame/editor paths all take the oid emitted by the clicked row), so minor stands.

Also checked and ruled out as refutations: no test file asserts the shared selection as intended (there is no `src/composables/useCompare.test.ts` and no test anywhere matching "compare" or "selectedOid"), so there is no contract making this deliberate; and the store's own doc comment ("Selection lives here — not in App.vue and never component-local — so the keyboard cursor, the detail pane and the graph all read one source of truth") is scoped to the history screen's own consumers, not to cross-tab sharing.

findings.title: branch_checkout never deserializes: UI sends opts:{} but Rust CheckoutOptions.detach is a required field
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs:41-45 — `#[derive(...)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct CheckoutOptions { pub detach: bool }` has NO #[serde(default)] on the struct or the field, so `detach` is a required key. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/bridges/commands.ts:152-158 defaults `opts: CheckoutOptions = {}` and always sends `args: { repo, name, opts }`. The only call site, /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts:63, is `commands.branchCheckout(repo, name, {})`. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/commands/branches.rs:104-105 has `#[serde(default)]` on `opts` only (that default applies when `opts` is absent, not when it is `{}`). /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/bridges/bindings.ts:233-235 declares `detach?: boolean` (optional), so the TS side believes it may omit it. CLAUDE.md:68-69 states the invariant this breaks: 'every field the frontend can omit carries #[serde(default)]'.
findings.repro: Open any repository, go to the Branches tab, double-click a local branch row (or click the sidebar row's ⋯, or the palette's branch item, or the detail pane's Checkout button). Same for the toolbar Branch ▾ → Checkout branch. Any of these calls App.vue:875 `branches.checkout(branch?.name ?? name)` → stores/branches.ts:63 `branchCheckout(repo, name, {})`.
findings.expected: HEAD switches to the branch, a success toast '已签出分支 X' appears, and the working copy/branch list reload.
findings.actual: Tauri fails while deserializing the command arguments (missing field `detach`), before AppState::run is ever entered, so the engine never runs and HEAD never moves. The rejection is not an ErrorPayload, so App.vue:548-554 reportError() cannot read `.message` and falls back to the generic toast '无法签出该分支。' ('Could not check out the branch.') with no cause — exactly the owner's 'fails with no error shown'. Checkout is unreachable from every entry point in the branch surface.
findings.fix: Add `#[serde(default)]` to CheckoutOptions (container level) in src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs, matching the crate convention used by MergeOptions/RebaseOptions (commands/integrate.rs:78-79, 226-227). Optionally also change the bridge default to an explicit `{ detach: false }` so the payload is self-describing. Independently, make reportError() fall back to `errorText()` (see BR-07) so a non-ErrorPayload rejection still tells the user something.
findings.testIdea: src-tauri: a unit test in src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs (or tests/) asserting `serde_json::from_value::<CheckoutOptions>(serde_json::json!({}))` is `Ok` and yields `detach == false`. Frontend: src/stores/branches.test.ts — invoke the store's `checkout('r', 'main')` against a mocked `commands.branchCheckout` and assert it was called with a full options object (`expect(branchCheckout).toHaveBeenCalledWith('r', 'main', { detach: false })`), which fails today with `{}` only if the mock is typed as the Rust shape.

notes:
Confirmed — I re-traced every hop and found no guard, default, or handler that rescues it.

(1) /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs:41-45 — CheckoutOptions is `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct CheckoutOptions { pub detach: bool }`. Neither the container nor the field carries `#[serde(default)]`. `derive(Default)` does not influence `Deserialize`, so serde still treats `detach` as a required key. Exact match to the claim.

(2) commands/branches.rs:104-105 — `#[serde(default)] pub opts: CheckoutOptions` on BranchCheckout. That default applies only when the `opts` key is entirely absent from the JSON; it does not reach into the nested struct. The key is never absent: commands.ts:152-158 always builds `args: { repo, name, opts }` with `opts: CheckoutOptions = {}`.

(3) bindings.ts:233-235 declares `detach?: boolean`, so the TS type system permits `{}` and tsc reports nothing — the shape mismatch is invisible from the frontend.

(4) commands/branches.rs:161-168 — `#[tauri::command] pub async fn branch_checkout(state: State<AppState>, app: AppHandle, args: BranchCheckout) -> ... { state.run(&app, args).await }`. Tauri deserializes `args` from the invoke payload before the fn body executes, so `AppState::run` is never reached and the engine never runs.

(5) `grep -rn branchCheckout src/` returns exactly one call site: stores/branches.ts:63, `commands.branchCheckout(repo, name, {})`. Every entry point in the branch surface (App.vue:875, reached from row dblclick 1592, row ⋯ 1422, palette 1278/1333, detail-pane @checkout 1595/1610, toolbar 614/703) funnels into it. Nothing can bypass it.

(6) Convention cross-check backs the diagnosis rather than refuting it: MergeOptions (commands/integrate.rs:78-80) and RebaseOptions (226-228) both use `#[serde(default, rename_all = "camelCase")]` at container level. `grep -rn "serde(default)" src-tauri/src/domain/` yields hits only in commit.rs and app.rs — nothing in refs.rs, so CheckoutOptions is the lone outlier in refs.rs, not a deliberate design choice.

(7) Test-coverage gap that explains survival: `ls src/stores/*.test.ts` returns only loadState.test.ts with zero checkout references; src-tauri/tests/ contains changelog_parity.rs, github_metadata.rs, handler_completeness.rs and nothing that exercises the wire shape. handler_completeness.rs only checks that each `#[tauri::command]` is registered in generate_handler!, which is a different invariant, so it cannot catch this.

(8) Failure surfacing matches the report: the store catches the rejection and assigns it to lastError; App.vue:548-554 reportError tests `"message" in error`, which is false for Tauri v2's plain-string deserialization rejection, so the user gets the bare `shell.toast.checkoutFailed` toast with no cause.

One nuance that does not move the verdict: branch_checkout_remote, branch_checkout_revision, and branchCreate(..., checkout: true) route through different argument structs and remain functional, so it is not literally every git operation. But checkout of an existing local branch — the core action of a Git client, and the one every entry point in the branch surface is built around — is dead from every route with a silent generic error. Blocker is correct; I found nothing that argues for major or minor.

findings.title: Checking out a remote-tracking branch whose short name already exists locally always fails
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts:72-86: `checkoutRemote` computes `suggestedName` = the short name ('main' from 'origin/main') and then deliberately passes `localName = nameExists ? undefined : suggestedName`. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/branches.rs:584 raises ReferenceExists when the local name is taken: `let name = local_name.unwrap_or(&short); if repo.find_branch(&name, Local).is_ok() { return Err(... "Branch '{name}' already exists") }` — and the same check is duplicated at 586-600. So when the local branch exists the UI withholds the name and the engine then re-derives exactly that name and refuses. Reached from /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:855-869 (checkoutFlow's `branch?.isRemote === true` arm), i.e. row dblclick (App.vue:1592), the checkout dialogue (App.vue:842-849 lists allBranches with emitFullName), and the palette only lists locals so it is unaffected.
findings.repro: In a normal clone (local `main` tracking `origin/main`), open the Branches tab, set the filter to 全部 or 远程, and double-click the `origin/main` row. Verified against real git in /tmp/audit-branch: with `main` and `origin/main` present, `git checkout main` switches to the local branch and reports '您的分支与上游分支 origin/main 一致'.
findings.expected: Switch to the existing local branch `main` (what `git checkout main` does), or, if the user really wants a second branch at origin/main's tip, ask for a distinct name.
findings.actual: English toast 'Branch \'main\' already exists' in the zh-CN UI and no checkout. The obvious intent — get onto main — is refused with no way forward, because nothing in the branch surface exposes a name prompt for this verb.
findings.fix: In stores/branches.ts:72-86, when `nameExists` is true, check out the existing local branch instead of calling checkout_remote (i.e. fall through to `commands.branchCheckout(repo, suggestedName)`), or pass a de-duplicated name such as `main-2` and surface it in the toast. Fix the engine's duplicated existence check at engine/branches.rs:586-600 at the same time.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/branches.test.ts — with a store fixture where `branches = [{name:'main'}]` and a mocked `branchCheckoutRemote`, call `checkoutRemote('refs/remotes/origin/main')` and assert the local branch path is taken (`expect(branchCheckout).toHaveBeenCalledWith(repo,'main',...)`) rather than `branchCheckoutRemote` with `localName === undefined`.

notes:
CONFIRMED. Every link in the chain verified in the baseline snapshot.

Frontend (/tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts:72-86) verified verbatim. Lines 77-79:
  const nameExists = branches.value.some((b) => b.name === suggestedName);
  await commands.branchCheckoutRemote(repo, shorthand, nameExists ? undefined : suggestedName, true);
suggestedName is derived by stripping "refs/remotes/" then cutting at the first "/" — for "refs/remotes/origin/main" that is "main".

Engine (/tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/branches.rs:563-601) verified verbatim:
  let shorthand = remote_ref.name()?.unwrap_or(remote_branch).to_string();
  let short = shorthand.split_once('/').map(|(_, rest)| rest.to_string())...
  let name = local_name.unwrap_or(&short).to_string();
  if repo.find_branch(&name, git2::BranchType::Local).is_ok() { return Err(ReferenceExists, "Branch '{name}' already exists") }

DECISIVE CHECK. The one uncertainty that could have refuted this was what libgit2's Branch::name() returns for a remote ref, since that determines which name the engine re-derives. It is pinned by the repo's OWN test at engine/branches.rs:1065:
  assert_eq!(resolved.name, "origin/feature", "form {form}");
with full_name == "refs/remotes/origin/feature". So for refs/remotes/origin/main, name() == "origin/main", and split_once('/') yields short == "main" — exactly the name the UI withheld. The guard is self-cancelling: it withholds the name precisely when the local exists, then the engine re-derives that same name and refuses. Its only effect is to strip the UI's ability to disambiguate; it cannot prevent the collision.

GUARD SEARCH (my default assumption was that a guard existed somewhere). I checked every candidate and found none:
- BranchCheckoutRemote::validate (commands/refs.rs:134-137) only calls require_not_bare + require_no_integration — no name/existence check.
- The ReferenceExists check at validation/branches.rs:28 belongs to validate_create (branch_create), a different verb.
- BranchListPane.vue:125 emits 'activate' for every row including remote, with no collision guard.
- App.vue:855 checkoutFlow: `if (branch?.isRemote === true)` goes straight to checkoutRemote.
- App.vue:503 checkoutSelectedBranch: `if (!branch?.isRemote) return;` then straight to checkoutRemote.
- App.vue:548-554 reportError pushes the raw engine message string, confirming the untranslated English toast in a zh-CN UI.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding, neither changing the verdict:
1. It MISSED a third entry point. The detail pane wires @checkout -> checkoutFlow(selectedBranchInfo.fullName) (App.vue:1609) and @pull -> checkoutSelectedBranch() (App.vue:1617). Both funnel into the same broken call, widening the blast radius beyond the two paths it cited.
2. "No way forward" is overstated. The filter defaults to "local" (App.vue:1086), so the failing row is not visible until the user switches to 全部/远程; switching back to 本地 and double-clicking the local `main` row works. A working equivalent is one click away.

ALSO CONFIRMED: the duplicated existence check at branches.rs:595-601 is real dead code and genuinely unreachable — the first block (587-593) returns for every case the second would match. There is no src/stores/branches.test.ts in the baseline (stores/ contains only loadState.test.ts), so the proposed test would be new.

SEVERITY CORRECTED blocker -> major. It fails safely (error toast; no crash, no data loss, no corruption), a working equivalent is one click away, and the verb's primary purpose — creating a tracking branch from a remote-ONLY branch — works correctly, since nameExists is false there and the UI supplies the name. This is a real defect on a common path (any normal clone has a local `main` tracking `origin/main`), but not an unusable or unsafe one, which is what blocker should be reserved for.

findings.title: Remote branches are half-wired: the detail pane is empty for them and every name lookup resolves against local branches only
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:1089-1094 — `selectedBranchInfo` searches `branches.branches.value`, which /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts:10-11 and 31 document and populate as LOCAL branches only (`branchList(repo, 'local')`; engine/branches.rs:56-60 maps Local to git2::BranchType::Local). But the list is fed the union (`:branches="branches.allBranches.value"`, App.vue:1586) and a row click emits `fullName` (BranchListPane.vue:124), so selecting `refs/remotes/origin/main` sets selectedBranchName to a name that lookup can never find → `:branch="selectedBranchInfo"` (App.vue:1607) is null → BranchDetailPane renders its EmptyState ('未选择分支' / '选一个分支，即可看到它的操作。', i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/panes.ts:189-190). Consequently the whole remote arm of the detail pane — the 抓取到本地 button (BranchDetailPane.vue:150-153) and App.vue:1615 checkoutSelectedBranch / App.vue:503-513 — is unreachable code. The same local-only lookup is used for the other verbs: renameBranchFlow (App.vue:775) and deleteBranch (App.vue:814) fall back to using the raw `selectedBranchName` as the old name when the lookup misses, and the toolbar's Branch ▾ → Rename (App.vue:704 → renameBranchFlow() with no preset) picks up that raw value.
findings.repro: (a) Branches tab → filter 远程 → click `origin/main`: the detail column shows '未选择分支'. (b) Same selection, then toolbar Branch ▾ → 重命名分支: the prompt is pre-filled with `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and confirming calls branch_rename with that value, which require_branch (commands/refs.rs:1793-1802) rejects with the English 'Branch \'refs/remotes/origin/main\' does not exist'.
findings.expected: Selecting a remote branch shows its detail (oid, tracking, and the remote-only verb), and Rename/Delete either act on something meaningful or are disabled for a remote ref.
findings.actual: Remote rows are selectable but lead to an empty detail pane with no explanation; Rename on that selection fails with a raw English error.
findings.fix: Resolve `selectedBranchInfo` against `branches.allBranches.value` (App.vue:1092) so the remote arm renders; guard renameBranchFlow/deleteBranch (App.vue:773-776, 812-815) on `branch?.isRemote` and refuse locally instead of passing a full refname through, and disable the two verbs in the toolbar when the selection is remote.
findings.testIdea: src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.test.ts — mount with `branch` set to a remote BranchReviewInfo and assert the 抓取到本地 button and the cloud icon render. Plus a test in src/App.test.ts (or a composable test) asserting `selectedBranchInfo` is non-null when `selectedBranchName` is 'refs/remotes/origin/main'.

notes:
Confirmed end to end; no guard, default, or handler anywhere in the chain rescues it.

(1) stores/branches.ts:11 keeps `branches` local-only and `refresh()` (24-26) fills it from `branchList(repo,"local")` while `remoteBranches` gets the "remote" pass; `allBranches` (31) is the union. The filter is honored, not silently ignored: bridges/commands.ts:134-140 forwards `filter`, src-tauri/src/commands/branches.rs:37 passes it to `engine::branches::list`, and engine/branches.rs:56-60 maps Local to `git2::BranchType::Local`.

(2) The Pinia-unwrapping red herring is not in play: App.vue:128 is `const branches = useBranches()` (composables/useBranches.ts:14 exposes `branches = computed(() => store.branches)`), so `branches.branches.value` legitimately reads the local-only list.

(3) App.vue:1092 resolves `selectedBranchName` against that local-only list, while App.vue:1586 feeds BranchListPane `branches.allBranches.value`, and BranchListPane.vue:124 emits `filtered[index].fullName` which App.vue:1591 stores verbatim. For a remote row `fullName` is the full ref path (engine/branches.rs:753 uses `branch.get().name()`, i.e. `refs/remotes/origin/main`), so the `.find` at 1092 can never match -> `selectedBranchInfo` is null -> BranchDetailPane.vue:70-75 renders EmptyState with exactly the zh-CN strings at i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/panes.ts:189-190.

(4) The remote arm is genuinely unreachable: BranchDetailPane.vue:150-153 (抓取到本地 / `fetchIntoLocal`) sits behind `v-else` on `remote`, which is derived from `props.branch?.isRemote` — always false for entries in a local-only list. Its only caller is `checkoutSelectedBranch` (App.vue:503-513, itself guarded `if (!branch?.isRemote) return;`), wired at App.vue:1615; grep finds no other call site.

(5) The rename repro holds. No watcher ever normalizes `selectedBranchName` (only writes are 413, 792, 1591). The toolbar option `branch.rename` is disabled only on `!hasRepo` (App.vue:615), `onToolbarChoose` (700-704) calls `renameBranchFlow()` with no preset, so App.vue:773 takes the raw fullName, the local-only lookup at 775 misses, `oldName` stays `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and `BranchRename::validate` -> `require_branch` (commands/refs.rs:1793-1802) does `find_branch(name, BranchType::Local)`, i.e. looks for `refs/heads/refs/remotes/origin/main`, misses, and returns the untranslated English "Branch 'refs/remotes/origin/main' does not exist" surfaced by `reportError`.

Not a blocker: `require_branch` runs in `validate`, before `execute`, so nothing mutates and no ref is touched; and the underlying capability is still reachable by double-clicking a remote row, which emits `activate` -> `checkoutFlow` -> `branches.checkoutRemote` (App.vue:852-856). The damage is confined to UX: an entire selectable row class drives a shipped detail pane to its empty state, one pane arm plus its handler are dead code, and a toolbar verb issues a command guaranteed to be rejected with a raw backend string. That is a broken feature in a primary pane, which is major.

One addition the auditor's fix omits: switching line 1092 to `allBranches` alone *unblocks* a destructive path. BranchDetailPane.vue:165-177 gates Rename on `:disabled="busy"` and Delete on `:disabled="busy || !canDelete || isCurrent"` — neither consults `remote`. Today the empty pane is the only thing keeping those verbs off a remote ref; with the lookup fixed, the danger Delete button becomes live for `refs/remotes/origin/main` and `deleteBranch` (App.vue:813-816) will confirm on a raw refname and pass it to `branches.remove`. The pane-side `!remote` guard must land in the same change as the toolbar one.

findings.title: The branch pane's Compare button never compares that branch
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:1619 — `@open-compare="goTab('compare')"` carries no ref. Landing on the compare tab runs the watcher at App.vue:461 → seedCompareDefaults (App.vue:448-459), which picks `head = all.find(e => e.isHead)` and `base = head.upstream's remote ref ?? main|master`, i.e. the checked-out branch against its upstream — never the branch the user was reading. If compare already holds a pair from an earlier visit, the watch is skipped entirely (App.vue:450) and the stale pair stays. There is no other path from the branch surface into compare: ComparePane's picker (App.vue:1636 pickCompareRef) is the only other writer.
findings.repro: Branches tab → select local branch `feature` (not the checked-out one) → click 比较 in the detail pane. Repo has `main` tracking `origin/main`.
findings.expected: Compare `feature` against the current branch (or against its upstream), i.e. the two refs the user pointed at.
findings.actual: The compare tab opens on `origin/main` vs `main` (the HEAD pair). If the user had already used Compare once, it opens on the previous pair. Either way the branch the user asked about is not in the comparison.
findings.fix: Give the branch pane a real handler, e.g. `@open-compare="openCompareFor(selectedBranchInfo)"`, which sets `compare.setBoth(toRefChoice(selectedBranchInfo), toRefChoice(headBranch))` (toRefChoice is exported from src/composables/useCompare.ts:37) before `goTab('compare')`; keep seedCompareDefaults for the toolbar/palette entry only.
findings.testIdea: src/App.test.ts — with a branch selected, trigger the detail pane's open-compare emit and assert `compare.left.id === 'refs/heads/feature'`; today it asserts the seeded `origin/main` instead.

notes:
Confirmed by full trace; no guard/default/handler exists that the auditor missed.

Wiring: BranchDetailPane.vue:161 `@click="emit('openCompare')"` with `openCompare: []` (BranchDetailPane.vue:43) carrying no payload; App.vue:1619 `@open-compare="goTab('compare')"` where goTab (App.vue:420-427) only navigates. `grep -rn "openCompare|open-compare" src docs` returns exactly three hits (emit decl, emit call, that one binding), so there is no alternate path.

State writers: only `compare.setBoth` at App.vue:458 (seedCompareDefaults) and `compare.choose` at App.vue:479 (pickCompareRef, wired solely from ComparePane's picker at App.vue:1636). seedCompareDefaults targets `all.find(e => e.isHead)` against head's upstream else main/master, and is gated by `if (compare.left.value !== null || compare.right.value !== null) return;`. `forRepo` (useCompare.ts:166-175) clears left/right only on repo change, so a prior pair survives within the repo and the gate skips seeding entirely. Both outcomes exclude the selected branch.

Refutation attempts that failed: (1) the "Compare…" ellipsis could mean "shortcut into the compare surface", but ComparePane's own picker is `compare.chooseRef: "Choose a ref"` (no ellipsis), the tab bar already exposes Compare, and a pane-local button that only switches tabs carries no information; (2) docs/04-ui-spec.md §S9 specifies the branches pane as owning a base-branch selector ("Compare against:" — our copy), so comparison is meant to be branch-relative; (3) the same pane already has this bug class fixed in `pushSelectedBranch` (App.vue:486-503): "pressing Push while reading another branch's pane pushes the wrong ref — silently… The pane's own branch is the one the user is looking at." Same reasoning, same pane, unrepaired here.

Corrections to the finding: the testIdea targets src/App.test.ts, which does not exist — the suite is src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts (a static fs walk over .vue sources, node env), src/templateCompiles.test.ts, and per-component/per-store files; an App-level behavioural test is new infrastructure and must mock ../bridges/commands (Tauri). Separately, the suggested fix inverts base/target: the file's convention is setBoth(base, target) (line 458, `compare.baseSide` / `compare.compareSide`), so setBoth(selected, head) makes the ahead/behind ribbon read backwards for a feature branch; it also lacks a guard for "no branch selected" and "selected branch is HEAD", where base and target collapse.

Severity stays major: wrong-ref, user-visible, silently misleading about what changed in a branch, recoverable only by hand-picking both sides; not destructive, so not a blocker.

findings.title: Filtering or searching to zero rows renders a blank list with no empty state
findings.evidence: BranchListPane.vue:54-61 computes `filtered` from props, but the ListShell `status` comes from the store (App.vue:1585 `:state="branches.state.value"`), which stores/branches.ts:33 sets to `dataState([...locals, ...remotes])` — the unfiltered set. loadState.ts:14-16 returns 'data' for any non-empty array, and ListShell.vue:50-71 renders the empty arm only when `status === 'empty'`; with 'data' it renders the default slot, i.e. the VirtualList at BranchListPane.vue:117 with `:count="filtered.length"` = 0.
findings.repro: Repo with local branches but no remotes: Branches tab → click the 远程 filter. Or type a string that matches nothing into the search box. (The filter radio is at BranchListPane.vue:86-99, the search at 101-107.)
findings.expected: An empty state saying nothing matches, as docs/04 §1.2 and CLAUDE.md:91-92 require ('Every async list renders the four-state contract … no list may skip a state').
findings.actual: A blank pane under the toolbar: no rows, no message, no way to tell 'no remote branches' from 'still loading' or 'the filter is wrong'.
findings.fix: Derive the shell status from the filtered set, e.g. pass a computed that returns 'empty' when `state.status === 'data' && filtered.length === 0` (with a distinct 'no matches for {needle}' caption), and have BranchListPane compute it from the same `filtered` it renders.
findings.testIdea: src/components/panes/BranchListPane.test.ts — mount with `state = {status:'data',data:[localBranch]}`, `filter='remote'`, and assert the EmptyState (e.g. `wrapper.findComponent(EmptyState).exists()` or the rendered caption text) appears; today the rendered list is empty with no EmptyState.

notes:
CONFIRMED, but severity overstated. Full path re-traced, no guard exists.

Evidence chain in /tmp/meridian-baseline:
1. App.vue:1584-1585 passes `:state="branches.state.value"` and `:branches="branches.allBranches.value"` — the raw unfiltered set.
2. stores/branches.ts:33 sets `state.value = dataState([...locals, ...remotes])`; stores/loadState.ts:15 returns `{status:'data'}` for any non-empty array. A repo with locals and no remotes yields status 'data'.
3. BranchListPane.vue:74 binds ListShell `:status="state.status"` (the store's status). The `filtered` computed (54-61) is consumed ONLY at line 117 as `:count="filtered.length"`. Nothing derives status from it.
4. ListShell.vue:50-71: the EmptyState arm is `v-else-if="status === 'empty'"`; status 'data' falls through to `<slot v-else />`.
5. VirtualList.vue:38-48 + 93: count=0 → offsets=[0] → totalHeight 0px, visible=[] → blank flex:1 scroll container. Nothing renders. Blank pane confirmed.

Refutation attempts, all failed:
- Is search server-side so the store would report 'empty'? No. stores/branches.ts:24 takes a `search` param, but App.vue calls `branches.refresh()` bare at 1343, 1374 and 1602 — the param is never passed. Filtering is purely client-side in BranchListPane.
- Is the local/remote radio backed by a distinct fetch? No. The store hardcodes branchList(repo,"local")/(repo,"remote"); the radio (86-99) only emits update:filter, which rewrites the local `filtered` computed.
- Is blank-on-zero an accepted convention here? Opposite. stores/branches.ts:15-21 carries a comment naming this exact confusion ("indistinguishable from 'this repository has no remotes', which is a different fact and a common one") and fixes only the data half. SettingsScreen.vue:295-302 already solves the render half with noMatchingTitle + nothingMatches {query}. i18n branch.* has no such key in either locale.

Severity corrected major -> minor. The CLAUDE.md:91-92 rule the finding cites governs FETCH states (loading|empty|error|data), and all four do render correctly here — nothing is skipped, so the literal contract is not violated. What is missing is a *filtered* empty state. Consequences: no message, no data loss, no wrong computation, no crash. The toolbar stays visible with the active filter tab highlighted, and SearchField.vue:40 renders a clear button whenever modelValue is non-empty, so the state is inferable and the user is never trapped. That is a UX-completeness gap, not a silent failure.

One inaccuracy in the proposed fix: it would leave `@empty-action="emit('create')"` (BranchListPane.vue:82) active in the no-match case, inviting the user to create a branch they do not need. The action must switch with the state. Also, the empty arm is currently fed branch.emptyTitle/emptyCaption ("No branches" / "Create a branch to start working"), which would be actively wrong text for a filter that matched nothing, so the title/caption must become state-dependent too.

findings.title: Pushing a branch never sets its upstream: the bridge's default overrides the Rust default_true
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:888-894 declares `RemotePublishBranch { ..., #[serde(default = "default_true")] pub set_upstream: bool }` and engine/remotes.rs:974-1005 documents the verb as "git's `push -u`", only calling set_tracking_config `if set_upstream`. But /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/bridges/commands.ts:309-318 defaults `setUpstream = false` and always sends it, and /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useGit.ts:83 calls `commands.remotePublishBranch(id, remote, branch)` without the fourth argument. So the serde default never applies and tracking is never configured. The branch pane's Push (App.vue:1613 → pushSelectedBranch, App.vue:489-500) is the only publisher in this surface.
findings.repro: Create a branch (`⌘⇧B`), commit, then press Push in the branch detail pane. Compare with `git push -u origin <branch>` (verified in /tmp/audit-branch: plain `git push origin topic` leaves `branch.topic.remote` unset).
findings.expected: The remote branch is created AND the local branch is configured to track it, so the pane shows the upstream and the ahead/behind badges work.
findings.actual: The remote ref is created but the local branch stays untracked: BranchDetailPane.vue:94-95 keeps showing 未跟踪任何上游, the tracking facts stay 0/0, and no UI can fix it — branch_set_upstream/branch_unset_upstream exist in Rust (commands/refs.rs:261-321) but have no caller in src/ (grep for branchSetUpstream returns nothing), and pushOptions is never supplied (App.vue:1606-1621 passes no `:push-options`), so SplitAction renders no options caret at all (SplitAction.vue:64).
findings.fix: Either default `setUpstream` to true in src/bridges/commands.ts:313 (matching the Rust default and the command's own doc), or pass `true` from useGit.push for a branch that has no upstream, and expose branch_set_upstream as a push option so a mis-published branch can be repaired.
findings.testIdea: src/composables/useGit.test.ts — mock `remotePublishBranch` and assert `git.push('feature')` calls it with `setUpstream === true`; today it asserts/observes `false`.

notes:
CONFIRMED after line-by-line retrace; no guard, default, or handler rescues it.

Chain: src/bridges/commands.ts:309-318 defaults setUpstream=false AND always includes it in the payload (args:{repo,remote,branch,setUpstream}) via a raw @tauri-apps/api/core invoke with no arg filtering. src/composables/useGit.ts:75-84 calls it with 3 args. src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:892-893 declares #[serde(default = "default_true")] pub set_upstream: bool — serde `default` only fills a MISSING field, so the Rust default is unreachable from this caller and is dead code. engine/remotes.rs:1002-1005 calls set_tracking_config only when set_upstream, so branch.<name>.remote/.merge are never written.

All three UI entry points funnel through useGit.push: App.vue:672 (toolbar), App.vue:1022 (commit-and-push), App.vue:497 invoked from App.vue:1613-1614 (branch pane). useGit's run() only refreshes stores on success; no post-push tracking fixup exists.

Impact verified at engine/branches.rs:756-775: branch.upstream() fails, upstream=None and (ahead,behind)=(0,0) with no fallback to refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch> — so the Upstream fact (BranchDetailPane.vue:93-95) and the ahead/behind badges (App.vue:259-260) are dead for every app-created branch.

No repair path: branch_set_upstream/branch_unset_upstream are registered (lib.rs:125-126) but grep finds zero callers in src/; the sibling remote_push command (refs.rs:780-803), which does honor set_upstream: Option<String>, is not bridged in commands.ts at all; pushOptions is undefined (BranchDetailPane.vue:28,30,146) and App.vue passes none, so SplitAction.vue:64's caret never renders.

Intent corroborated twice: docs/03-command-surface.md:250 specifies `remote_publish_branch | repo, branch, remote, opts{set_upstream} | PublishReport | push + set upstream`, and remotes.rs:974-975 documents it as git's `push -u`.

Checked and NOT broken, so I did not inflate impact: pull still works (remotes.rs:587-588 falls back to refs/remotes/{name}/{branch}); delete uses HEAD reachability like git's own -d (branches.rs:375, 407-415); force-push unaffected.

Two citation slips, neither refuting: the pane string is `未设置上游` (zh-CN/panes.ts:195), not `未跟踪任何上游`; and src/composables/useGit.test.ts does not exist (only interactionCompleteness, templateCompiles, AboutScreen, changelog, i18n catalog, stores/loadState), so the claim "today it asserts/observes false" is unsupported — the test must be created.

Severity major stands: push and pull both succeed (no data loss, not a blocker), but every app-created branch permanently loses tracking metadata, two visible affordances die for those branches, and recovery requires leaving the app for the git CLI.

findings.title: Every branch failure shows the raw English engine message; the localised errorText catalogue is never called
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/i18n/index.ts:149-168 exports `errorText(payload)` which maps `errors.byCode.<code>` through params, with the comment 'The backend does not localise. ErrorPayload.message is an English sentence … treated here as a developer-facing fallback only'. The catalogue exists and covers exactly the codes the branch surface produces — src/i18n/locales/zh-CN.ts:158-172 has reference_not_found, reference_exists, checkout_conflicts, operation_in_progress, invalid_reference_name, unknown_revision, checkout_failed, invalid_request. But `errorText` has zero callers (grep -rn errorText src/ returns only its definition), and the branch paths use the raw message: App.vue:548-554 `reportError` reads `error.message` directly, and App.vue:583 puts `error.message` into the activity list. The Rust messages are English: validation/branches.rs:76-80 ('Branch \'{name}\' does not exist'), 82-85 ('Already on \'{name}\''), commands/refs.rs:1797 ('Branch \'{name}\' does not exist'), 1878 ('Not fully merged: …'), engine/branches.rs:574 ('Remote branch … does not exist — fetch first'), 589 ('Branch \'{name}\' already exists').
findings.repro: Set the app to 简体中文 (the default), then trigger any failing branch verb — e.g. the 全部 filter → double-click `origin/main` when a local `main` exists (BR-02), or the sidebar ⋯ on the branch you are already on (branch_checkout refuses with 'Already on \'main\'').
findings.expected: A Chinese sentence from the catalogue, e.g. '「main」已存在。' for reference_exists or '该仓库还有另一个操作正在进行中。' for operation_in_progress.
findings.actual: The English Rust sentence is shown verbatim in a danger toast ('Branch \'main\' already exists'), and the same string is recorded in the activity list. errors.title/detail/retryable/copyCode (zh-CN.ts) are likewise unused, so no localised error surface exists anywhere.
findings.fix: Route both call sites through the catalogue: `reportError` should render `errorText({ code, message, params })` (importing from src/i18n) and runVerb should pass the same string to activity.finish; keep `error.message` only as the last-resort fallback that errorText already implements.
findings.testIdea: src/i18n/errorText.test.ts (or an App-level test) — assert that a toast produced from `{code:'reference_exists', message:"Branch 'main' already exists", params:{name:'main'}}` under locale zh-CN equals '「main」已存在。' and contains no ASCII 'Branch'; today it renders the English message.

notes:
CONFIRMED. I attempted to refute and could not; every link in the chain verifies by direct read.

(1) Dead function: `errorText` at src/i18n/index.ts:159-168 is real and correctly typed against `ErrorCode` (`const key = \`errors.byCode.${payload.code}\``, falling back to `payload.message` when vue-i18n echoes the key back). `grep -rn errorText src/` returns exactly one hit — its own definition. Zero callers. No `errorText.test.ts` exists, confirming the auditor's proposed test file is genuinely absent.

(2) Raw message at both named call sites: App.vue:548-554 `reportError` duck-types with `"message" in error` and reads ONLY `.message`, then pushes it verbatim. This is the mechanism that makes the localisation unreachable — `code` and `params` are present on the object but discarded. App.vue:583 `runVerb` does `activity.finish(id, "failed", error.message)`.

(3) No downstream rescue layer — this was my primary refutation hypothesis and it fails. `pushToast` (src/layout/useShell.ts:85-88) stores `text` verbatim into the queue, and ToastHost.vue:31 renders `{{ toast.text }}` with no `t()` call. The locale file even documents this design: `src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/shell.ts:62` — "提示正文与操作按钮由调用方 pushToast 时决定，组件只负责给这个关闭" (the toast body is decided by the caller at pushToast time). So localisation was architecturally assigned to the caller, and the caller does not do it.

(4) Data needed is present: `ErrorPayload` (src/bridges/bindings.ts:31-38) carries `code`, `message`, `params`, `retryable`, `domain`. `stores/branches.ts:55/67/83/95/107` assign `lastError.value = error as ErrorPayload` — the raw payload passes through the store untouched. Rust populates params: engine/branches.rs:588-591 returns `ErrorCode::ReferenceExists` with `format!("Branch '{name}' already exists")` AND `.with_param("name", name)`, so `errorText` would interpolate to 「main」已存在。 correctly.

(5) Rust side is genuinely English: validation/branches.rs:76-80, 82-85 ("Already on '{name}'"), commands/refs.rs:1819, engine/branches.rs:574, 589.

(6) Catalogue covers the surface: zh-CN.ts:158-172 has reference_not_found, reference_exists, checkout_conflicts, operation_in_progress, invalid_reference_name, unknown_revision, checkout_failed, invalid_request — matching what the branch verbs emit.

(7) Default locale is zh-CN: index.ts:27 `DEFAULT_LOCALE: Locale = "zh-CN"`.

(8) Repro is live, not blocked: App.vue:855-867 — when `branch?.isRemote === true` it calls `branches.checkoutRemote(branch.fullName)` with NO local-branch-exists guard, reaching engine/branches.rs:589 ReferenceExists. The alternate repro (checkout on the current branch → validation/branches.rs:82-85) is equally unguarded.

(9) Not deliberate: no test asserts English error passthrough anywhere; the only test hits on those strings are unrelated.

EVIDENCE CORRECTIONS (neither refutes the finding):
- The claim "errors.title/detail/retryable/copyCode are likewise unused" is wrong about `errors.title` — it IS used at src/components/screens/AboutScreen.vue:217 as an EmptyState `:title`. Only `errors.detail`, `errors.retryable` and `errors.copyCode` are genuinely dead.
- The auditor found two unlocalised surfaces; there are THREE. AboutScreen.vue:218 renders `:caption="info.error.message"` — a raw English ErrorPayload.message (sibling fixture AboutScreen.test.ts:117 confirms shape `{ code: "io", message: "timeout", retryable: true, domain: "fs" }`). The title beside it is localised; the caption under it is not.

SEVERITY: major stands. Not a blocker (no data loss, crash, or security impact, and the failure mode is graceful — the user still learns what went wrong). But it violates the product's own documented primary constraint (Chinese by default, src/i18n/index.ts:2-11), reproduces on EVERY failing branch verb rather than an edge case, and breaks the invariant the module states about itself at index.ts:14-15: "every code has an entry in errors.byCode, so the fallback should never be seen" — that invariant is false in practice.

Minor catalogue-quality note (not a refutation): `invalid_request` maps to the generic "Meridian 拒绝了这个请求。", so the "Already on 'main'" case would localise to a vague string that drops the branch name. A dedicated code (e.g. `already_on_branch`) would be needed to localise that case meaningfully.

findings.title: branch_delete's DeleteReport is discarded, so a skipped deletion is reported as a successful one
findings.evidence: engine/branches.rs:344-389 returns `DeleteReport { deleted, skipped }` and never errors on a skip: a branch that no longer exists lands in `skipped` with class 'reference_not_found' (357-364), the checked-out branch with 'branch_is_head' (366-373), an unmerged one with 'delete_unmerged_branch' (375-382). The type's own doc (engine/branches.rs:27-29) says branches that vanished between the UI's snapshot and the command 'land in skipped … instead of failing the whole batch'. The bridge types the result as `invoke<unknown>` (commands.ts:180-187), stores/branches.ts:100-110 discards it and returns `true` whenever the invoke resolves, and App.vue:827-828 then toasts success. The validator only catches the unmerged case (commands/refs.rs:1865-1882), and its unmerged() helper deliberately skips names that no longer resolve (engine/branches.rs:393-404), so the not-found path always reaches execute.
findings.repro: Branches tab → select branch `topic` (fully merged, not checked out) so the detail pane shows it. In a terminal in the same repo run `git branch -D topic` (no refsChanged event is emitted for out-of-app changes — only in-app commands emit, useAppEvents.ts:30-35). Back in Meridian press 删除 and confirm.
findings.expected: Either an error explaining that the branch no longer exists, or at minimum no success claim.
findings.actual: Toast '已删除分支 topic' although nothing was deleted; the only visible change is that the row disappears on the next refresh. The skip reason never reaches the user, and `skipped` is never inspected anywhere in the frontend.
findings.fix: Have stores/branches.ts:100-110 return the DeleteReport (or a boolean derived from `report.deleted.length > 0`) and let deleteBranch (App.vue:827-829) branch on it, surfacing `report.skipped[0].reason`/class through the error catalogue; the Rust side already computes both.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/branches.test.ts — mock `branchDelete` to resolve `{deleted: [], skipped: [{name:'topic', reason:"Branch 'topic' does not exist", class:'reference_not_found'}]}` and assert `remove()` resolves false / the caller does not toast success; today it resolves true.

notes:
Confirmed end-to-end; no guard anywhere in the chain. engine/branches.rs:344-389 `delete()` only `?`-propagates from `is_merged`/`branch.delete()`; every "cannot delete" condition is pushed into `report.skipped` and it returns `Ok`. commands/refs.rs:215-234: `BranchDelete::validate` is only `validate_unmerged_delete`, `execute` returns the report unchanged. state.rs:57-101 `AppState::run` is the documented 7 steps with step 4 ("policy hooks") still a comment, so `Risk::Destructive` gates nothing and nothing inspects `C::Output`. The bridge (commands.ts:179-186) types it `invoke<unknown>` and `invoke` is imported raw from `@tauri-apps/api/core` at commands.ts:10 — there is no wrapper in src/ that could turn a skip into a rejection. stores/branches.ts:100-110 discards the resolved value and returns `true`; the `refresh()` it calls swallows its own errors into `state` (lines 23-35) so it cannot fail the call either. App.vue:812-829 toasts success on `ok`. `grep -rn "skipped" src/` returns only two unrelated hits and bindings.ts has no DeleteReport type, so nothing in the frontend reads the report. useAppEvents.ts:12-13 ("Stores never poll") plus a setInterval grep across App.vue/stores/composables confirms the repro precondition: an out-of-band `git branch -D` leaves a stale, selectable row.

Two corrections to the evidence, neither of which rescues the code: (1) the `delete_unmerged_branch` skip arm is unreachable via the command — `validate_unmerged_delete` (refs.rs:1865-1882) rejects non-forced unmerged deletes, and with `force=true` the engine's `!force` guard is false so it deletes; that arm only fires for a direct engine caller, so the finding lists three reachable skips where there is one. (2) `branch_is_head` is UI-guarded: BranchDetailPane.vue:171-177 renders the button `:disabled="busy || !canDelete || isCurrent"`, and BranchListPane declares a `delete` emit but never fires it.

Severity corrected major -> minor. The only reachable arm is `reference_not_found`, which needs an out-of-band git operation or a stale pane between snapshot and click; nothing is deleted or over-deleted; the branch was already gone, so the resulting state matches the user's intent and the row vanishes on the next refresh regardless. The residual harm is one misleading success toast on a destructive verb — a UX correctness defect, not a silent failure with consequences.

findings.title: can-delete is hard-coded true, so the protected-branch guard and its reason string are unreachable and the default branch is deletable
findings.evidence: App.vue:1609 passes `:can-delete="true"` to BranchDetailPane, whose prop is documented 'Disables the destructive verbs (protected/current branch)' (BranchDetailPane.vue:26) and whose `deleteReason` computed returns t('branch.reasonProtected') only when `!props.canDelete` (BranchDetailPane.vue:57-62) — a branch that can never be taken. The Delete button is therefore disabled only for the current branch (BranchDetailPane.vue:169-178), and the confirm dialogue (App.vue:816-824) shows only the branch name with no default-branch warning. deleteBranch calls `branches.remove(branch?.name ?? name)` with the store's default `force = false` (stores/branches.ts:100, commands.ts:180-187), so unmerged branches are still refused by validate_unmerged_delete.
findings.repro: Repo with `main` merged into `feature`. Check out `feature`, select `main` in the Branches tab, press 删除, confirm. Verified with git in /tmp/audit-branch: while on `feature`, `git branch -d main` succeeds ('已删除分支 main').
findings.expected: The default/protected branch is not deletable from the UI (which is what the canDelete prop and the 此分支受保护。 string were built for), or at least the confirm dialogue warns that this is the default branch and that there is no undo.
findings.actual: main is deleted after the ordinary confirm. Snapshots/undo are explicitly not implemented in this tree (CLAUDE.md:113-121), so the UI offers no way back; afterwards selectedBranchInfo becomes null and the pane falls to its empty state.
findings.fix: Pass a real value, e.g. `:can-delete="!isDefaultBranch(selectedBranchInfo)"` computed from the repository's default/HEAD branch (or a configured protected list), and add the default-branch warning to the confirm dialogue message.
findings.testIdea: src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.test.ts — mount with `branch = {name:'main', isHead:false}` and `canDelete = false`, assert the delete button is disabled and its title is the protected reason; plus an App-level test asserting the pane receives canDelete=false for main.

notes:
Traced the whole path and could not find a guard the auditor missed, so the mechanical claim is CONFIRMED: App.vue:1609 passes the literal `:can-delete="true"` (only occurrence of that prop in the file); BranchDetailPane.vue:26 documents the prop as covering "protected/current branch" but line 30 defaults it true, so `deleteReason`'s `t("branch.reasonProtected")` branch (lines 57-62) is unreachable and the zh-CN/en strings (panes.ts:210/213) are rendered nowhere. The button's effective guard is `busy || !canDelete || isCurrent` (BranchDetailPane.vue:172), so the checked-out branch is the only thing blocked. The list-pane path is inert anyway: BranchListPane never emits `delete` (its template only emits refresh/create/update/select/activate/contextmenu) and App binds `@contextmenu="() => {}"`. useBranches.ts:67-71 calls store.remove(id,[name]) leaving force=false, so validate_unmerged_delete (refs.rs:1863-1886) is the only backend gate; I reproduced git's behavior in a scratch repo — on `feature` with `main` merged, `git branch -d main` exits 0. No default/protected-branch concept exists anywhere: RepoInfo (bindings.ts:70-80) and BranchInfo (158-169) carry no such flag, and grep -i protect in src/ and src-tauri/src/ hits only git-config protection in commands/repository.rs plus the doc comment.

However three supporting claims are wrong or overstated, so severity should NOT rise: (1) "the confirm dialogue shows only the branch name" is false — App.vue:820 renders `deleteBranchMessage` = "删除 {branch}？此操作无法撤销。" / "Delete {branch}? This cannot be undone." (i18n .../zh-CN/diff.ts:249, en/diff.ts:268), i.e. the "no undo" warning the finding asks for already ships; (2) "the UI offers no way back" is overstated — with force hard-coded false, branches::unmerged (engine/branches.rs:392-407) refuses any tip not reachable from HEAD, so the oid shown in the pane is still reachable from the current branch and `git branch main <oid>` restores it; a ref pointer is lost, not commits; (3) the proposed fix cannot compile — `isDefaultBranch()` has nothing to read, and in a remote-less repo no default branch exists to infer.

The tree's own contract agrees with git: docs/03-command-surface.md:195 defines branch_delete's precondition as "merged or upstream gone or force" — protected-branch protection is deliberately outside the command surface, and CLAUDE.md:113-121 states policies are specified but not present in this P0 skeleton. So the real residue is a UX/safety footgun versus sibling tools (GitHub Desktop refuses to delete the default branch) plus genuinely dead plumbing — not data loss, not a spec violation. Correct severity remains minor.

findings.title: No in-flight guard on the branch verbs: a second click re-issues the command and produces a spurious error
findings.evidence: BranchDetailPane declares `busy` with default false (BranchDetailPane.vue:27, 30) and uses it to disable Checkout/Merge/Rebase/Push/Pull/Rename/Delete (BranchDetailPane.vue:119, 131, 135, 145, 150, 165, 172), but App.vue:1606-1621 never passes `:busy` — and could not, because the store calls it wraps have no busy flag: stores/branches.ts has no such state, and useGit's `busy` (useGit.ts:26, 39, 49, 55) is returned but read nowhere in App.vue. So `busy` is permanently false and every verb stays enabled while a command is queued.
findings.repro: On a large repository, click Checkout in the branch detail pane and immediately click the same branch's row again and double-click it (or click Checkout twice). Both calls reach branch_checkout.
findings.expected: The second click is a no-op because the verb is in flight.
findings.actual: The second call fails validation in validate_checkout (validation/branches.rs:81-86) with 'Already on \'feature\'' — an English danger toast right after a successful checkout, which reads as 'your checkout failed'.
findings.fix: Expose a per-verb busy flag (e.g. a `busy` ref in stores/branches.ts set around checkout/create/rename/remove) and pass it as `:busy` to BranchDetailPane, and/or gate checkoutFlow on it; then have the engine's 'already on' case be treated as a no-op success rather than an error.
findings.testIdea: src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.test.ts — mount with `busy = true` and assert every verb button has the `disabled` attribute; and a store test asserting two overlapping `checkout()` calls issue only one `branchCheckout` invoke.

notes:
CONFIRMED. I re-traced every hop and could not find the guard the auditor was supposed to have missed.

1) The dead prop is real. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.vue:27 declares `busy?: boolean`, line 30 defaults it to `false`, and it gates all seven verbs at 119 (checkout), 131 (merge), 135 (rebase), 145 (SplitAction push), 150 (pull), 165 (rename), 172 (delete). /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/common/SplitAction.vue:37 honors it too (`if (props.disabled || props.busy) return;`). Every line number in the evidence is exact.

2) Nothing ever sets it. `grep -rn BranchDetailPane src/` returns exactly two hits: the import at App.vue:51 and the single call site at App.vue:1606-1621. That block passes `:branch`, `:current-branch`, `:can-delete` and thirteen listeners — no `:busy`. So the prop is permanently false.

3) No substitute exists upstream. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts (read in full, 125 lines) exposes only state/branches/remoteBranches/allBranches/lastError/refresh/create/checkout/checkoutRemote/rename/remove — no in-flight flag. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useGit.ts:26,39,49,55 does have a `busy` ref, but `git.busy` is read nowhere in App.vue; the grep for `busy` in App.vue yields only line 651 (activitySummary, a toolbar-chip computed), 1439 (repositories.busy), 1487 (committing), 1634 (compare.busy), 1726 (feedbackBusy), 1755 (literal false). None of them reaches BranchDetailPane.

4) The near-miss I chased, and why it does not help. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/state.rs:65 does `self.queue.enqueue(&repo_id).await` before every command, which looks like a guard. But /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/queue.rs:27-36 is a bare `tokio::sync::Mutex` — it SERIALIZES, it does not DEDUPLICATE, and its own doc comment says so ("Mutating commands await their repository's turn... Read-only loads bypass the queue"). The second branch_checkout waits its turn and then executes anyway. That makes the bug deterministic rather than racy: by the time it runs, branch.is_head() is true, so /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/validation/branches.rs:81-86 returns `ErrorCode::InvalidRequest, "Already on '{name}'"`. That propagates through the store's catch into `lastError`, then reportError (App.vue:548-554) pushes `{ kind: "danger", text: error.message }` — the raw, untranslated English string, in an app that i18n's every other string.

5) Reachability confirmed. confirmDirtyCheckout returns true immediately on a clean tree (App.vue:882, `if (workingCopyTotal.value === 0) return true;`), so no dialogue gates the second click. The Checkout button's visibility is `v-if="!isCurrent"`, where isCurrent derives from `branch.isHead` — which only updates after the awaited `refresh(repo)` inside `branches.checkout`. During the in-flight window the button is still rendered and enabled, so an ordinary double-click fires emit('checkout') twice and both reach branch_checkout.

Severity `minor` is correct as filed: the queue prevents concurrent ref mutation, the branch really is checked out, and there is no data loss — the damage is a misleading danger toast that reads as "your checkout failed" immediately after a successful checkout, in an otherwise fully-localized UI. Not a blocker or major.

Two corrections to the filed fix, which is why I am not simply rubber-stamping it:
(a) It proposes also making the engine treat "already on" as a no-op success. That is the wrong layer. validate_checkout is a correctness guard for the command layer; a CLI or headless caller legitimately needs to know the ref was not switched. Silently promoting a refused command to success to absorb a UI double-click weakens the engine for every other caller.
(b) It under-specifies where the guard goes. Passing `:busy` fixes only one of six entry points into checkoutFlow — App.vue:1610 (the pane button). The row `@dblclick` at 1592, the row verb menu at 1595, the toolbar option at 703, the command palette at 1333/1339, and row options at 1422 all bypass BranchDetailPane entirely and would still double-fire. A store-level or flow-level guard is load-bearing; the prop alone is cosmetic.

Minor evidence note, not affecting the verdict: the repro's "double-click the row" phrasing is imprecise — a single dblclick gesture emits `activate` once (/tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/panes/BranchListPane.vue:125), so that path needs two separate gestures. The "click Checkout twice" variant it offers as the alternative is the clean and correct repro.

findings.title: Merge/Rebase are offered for the branch you are already on and report success for a no-op
findings.evidence: BranchDetailPane.vue:130-139 renders Merge into {currentBranch} and Rebase onto for every non-remote branch, including the checked-out one (only the Checkout button is hidden when isCurrent, BranchDetailPane.vue:115-128). App.vue:1611-1612 forwards them to mergeBranch/rebaseBranch (App.vue:800-809) → useGit.merge/rebase (useGit.ts:86-89) → merge_start/rebase_start with the branch name. A self-merge is analysed as up-to-date by engine/merge.rs:412-417 (IntegrationOutcome::UpToDate), and a self-rebase likewise (engine/rebase.rs:637-643), which returns Ok; runVerb (App.vue:575-589) treats any Ok as success and toasts '已合并 {branch}' / '已变基 {branch}'. The label is also wrong in this state: with the current branch selected, mergeLabel (BranchDetailPane.vue:51-55) reads '合并到 main' while the operation is `git merge main` from main.
findings.repro: Branches tab → select the branch you are currently on → press 合并到 main (or 变基到 main).
findings.expected: The verb is hidden or disabled for the current branch, or the toast says nothing needed doing.
findings.actual: The toast claims the merge/rebase happened; no ref moved. (git itself exits 0 with '已经是最新的。' here — verified in /tmp/audit-branch — but a GUI that reports '已合并 main' for a no-op is claiming work it did not do.)
findings.fix: Hide/disable the merge and rebase buttons when `isHead` (BranchDetailPane.vue:130-139), and/or map IntegrationOutcome::UpToDate to an informational toast ('已是最新') rather than the success string in App.vue:802/808.
findings.testIdea: src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.test.ts — mount with `branch = {name:'main', isHead:true}` and assert the merge and rebase buttons are absent or disabled; today both render enabled.

notes:
CONFIRMED — I re-traced all seven hops and found no guard, default, or handler the auditor missed.

1. Render (`/tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.vue:130-139`). The merge/rebase buttons sit inside `<template v-if="!remote">` — the *only* predicate is `isRemote`. The sibling checkout button three lines up is guarded `v-if="!isCurrent"` (:115-116) and delete is guarded `:disabled="busy || !canDelete || isCurrent"` (:172), so the component demonstrably has `isCurrent` in hand and simply does not apply it to the two integration verbs. `isCurrent` = `props.branch?.isHead` (:48), and `isHead` is genuinely populated by the engine (`src-tauri/src/engine/branches.rs:782`, `is_head: branch.is_head()`), so the flag is correct — it is just unused here.

2. Reachability is real. `BranchListPane.vue:63-64,121,134` renders the HEAD branch as an ordinary selectable row (`isCurrent` only adds a `.head` class and a dot), and `App.vue:1089-1093` `selectedBranchInfo` resolves it by `fullName` with no head exclusion. So the repro path — Branches tab → click the branch you are on — does land on a pane rendering both verbs enabled.

3. Forwarding (`App.vue:1611-1612`) passes `selectedBranchInfo?.name ?? selectedBranchName` straight into `mergeBranch`/`rebaseBranch`. `App.vue:800-809` guard only on falsy `name`; there is no `name === head` comparison, and `selectedRepo?.headBranch` is in scope right there (it is bound to `:current-branch` at :1609).

4. `useGit.ts:86-89` passes the name to `commands.mergeStart`/`rebaseStart` unchanged. Critically, `run()` (:36-51) does `await action(id); … return null` — it **discards the returned `IntegrationResult`**. Grepping the frontend, `IntegrationResult` appears only in `bindings.ts:532`; nothing anywhere in `src/` reads `outcome`. So the engine's `upToDate` verdict is computed, shipped over the IPC boundary, and thrown away.

5. `runVerb` (`App.vue:575-589`) treats `error === null` as success unconditionally and pushes `t("shell.toast.merged", …)`. The actual strings are `"已合并 {branch}。"` (`src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:279`) and `"已变基到 {branch}。"` (:280), English `"Merged {branch}."` / `"Rebased onto {branch}."` (`en/diff.ts:299-300`). An unqualified past-tense success claim for work that did not occur.

6. Engine self-merge (`engine/merge.rs:412-417`): `repo.merge_analysis(&[&annotated])` where `annotated` resolves to HEAD's own commit → `is_up_to_date()` → `Ok(IntegrationResult::new(IntegrationOutcome::UpToDate { … }))`. Preceded only by `is_bare()` and `integration_in_progress()` guards.

7. Engine self-rebase (`engine/rebase.rs`): `plan()` (:465-490) computes `range_commits(head, upstream_commit)` with upstream == head → empty vector → empty `steps`; the execute path then hits `if steps.is_empty()` at :637, `merge_base(onto, original_head) == onto` is trivially true for a self-rebase, and it returns `Ok(UpToDate)`. Same shape as the merge path.

The dispatch layer adds no backstop either: `MergeStart::validate` is only `require_no_integration(cx)` (`commands/integrate.rs:117-129`), which rejects a *concurrent* integration, not a self one.

Severity stays minor, and I checked the case for raising it. Nothing is destroyed or mis-stated in the repository — git itself exits 0 with "已经是最新的。" for this exact operation, so the engine's `Ok` is git-faithful, and the end state after the click is identical to the end state before it. The damage is confined to two things: a button that does nothing while claiming otherwise, and a mislabelled verb. It is worth noting the codebase takes its own UI-honesty principle seriously enough to comment on it (App.vue:487-489 calls pushing the wrong ref "the worst kind of quiet wrongness"), which is why this is a legitimate report rather than nitpicking — but a false toast over a no-op that the underlying VCS agrees was a no-op does not reach major.

One correction to the report's framing: the self-merge is not the most common way to hit this. The same discard-the-outcome bug fires whenever a user merges or rebases a *different* branch that is already up to date — an ordinary, common action. That broader path is a stronger argument for the outcome-propagation fix than the `isHead` guard is.

findings.title: The branch selection survives a repository switch
findings.evidence: `selectedBranchName` (App.vue:1085) is only written by the sidebar/row handlers (App.vue:413) and by renameBranchFlow (App.vue:792) — there is no watch on activeRepoId/repos.selectedId that clears it, unlike the compare tab which explicitly calls `compare.forRepo(id)` for exactly this reason ('Compare is repository-scoped: it must not answer for the previous repo', App.vue:519-524; useCompare.ts:167-173 nulls left/right). `selectedBranchInfo` then re-resolves that name inside the NEW repository's branch list (App.vue:1089-1094), and the row highlight is driven by the same string (BranchListPane.vue:121-123).
findings.repro: Repo A: Branches tab → select `main`. Switch to repo B (sidebar repo switcher / ⌘K) which also has `main`, and open its Branches tab. Variant: repo B has no `main`.
findings.expected: No branch is selected in B until the user picks one; the detail pane shows its empty state and the list shows no highlighted row.
findings.actual: Repo B's `main` appears selected — its oid/tip/ahead-behind in the detail pane are B's, not the branch the user chose — and its Checkout/Rename/Delete are one click away in a repository the user never selected them in. In the variant, the list shows no highlighted row while the detail pane still says 未选择分支, so the two columns disagree about what is selected.
findings.fix: Watch the active repository (or `branches.branches`) in App.vue and reset `selectedBranchName.value = null` when it changes, mirroring the `compare.forRepo` call at App.vue:520-524.
findings.testIdea: src/App.test.ts — set selectedBranchName to 'refs/heads/main' with repo A active, switch `repos.selectedId` to B, and assert `selectedBranchInfo` is null until a new selection is made; today it resolves to B's main.

notes:
Confirmed on the primary repro. `selectedBranchName` (App.vue:1085) is written only at App.vue:413 (sidebar branch row), App.vue:792 (renameBranchFlow) and App.vue:1591 (list @select). App.vue is mounted once in src/main.ts and routing is a hash-change ref in src/router/index.ts, so nothing remounts and nothing resets the ref on a repository switch — there is no watch on activeRepoId or repos.selectedId touching it. `selectedBranchInfo` (App.vue:1089-1094) re-resolves that same string against `branches.branches.value`, which useBranches.ts:19-26 refreshes for the newly selected repo, so in repo B it resolves to B's branch with the matching fullName. The row highlight is driven by the same string (BranchListPane.vue:121-123). The codebase itself states the invariant the branches tab misses: App.vue:519-524 watches activeRepoId and calls `compare.forRepo`, which nulls left/right/comparison (useCompare.ts:167-176). Both entry points reach the bug — sidebar RepoSwitcher -> openRepository (App.vue:1418) and the Cmd-K palette `repo:` item -> onPaletteSelect (App.vue:1332) — and both navigate to repositoryPath(id) with no tab query, so the user must click Branches to see the stale pane, exactly as the repro states.

One correction: the variant "repo B has no main" is not a defect. There selectedBranchInfo is null AND no row matches fullName === selectedName, so the detail pane shows 未选择分支 and the list shows no highlight — that is precisely the expected state, and the finding's own claim that "the two columns disagree" contradicts the behaviour it just described. Only the both-repos-have-main case is a real defect.

Severity minor is right, and I would not raise it. The detail pane renders repo B's real branch with B's own oid/tip/ahead-behind, so no cross-repo data is mislabelled — the user's complaint is "why is something already selected", not "this is the wrong repository's data". deleteBranch (App.vue:812-830) and renameBranchFlow (App.vue:770-797) both gate behind a dialogue that names the branch. The only unguarded verb is Checkout, because confirmDirtyCheckout returns true immediately on a clean tree (App.vue:882) — one click switches branches in a repo where the user selected nothing. That is misleading-selection-plus-one-armed-verb, not corruption, so minor is correct.

findings.title: The 'fully merged' badge reads a field no producer ever sets
findings.evidence: BranchListPane.vue:155-159 renders a muted checkmark RowBadge when `filtered[index].fullyMerged`, and BranchDetailPane.vue:80 renders a 'Merged' badge from the same field; contracts.ts:497-500 declares `BranchReviewInfo extends BranchInfo { fullyMerged?: boolean; lastAuthor?: string }`. But the engine's BranchInfo (src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs:16-28) has no such field and engine/branches.rs:747-790 (branch_info) never computes it, even though the merged predicate already exists as engine/branches.rs:407-416 (`is_merged`, used by delete). docs/03-command-surface.md:187 lists `fully_merged` in branch_list's output. App.vue:1093 additionally strips both fields (`{ ...branch, fullyMerged: undefined, lastAuthor: undefined }`) before handing the object to the detail pane, so even a producer would not reach the pane.
findings.repro: Make any branch fully merged into HEAD (e.g. `main` after merging it into `feature`) and look at the Branches list and the branch detail pane.
findings.expected: A merged indicator on the row and in the detail header, per the icon set (icon-set.ts:388 'badge.fullyMerged') and docs/03 §6.
findings.actual: Neither badge can ever appear; the RowBadge and the whole `lastAuthor` fact row (BranchDetailPane.vue:97-100) are dead UI.
findings.fix: Populate `fully_merged` in engine/branches.rs branch_info (reuse is_merged for the local case) and add it to BranchInfo; drop the stripping at App.vue:1093 (or keep it only for fields the engine genuinely does not produce).
findings.testIdea: src-tauri unit test on engine::branches::list asserting the row for a merged branch has fully_merged == true; frontend BranchListPane.test.ts mounting a branch with `fullyMerged: true` and asserting the badge renders.

notes: Confirmed by full re-trace; no guard or producer was missed. Producer: src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs:16-28 declares BranchInfo with exactly ten fields (name, full_name, oid, is_head, is_remote, upstream, ahead, behind, tip_summary, tip_time) under rename_all=camelCase and no serde(flatten); engine/branches.rs:747-789 branch_info() is the only constructor and fills all ten; commands/branches.rs:144 branch_list returns it verbatim. The merged predicate does exist at engine/branches.rs:407-416 (is_merged) but its only callers are lines 375 and 399, both in the delete flow — the list path never touches it, and graph_descendant_of appears at branches.rs only inside is_merged and in the fast-forward ancestor check at :467. Bridge/store add nothing: bindings.ts:158-169 mirrors the ten fields, commands.ts:134-139 is a bare invoke, stores/branches.ts:24-39 only splits and concatenates. Consumer side confirmed dead: a repo-wide grep for fullyMerged returns six hits — contracts.ts:498 (declaration), BranchListPane.vue:156 and BranchDetailPane.vue:80 (the two v-if reads), icon-set.ts:388 (unused entry), App.vue:1093 (the only assignment, setting undefined). No frontend producer, no test sets the field. Two corrections that do not change the verdict: (1) the App.vue:1093 strip guards only the detail pane path — BranchListPane is fed branches.allBranches.value at App.vue:1584 straight from the store, unswiped, so an engine-side fully_merged would make the list-row badge appear on next reload while the detail header badge and lastAuthor row stayed dead; (2) lastAuthor is a strictly larger gap than fullyMerged, since no author field exists anywhere in BranchInfo and last_author appears nowhere in src-tauri, so it is not the same one-line fix. Severity stays minor: no crash, no incorrect output, no data loss — a badge and a fact row that can never render. It is a real bug rather than aspirational scaffolding only because docs/03-command-surface.md:187 asserts fully_merged inside branch_list's return shape, a genuine contract divergence; note also that :203 gives the concept's documented home as branch_review_load, whose ReviewModel{rows[], fully_merged[]} is computed relative to a base ref via CheckRevisionIsAncestorOfRevision — a different predicate from is_merged's tip-reachable-from-HEAD, so is_merged is a defensible cheap approximation but not the documented review semantics.

findings.title: The branch search box never reaches the engine: branch_list's search argument is dead
findings.evidence: App.vue:1087 keeps `branchSearch` as a shell ref and binds it to the pane (App.vue:1589/1601); the only writer of the store's search argument is useBranches' own `search` ref (useBranches.ts:11), refreshed by the watcher at useBranches.ts:27-30 — but nothing ever assigns to `branches.search`, so every refresh sends `search: undefined` (useBranches.ts:34, commands.ts:134-140 → branch_list's `search: Option<String>`, commands/branches.rs:38-46, which would do the filtering engine-side). The pane therefore filters the full list client-side (BranchListPane.vue:54-61). Note also that the store's own refresh calls inside create/checkout/rename/remove omit the search argument entirely (stores/branches.ts:52, 64, 79, 91, 104).
findings.repro: Open a repository with many branches, open the Branches tab and type in the search box while watching the invoke log / the engine — no branch_list call is made and the full list is fetched on every refsChanged.
findings.expected: Either the search reaches branch_list (as the command surface and the store's signature both provide for), or the parameter is removed and the pane documents the filter as client-side.
findings.actual: The engine-side filter is unreachable dead plumbing; the pane loads every branch of the repository on every refresh and filters in the renderer, and the row-count/empty-state contract is computed from the unfiltered set (see BR-05).
findings.fix: Either bind the search box to the store (`branches.search.value = $event`, with a debounce) and drop `branchSearch`, or delete the unused `search` ref and the `search?` parameter from stores/branches.ts and commands.ts so the dead path cannot mislead the next reader.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/branches.test.ts — call `refresh(repo, 'feat')` and assert `branchList` was invoked with the needle; and an App test asserting that typing in the search box reaches `branch_list` rather than only re-rendering.

notes: CONFIRMED at every hop. App.vue:1087 declares a shell-local `branchSearch = ref("")` whose only other appearances in the file are the pane binding at 1589 and the write-back at 1601 — no watcher, no sync into the store. useBranches.ts:11 declares its own `search` ref; a repo-wide grep for `search.value` returns only two hits, both reads (useBranches.ts:29, 34). Nothing anywhere assigns to it, so `store.refresh(id, search.value)` always sends "", and the engine discards an empty needle anyway (commands/branches.rs:38-46 does `.filter(|s| !s.is_empty())` before matching). The remaining refresh paths pass nothing at all: useAppEvents.ts:33 calls `branches.refresh(event.payload.repo)` on every `refsChanged`, and stores/branches.ts does the same inside create/checkout/checkoutRemote/rename/remove — so a refsChanged refetches the full branch set regardless of the needle, confirming the repro. The Rust side genuinely implements the filter (branches.rs:38-46) and docs/03-command-surface.md:187 documents `search?` as part of the public branch_list contract, so the engine code is live contract, merely unreachable from the renderer; BranchListPane.vue:54-61 filters client-side instead. The only frontend caller of branchList is stores/branches.ts:28-29. I searched for the guard the auditor might have missed and found none: no debounced watcher on branchSearch, no second useBranches() call site, no store-level search ref, no alternate command caller passing a non-empty needle, no Rust integration test exercising it. One imprecision in the finding: "every refresh sends search: undefined" is only true of the useAppEvents/store-verb path — the composable watcher path sends "" — but both are engine no-ops, so the conclusion stands. Severity minor is right: search does work, it is just done in the renderer, so there is no user-visible incorrectness, no crash, no data loss; this is dead plumbing plus a full-list fetch. It is not not-a-bug because a parameter that reads as load-bearing across four layers and is never written is precisely what misleads the next reader.

findings.title: Toolbar Fetch always fails: `remote_fetch` is sent a string where Rust expects a struct
findings.evidence: src/bridges/commands.ts:291-298 — `remoteFetch(repo, remote, refspecs = [], mode = "default")` always includes `mode` in the payload: `invoke("remote_fetch", { args: { repo, remote, refspecs, mode } })`. src/bridges/bindings.ts:485 declares `RemoteFetchMode = "default" | "prune" | "tags" | "pruneTags"`. Rust's field is a struct: src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:40 imports `RemoteFetchMode` from `crate::engine::remotes`, and src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:56-65 defines it as `struct RemoteFetchMode { prune: bool, tags: TagFetch, depth: Option<i32> }` with `#[serde(default, rename_all = "camelCase")]`. src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:687-694 is the args struct (`#[serde(default)] pub mode: RemoteFetchMode`) — `default` only applies when the key is ABSENT, and the frontend always sends it. Only caller: src/composables/useGit.ts:56-61. docs/03-command-surface.md:241 documents the wire shape as `opts{prune, tags, ...}`, confirming the intent.
findings.repro: Open any repository that has a remote and press 工具栏 → 抓取. The invoke payload is `{args:{repo,remote,refspecs:[],mode:"default"}}`. serde fails to deserialize the string into the struct, so the command rejects before `RemoteFetch::validate` (refs.rs:696-706) ever runs.
findings.expected: `git fetch <remote>` runs, the remote-tracking refs update, FetchReport is returned and the branch list's ahead/behind badges refresh.
findings.actual: The promise rejects with a serde string ("invalid type: string \"default\", expected struct RemoteFetchMode"). useGit.run (useGit.ts:45-47) stores that raw string in `lastError`; runVerb (App.vue:580-584) shows only the generic "操作失败。" toast and records `error.message === undefined` in the activity list. Fetch has never worked in this build, and the failure reads like a network problem rather than a broken call.
findings.fix: Stop sending the key from the wrapper — omit `mode`/`refspecs` unless the caller supplies them so the Rust `#[serde(default)]` applies — and type the parameter as the Rust struct (`{prune?: boolean; tags?: TagFetch; depth?: number}`). Better: rename the engine struct (e.g. `RemoteFetchOptions`) so it stops colliding with `domain::repository::RemoteFetchMode`, which is a different two-value enum (domain/repository.rs:187-196). Also wire or refuse `remote_prune` — with the current defaults `prune:false` and no caller passing it, stale tracking refs can never be pruned from the UI.
