findings.testIdea: Add `#[cfg(test)] mod wire` to src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs: `serde_json::from_value::<RemoteFetch>(json!({"repo":"x","remote":"origin","refspecs":[],"mode":"default"}))` must be Ok, and `json!({"repo":"x","remote":"origin"})` must also be Ok. On the frontend, add src/bridges/commands.test.ts that mocks `@tauri-apps/api/core`'s `invoke` and asserts `remoteFetch("r","origin")` sends no `mode` key (and `remotePull`/`remotePublishBranch` send the keys the Rust structs actually declare).

notes:
CONFIRMED. I re-traced every hop and empirically reproduced the failure.

The wire mismatch is real. src/bridges/commands.ts:291-298 unconditionally includes `mode` in the payload (`invoke("remote_fetch", { args: { repo, remote, refspecs, mode } })`), typed as the string union `RemoteFetchMode = "default" | "prune" | "tags" | "pruneTags"` (src/bridges/bindings.ts:485). Rust's engine::remotes::RemoteFetchMode (src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:55-64) is a struct `{prune: bool, tags: TagFetch, depth: Option<i32>}` with `#[serde(default, rename_all="camelCase")]`. The args struct at src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:687-694 carries `#[serde(default)] pub mode: RemoteFetchMode` — `default` applies only when the key is ABSENT.

I searched for the guard/default/handler the auditor might have missed and found none:
- AppState::run (src-tauri/src/state.rs:56+) is only reached AFTER Tauri's #[tauri::command] has deserialized `args`, so the pipeline's steps 1-6 (resolve/enqueue/validate/execute) never run. RemoteFetch::validate (refs.rs:696-706) is downstream of the failure.
- No `untagged`, `deserialize_with`, or `Visitor` exists anywhere in remotes.rs or refs.rs — the derives are plain `#[derive(Deserialize)]` at remotes.rs:56.
- lib.rs:141 registers commands::remote_fetch with no adapter layer.
- No frontend invoke mock or browser fallback exists (src/bridges/external.ts is only openUrl).

Empirical verification: I built an isolated cargo project at /tmp/serdecheck copying the exact derives from the snapshot. Result:
  WITH mode key ("default"): ERR -> invalid type: string "default", expected struct RemoteFetchMode
  WITHOUT mode key:          OK  -> RemoteFetchMode { prune: false, tags: Unspecified, depth: None }
This matches the reported serde string exactly.

Only caller confirmed: src/composables/useGit.ts:60 `commands.remoteFetch(id, remote)`, reached from the toolbar verb at src/App.vue:628 / case "fetch" at App.vue:666. That toolbar item is gated on `remoteReason !== undefined`, so it is enabled exactly when it is guaranteed to fail. The error path also matches: useGit.ts:45-47 stores the raw rejection in lastError; runVerb (App.vue:580-584) passes `error.message` to activity.finish, but the rejection is a string so `.message` is undefined, and reportError (App.vue:548-553) falls through to the generic toast — reading like a network failure.

Secondary claims checked: remotePull and remotePublishBranch are NOT broken — I verified both payloads deserialize OK (opts:{} hits PullOptions' `#[serde(default)]`; setUpstream maps to set_upstream via camelCase). The auditor correctly scoped these to a test assertion rather than a bug. remote_prune is indeed unwired: the Rust command exists (refs.rs:862-865, registered in lib.rs) but has no frontend wrapper or caller anywhere in src/.

One defect the auditor MISSED: bindings.ts:498 declares `RepositoryRemote.fetchMode: RemoteFetchMode` with the same wrong string union, but Rust's domain::repository::RemoteFetchMode (domain/repository.rs:186-196) is a two-value enum `All | Specified` serializing to "all"/"specified". The type is wrong in the RESPONSE direction too. It is latent (nothing in src/ reads fetchMode yet) so it does not change severity, but the fix must correct it or the same mistake is re-made on the read path.

Severity kept at blocker: a globally-prominent toolbar verb that has never once succeeded in this build, failing 100% of the time on its only code path, with an error message that actively misdirects the user toward blaming the network. `pull` still works so the app is not wholly unusable, but Fetch is the single most-used remote operation and it is dead.

findings.title: Toolbar Push pushes the branch that was checked out when the repo was opened, not the current HEAD
findings.evidence: src/composables/useGit.ts:75-84 — `const branch = branchName ?? repos.selected?.headBranch`. src/App.vue:671-672 calls `git.push()` with no argument. `repos.selected` is `repositories.value.find(...)` (src/stores/repos.ts:27-29) and the only writer of `repositories` is `upsert` (repos.ts:36-43), called from open/init/clone only (repos.ts:61, 78, 124). Nothing refreshes RepoInfo afterwards: useAppEvents.ts:26-29 makes `reposChanged` a no-op, and there is no `repositoryRefresh` wrapper in src/bridges/commands.ts although the Rust command is registered at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:69. `headBranch` is read as "the current branch" in four other places (App.vue:207, 225-226, 596, 847, 1608), so the staleness is visible beyond push.
findings.repro: Open repo A whose HEAD is `main` (RepoInfo.headBranch = "main"), check out `feature` (App.vue:875 → branches.checkout → `branch_checkout`), then press 工具栏 → 推送.
findings.expected: `feature` is published — the toolbar's own disabled reason (App.vue:609, zh-CN "HEAD 处于游离状态 —— 请先签出分支再推送。") promises the verb means "push HEAD".
findings.actual: `repos.selected.headBranch` is still "main", so `remotePublishBranch(id, "origin", "main")` re-pushes main. Because origin already has main, the push is a no-op fast-forward that succeeds, and the toast claims 已推送. `feature` is never published; its row still shows ahead>0 with no upstream, and the window subtitle still says "在 main 上".
findings.fix: Resolve the branch from the live branch list (`branches.branches.value.find(b => b.isHead)?.name`) or pass the branch down from the list, and add a `repositoryRefresh` bridge so RepoInfo.headBranch is re-read on refsChanged (which also fixes the stale subtitle and the "Merge into <old branch>" label).
findings.testIdea: src/composables/useGit.test.ts: seed the repos store with RepoInfo{headBranch:"main"} and the branches store with a branch `feature` whose isHead is true; assert `remotePublishBranch` is invoked with "feature".

notes:
CONFIRMED — every step of the chain re-verified in /tmp/meridian-baseline, and I could not find the missing guard.

1. useGit.ts:75-84 — `const branch = branchName ?? repos.selected?.headBranch`. The toolbar calls `git.push()` with no argument (App.vue:672, `case "push": await runVerb(() => git.push(), t("shell.toast.pushed"))`). Confirmed verbatim.
2. Staleness source confirmed: `repos.selected` is `repositories.value.find(r => r.id === selectedId.value)` (stores/repos.ts:27-29). `grep -rn "upsert|repositories\.value"` over src/ shows the ONLY writers of `repositories` are `upsert` (repos.ts:36-43) called from `open` (:61), `init` (:78), `clone` (:124), plus `remove` (:160) which only filters. Nothing re-reads RepoInfo.
3. No refresh path: `grep -rn "repositoryRefresh" src/` returns ZERO hits. The Rust command is real (`src-tauri/src/commands/repository.rs:296 pub async fn repository_refresh`, registered at `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:69`) but has no TS wrapper. `useAppEvents.ts:29-33` handles `refsChanged` by refreshing only branches + history; `reposChanged` (:26-28) is an explicit no-op. `useRepositories.ts` exposes no refresh.
4. No Rust-side HEAD guard: `RemotePublishBranch::validate` (commands/refs.rs:901-904) is only `require_remote` + `require_local_branch` (refs.rs:1804 → require_branch). A stale-but-existing local branch validates and is pushed. `execute` passes `self.branch.trim()` straight to `remotes::publish_branch`.
5. The detached-HEAD guard at App.vue:596 reads the same stale value (`hasHead = selectedRepo.value?.headBranch != null`), so it is wrong in BOTH directions: stale-null keeps Push disabled after you check out a branch (and useGit then throws the "HEAD is detached" error), stale-"main" keeps it enabled while HEAD is actually detached. The zh-CN reason string at i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:197 is exactly "HEAD 处于游离状态 —— 请先签出分支再推送。", which is the contract the handler breaks.

What the auditor UNDERSTATED: the worst path is commit-and-push. `commitNow()` commits to LIVE HEAD (App.vue:998 `workingCopy.commit`), then App.vue:1022 pushes the STALE branch and reports `shell.toast.committedAndPushed`. So a genuine commit on `feature` is announced as pushed while `main` is published instead.

SEVERITY CORRECTION: blocker → major. It is a real silent wrong-ref write to a remote with a false success toast, which is why it is not minor. But it is not a blocker: (a) in the dominant repro the stale branch is already on origin, so the push is a no-op fast-forward and nothing is destroyed; (b) no local data loss — the unpublished commit is still on `feature` locally; (c) recovery is trivial and a correct path already exists in the same file: `pushSelectedBranch` (App.vue:490-497) resolves the pane's own branch and passes it explicitly to `git.push(name)`, so the branch pane publishes correctly; (d) it needs the checkout-after-open sequence to trigger. Publishing an unintended ref to a shared remote is the ceiling of the harm here, which is serious-but-recoverable, i.e. major.

Minor inaccuracy in the finding: `src/composables/useGit.test.ts` does not exist (existing tests are interactionCompleteness, templateCompiles, components/about/changelog, components/screens/AboutScreen, i18n/catalog, stores/loadState), so the test idea is a file to be created, not an existing one to extend. Does not affect the verdict.

findings.title: `remotePublishBranch` is always called with `setUpstream:false`, overriding the Rust default, so a first push can never record tracking
findings.evidence: src/bridges/commands.ts:309-319 — `setUpstream = false` and the key is always included. src/composables/useGit.ts:83 calls it with three arguments. Rust declares the opposite default: src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:888-895 `#[serde(default = "default_true")] pub set_upstream: bool` (default_true at refs.rs:1712). src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:1006-1012 writes `branch.<name>.remote`/`.merge` only when `set_upstream` is true, while src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:1014-1018 documents `PublishReport.upstream` as "the upstream shorthand that was recorded" and reports it unconditionally.
findings.repro: Create branch `feature`, then press 推送 in the branch pane (App.vue:1613 → pushSelectedBranch → `git.push("feature")`). Verified with the git CLI in /tmp/audit-remotes: `git push origin feature` writes no `branch.feature.*`; `git push -u origin feature` writes `branch.feature.remote=origin` and `branch.feature.merge=refs/heads/feature`.
findings.expected: `git push -u` semantics (the engine's own doc comment at engine/remotes.rs:976-977 calls this command "push a local branch and make it the upstream"): tracking is recorded, so the row shows `origin/feature` and ahead/behind.
findings.actual: No tracking is written. `branch_info` (src-tauri/src/engine/branches.rs:757-776) computes upstream/ahead/behind from `branch.upstream()`, so the row keeps upstream=None and (0,0) forever, and `PublishReport.upstream` reports an upstream that was never recorded. There is no UI to set upstream afterwards (see F15), so the branch stays untracked permanently.
findings.fix: Default the wrapper to true (or omit the key so Rust's `default_true` applies) for the publish verb; reserve `setUpstream:false` for an explicit plain push. Then make `PublishReport.upstream` honest when tracking is not written.
findings.testIdea: src/bridges/commands.test.ts: assert `remotePublishBranch("r","origin","feature")` does not send `setUpstream: false`. Rust side: deserialize `{"repo":"x","remote":"origin","branch":"feature"}` into `RemotePublishBranch` and assert `set_upstream == true`.

notes:
CONFIRMED — every link re-traced against the snapshot, and I could not find the guard/default/handler the auditor missed.

Arg path: `src/bridges/commands.ts:309-317` declares `setUpstream = false` and always includes the key (`args: { repo, remote, branch, setUpstream }`) — it is never omitted. `src/composables/useGit.ts:83` is the ONLY call site in the entire `src` tree (verified by grep) and passes 3 args. Reached from `App.vue:1613` -> `pushSelectedBranch` (App.vue:489-499) -> `git.push(name)`.

Rust side: `RemotePublishBranch` (`src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:888-894`) is `#[serde(default = "default_true")] pub set_upstream: bool` under `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, so the wire key is exactly `setUpstream` — which the TS always sends, so `default_true` provably never fires from the UI. `commands.ts:9` imports plain `invoke` from `@tauri-apps/api/core`; there is no shim/middleware that could rewrite the arg. `remotes.rs:1002-1005` calls `set_tracking_config` (branches.rs:658-668, the ONLY writer of `branch.<n>.remote`/`.merge`) exclusively inside `if set_upstream`.

Missed-alternatives I hunted, all dead ends:
1. `push()` -> `apply_tracking_updates` (remotes.rs:1194+) updates `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` (the remote-tracking ref), NOT branch config. Not an implicit-tracking rescue.
2. No second frontend call site, no alternate publish verb in src.
3. `branch_info` (branches.rs:757-776) derives upstream/ahead/behind from `branch.upstream()`; None -> (0,0), so the row can never recover.
4. No in-app remedy: grep finds ZERO frontend bindings for `branch_set_upstream` (the Rust command exists at refs.rs:278 and is registered at lib.rs:125, and docs/04-ui-spec.md:222 lists "set upstream" in the branch context menu, but nothing in `src` calls it).

TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding's framing (neither refutes it):
- UNDERSTATED impact: `BranchDetailPane.vue:100-110` renders the Tracking fact block with NO `v-if="upstream"` guard, so an untracked branch actively prints "ahead by 0 / behind by 0" — a false measurement, not merely a missing field. Also `useCompare.ts:41` uses `branch.upstream` as the compare baseline, and `BranchListPane.vue:140-141` never shows the upstream column.
- OVERSTATED one sub-claim: `PublishReport.upstream` does lie (remotes.rs:1000-1001 fills it unconditionally while its doc comment at :212 says "the upstream shorthand that was recorded"), but grep shows NO frontend consumer of that field — it is a latent contract defect, not a user-visible wrong string. Only the branch-row half of the display defect is visible today.

Spec corroboration: `docs/03-command-surface.md:250` documents `remote_publish_branch` semantics as "push + set upstream", and `remotes.rs:974-975` says "git's `push -u`" — so the frontend deviates from its own documented surface.

Severity major CONFIRMED, not raised: the push itself succeeds and commits land safely on the remote; no data is lost and no operation fails. The damage is persistent wrong information in the primary push path, with no in-app workaround. That clears the major bar without reaching blocker.

TestIdea nit (does not affect the finding): it cites `src/bridges/commands.test.ts`, which does not exist. Frontend tests live at `src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts`, `src/templateCompiles.test.ts`, `src/i18n/catalog.test.ts`, `src/stores/loadState.test.ts` and two component tests — a new file or an existing one is required.

findings.title: Pull always fetches `origin`'s copy of the current branch and ignores the branch's configured upstream
findings.evidence: src/composables/useGit.ts:62-67 — `remotePull(id, repos.defaultRemote)` with `branch` null and `opts {}`. src/bridges/commands.ts:300-307. src/stores/repos.ts:31-34 — `defaultRemote` prefers a remote literally named `origin`, else `remotes[0]`. src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:757-764 fills the null branch with the checked-out branch name. src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:583-587 builds the refspec from the *passed* remote and branch (`+refs/heads/{branch}:{tracking}`) and never consults `branch.<name>.remote`/`.merge` — which the engine already reads elsewhere (src-tauri/src/engine/repository.rs:478 branch_upstreams).
findings.repro: Build a fork checkout: remotes `origin` (your fork) and `upstream` (the project), with `git branch -u upstream/main main`; press 工具栏 → 拉取. Verified with the git CLI in /tmp/audit-remotes/forkclone: plain `git pull` fast-forwards from `upstream/main` (the branch's upstream); Meridian's path fetches `refs/heads/main` from `origin` and merges the fork's history instead.
findings.expected: `git pull` semantics: integrate the branch's configured upstream (`branch.<name>.remote` / `branch.<name>.merge`).
findings.actual: The fork's `main` is merged into local `main`. No warning: the user either gets a wrong merge commit (fork content silently entering the branch that tracks upstream) or an unexpected conflict, and the branch's real upstream is never fetched.
findings.fix: When the caller does not name a branch, resolve the branch's tracking config (reuse `branch_upstreams` from engine/repository.rs:478) and pull that remote/refspec; fall back to `defaultRemote` only when the branch has no upstream, as git does.
findings.testIdea: An engine test (or a CLI-driven fixture) with `main` tracking `upstream/main`: assert `remotes::pull(repo, "origin", "main", &Default::default())` is not what the toolbar sends, i.e. add a test that the resolved remote for a branch with `branch.main.remote=upstream` is `upstream`. Frontend: src/composables/useGit.test.ts asserting `remotePull` receives the tracking remote, not `defaultRemote`.

notes:
CONFIRMED — re-traced end to end, no guard found.

Path (all in /tmp/meridian-baseline):
1. src/App.vue:668-669 — toolbar verb "pull" calls `git.pull()`. The toolbar button's only guard is `remoteReason` (App.vue:596-602, 629), which is set purely from `repositories.defaultRemote !== null`.
2. src/composables/useGit.ts:62-67 — `commands.remotePull(id, repos.defaultRemote)`; `branch` omitted (null) and `opts` defaults to `{}`.
3. src/stores/repos.ts:31-34 — `defaultRemote` = remote literally named `origin`, else `remotes[0]`. No branch-tracking input at all. Worse, `loadRemotes` (repos.ts:45-54) assigns only `.remotes` and discards the `upstreams: UpstreamTracking[]` that `repositoryRemotesLoad` already returns (bindings.ts:502-515), so the frontend structurally cannot see tracking config today.
4. src/bridges/commands.ts:300-307 — `remote` forwarded verbatim as `remote`.
5. src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:760-775 — `RemotePull::execute` fills the null branch from `branches::head_branch_name` and calls `remotes::pull(cx.repo, self.remote.trim(), &branch, &self.opts)`. `RemotePull::validate` (:735-759) checks only require_remote / require_no_integration / require_attached_head / branch-is-checked-out / require_clean — no upstream resolution anywhere.
6. src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:587-591 — `let tracking = tracking_ref(repo, name, branch)...; let refspec = format!("+refs/heads/{branch}:{tracking}"); fetch(repo, name, &[refspec], ...)`. Both the remote and the refspec derive from the *passed* remote and the local branch name. `tracking_ref` (:1140-1148) only transforms via that remote's own fetch refspecs. The single `branch.<branch>.remote` read in the whole file is the test helper `tracking_of` at :1383. So `branch.<name>.remote` / `.merge` are never consulted — the engine's `branch_upstreams` (engine/repository.rs:480-495) is not on this path.

Independent repro with the git CLI (fresh bare upstream + fork clone, `main` tracking `upstream/main`, a fork-only commit on `origin/main` and an upstream-only commit on `upstream/main`): plain `git pull` integrated the upstream commit; the Meridian-shaped sequence (`git fetch origin '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main'` then merge `refs/remotes/origin/main`) integrated the fork's.

Severity stays major. It is silent (no warning anywhere in useGit.ts / App.vue / the command layer) and the two outcomes are both bad: (a) if the fork's branch has diverged, a merge commit or conflict from the wrong remote lands on a branch the user believes tracks `upstream`; (b) the more common fork case — fork `main` behind local `main` — hits remotes.rs:604 (`graph_descendant_of(local_tip, remote_tip)`), returns `PullOutcome::UpToDate`, and the UI reports "pulled" while the branch's real upstream was never fetched at all. No crash, no data loss, and recoverable from a terminal, so not a blocker; but a plausible fork/contributor configuration silently produces the wrong repository state, which is why it clears major rather than minor.

One correction to the proposed fix: it should not land in `remotes::pull`. docs/03-command-surface.md:243 defines `remote_pull(repo, remote, branch?, opts{...})` with `remote` as a required explicit argument, and CAP-G6-03 (docs/01-product-spec.md:155) specifies "remote + branch selection" — an engine that silently overrides a caller-named remote contradicts that contract. The discrepancy is in the caller.

findings.title: A failed remote-list load is rendered as the fact "this repository has no remote" and disables Fetch/Pull/Push
findings.evidence: src/stores/repos.ts:45-54 — `catch { remotes.value = []; }`: the ErrorPayload is discarded entirely and `remotesLoading` is written but read by nobody (grep: only repos.ts:25,46,52,186). src/App.vue:595-610 derives `hasRemote` from `defaultRemote` and the reason `shell.toolbar.noRemote` = "此仓库没有配置远程。" (src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:196), applied to fetch/pull/push at App.vue:628-630. Secondary: src/stores/repos.ts:90-93 — `select` does not clear `remotes`, so between the switch and the load resolving, `defaultRemote` still answers with the previous repository's remote name and the verbs are enabled against a remote that may not exist.
findings.repro: Make `repository_remotes_load` fail for a repo that does have a remote — e.g. a config read error, a permission problem on `.git/config`, or any transient failure — then open/select the repository.
findings.expected: The load failure is reported as a failure (the four-state contract in src/stores/loadState.ts exists for exactly this), and the toolbar stays neutral about whether a remote exists.
findings.actual: `remotes` becomes `[]`, `defaultRemote` becomes null, and the toolbar asserts "此仓库没有配置远程。" as a fact. Fetch/Pull/Push are disabled and there is nothing on screen indicating that a load failed; the verbs stay dead until the repo is closed and re-opened.
findings.fix: Keep the error (a `remotesState` or the store's `lastError`) and render it; only disable the verbs on a *successful* empty list. Clear `remotes` in `select` before loading so a switch cannot briefly use the previous repo's remote.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/repos.test.ts: mock `repositoryRemotesLoad` to reject, then assert the store records the error (or reports an error state) and that `defaultRemote` is not presented as a confirmed absence.

notes:
I re-traced every hop of the claim against /tmp/meridian-baseline and found no guard, default, or handler that rescues it. It is confirmed, with one addition to the evidence.

1. The swallow is real and complete. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/repos.ts:45-54 is `catch { remotes.value = []; }` — the binding is omitted entirely, so the ErrorPayload is unreachable, and `lastError` (repos.ts:22) is never written. The store's other async entry points (`open` 65-70, `init` 82-87, `clone` 128-133, `discoverNearby` 151-155, `reveal` 173-176) all set `lastError`, so `loadRemotes` is the lone exception in its own file.

2. The failure is reachable, not theoretical. The command is fallible end to end: src-tauri/src/commands/repository.rs:494 returns `state.run(...)`, which is `Result<_, ErrorPayload>` (src-tauri/src/state.rs:56); a poisoned repo lock is a hand-written Err at state.rs:71-73, a panicked task becomes Err at state.rs:93-96, and engine/repository.rs:444-452 `remotes_model` propagates `branch_upstreams` (which opens `repo.config()?` at 481), `repo.find_remote(&name)?`, and `fetch_refspecs()?`/`push_refspecs()?`. A `.git/config` that cannot be read, or any of those, produces Err where `open()` (engine/repository.rs:29, a bare `Repository::open`) succeeded.

3. The false-fact rendering is exact. src/App.vue:595 `const hasRemote = repositories.defaultRemote.value !== null;` → App.vue:598-605 sets `remoteReason = t("shell.toolbar.noRemote")`, applied verbatim to fetch/pull/push at App.vue:628-630. The string is `noRemote: "此仓库没有配置远程。"` at src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:196 — a statement about the world, not about the load.

4. `remotesLoading` is indeed write-only. Grep across src/ hits it only at repos.ts:25 (decl), 46, 52 (writes), 186 (export). No component or composable reads it, so nothing distinguishes "loading" from "confirmed empty" anywhere.

5. Nothing else retries. `loadRemotes` is called only from repos.ts:63, 80, 92, 126 and exported; `remove` (159-164) does not re-load, so after a failed load the toolbar stays dead until close-and-reopen, exactly as claimed.

6. Extra evidence the auditor did not have, which makes it worse rather than better: the sidebar "远程" section is NOT built from `repos.remotes`. src/App.vue:271-278 derives `remoteRows` from the branches store's remote branches (`branches.branches.filter(b => b.isRemote)`), and that store (src/stores/branches.ts:24-39) does implement the four-state contract properly — `state.value = errorState(error)` on failure. So a failure confined to the remotes path leaves the sidebar still listing remote branches while the toolbar simultaneously asserts the repo has no remote, and branches.ts:17-21 carries an explicit docstring naming this exact failure mode ("indistinguishable from 'this repository has no remotes'"). The repos store violates the convention the sibling store documents.

7. The fix is also cheaper than reported: `repositories.lastError` is already rendered as a banner at src/App.vue:1440-1441 (`:error-message="repositories.lastError.value?.message ?? null"`), so the plumbing to surface the error exists and only the assignment is missing.

I also checked the secondary claim and it holds but is correctly scoped as secondary: repos.ts:90-93 `select` sets `selectedId` then fires `void loadRemotes(id)` without clearing `remotes`, so for the duration of the in-flight load `defaultRemote` still answers with the previous repository's remote name. It is low-impact because the resulting wrong action is loud rather than silent — src/composables/useGit.ts:58/64/77 passes that stale name into `remoteFetch`/`remotePull`/`remotePublishBranch`, and a bad name surfaces as a git error toast rather than a wrong write. It is still a real correctness hole and belongs in the same fix.

Severity stays major, not blocker and not minor. It is not a blocker: no data corruption, no wrong write, and it needs a fallible-command condition rather than ordinary use. It is above minor because the failure is silent, it converts an error into a confident false claim about the user's repository, it kills three primary verbs with no on-screen indication and no recovery path short of reopening the repository — and the codebase already documents that this is the bug class it cares about.

One correction to the finding's testIdea: there is no src/stores/repos.test.ts (find src -name "*.test.ts" returns only changelog, AboutScreen, catalog, interactionCompleteness, loadState, templateCompiles), so the test has to be written from scratch rather than added to an existing file.

findings.title: Selecting a remote-tracking branch leaves the branch detail pane empty, making its only verb unreachable
findings.evidence: src/App.vue:1089-1094 — `selectedBranchInfo` searches `branches.branches.value` only. src/stores/branches.ts:11,31 — `branches` holds locals, `remoteBranches` holds remote-tracking refs (both merged in `allBranches`, branches.ts:22). src/App.vue:1584 passes `branches.allBranches.value` to the list, and src/components/panes/BranchListPane.vue:124 emits `filtered[index].fullName`, e.g. `refs/remotes/origin/main`. The remote row's verb lives behind `v-else` on `remote` at src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.vue:150-153, wired at src/App.vue:1615 to `checkoutSelectedBranch` (App.vue:503-513).
findings.repro: In the branch tab set the filter to 远程 (or 全部) and click a row such as `origin/main`.
findings.expected: The detail pane shows the remote branch (docs/04 §4.1 "Remote branch | checkout (tracks)") and its 抓取到本地 verb.
findings.actual: `selectedBranchInfo` is null because the row only exists in `remoteBranches`, so the pane renders its no-selection state. The remote branch's only verb — the one that creates the local tracking branch — cannot be reached from the pane at all; only the double-click/`activate` path works.
findings.fix: Resolve the name against `branches.allBranches.value` in `selectedBranchInfo` (and keep the local-only assumption out of any verb that must not act on a remote ref).
findings.testIdea: A unit test of the lookup (or src/App.test.ts): with `selectedBranchName = "refs/remotes/origin/main"` and that row present in `remoteBranches`, assert `selectedBranchInfo` is non-null and `isRemote === true`.

notes:
Confirmed, no rescuing guard exists. Traced line by line in /tmp/meridian-baseline.

1. Store split is real: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts:27-32 does `branches.value = locals` (branchList(repo,"local")) and `remoteBranches.value = remotes`; allBranches (line 22) is the merge. Rust src-tauri/src/engine/branches.rs:53-59 maps BranchFilter::Local => &[git2::BranchType::Local], so `branches.value` contains only refs/heads/*.

2. The lookup is local-only: src/App.vue:1089-1094 `selectedBranchInfo` searches `branches.branches.value` by fullName. A remote row's fullName is `refs/remotes/origin/main` (branch_info, branches.rs:750-753 uses branch.get().name()), which can never match a local ref.

3. Remote rows are selectable: App.vue:1586 passes `allBranches` to the list; BranchListPane.vue:57-58 keeps remotes when filter is remote/all; the filter tabs are live (App.vue:1600 @update:filter); BranchListPane.vue:124 emits select with filtered[index].fullName; App.vue:1591 assigns it directly to selectedBranchName. No normalization, no guard.

4. Consequence: selectedBranchInfo is null, so BranchDetailPane.vue:67-72 renders the `branch.noSelectionTitle` empty state while the clicked row is still highlighted selected (BranchListPane.vue:121 compares fullName === selectedName, which does match). The remote-only verb at BranchDetailPane.vue:150-153 (`branch.fetchIntoLocal` = 抓取到本地) and the whole identity/facts block never render. Only @activate (App.vue:1592 -> checkoutFlow) reaches a remote branch, and that path does work (App.vue:852-868 -> branches.checkoutRemote). So the verb is reachable, but only via an undiscoverable double-click.

Severity stays major: docs/04-ui-spec.md:223 specifies "Remote branch | checkout (tracks) | delete remote, rename remote branch, show in history, fetch this remote" — a documented P0 verb set is entirely absent for remote rows, and the pane actively asserts "no branch selected" while a row is selected. Not a blocker: nothing crashes, no data risk, and one alternate path (double-click) works.

One correction to the finding: its `fix` line ("keep the local-only assumption out of any verb that must not act on a remote ref") understates the scope. BranchDetailPane already gates merge (130), rebase (135) and push (142) behind `!remote`, but rename (165) and delete (169) are NOT gated. Switching selectedBranchInfo to allBranches alone would newly expose rename and delete on a remote ref, and both fail at the engine: rename -> branches.ts:90 -> branches.rs:329-331 find_branch(old, BranchType::Local) -> branch_not_found; delete -> branches.rs:357-364 skipped with class reference_not_found. The patch must gate both as well.

Also, the testIdea location does not exist: there is no src/App.test.ts in this repo. The suite is src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts, src/stores/loadState.test.ts, src/i18n/catalog.test.ts, src/templateCompiles.test.ts, src/components/screens/AboutScreen.test.ts, src/components/about/changelog.test.ts. The lookup is a closure inside App.vue's setup block, so a unit test requires extracting it (store getter or a pure helper) first — an App.test.ts that mounts the shell would need heavy Tauri mocking.

findings.title: No sync verb is guarded while one is in flight: `useGit.busy` is written and read by nobody
findings.evidence: src/composables/useGit.ts:26 declares `busy`, :39 and :49 write it, :54 exports it — and no consumer reads it (grep for `useGit` finds only App.vue:43,131, which uses the verb methods). src/App.vue:1606-1621 passes only `:branch`, `:current-branch` and `:can-delete` to BranchDetailPane, so its `busy` prop stays at the default false (src/components/panes/BranchDetailPane.vue:30) and every `:disabled="busy"` in that component (lines 119, 131, 135, 145, 150, 165, 172) is inert. The toolbar verb model (src/App.vue:593-639) has no busy term either, and `pushOptions` is likewise never passed (only declared at BranchDetailPane.vue:28,146).
findings.repro: Double-click 工具栏 → 推送, or double-click 推送 in the branch pane.
findings.expected: The second click is ignored while the first is in flight.
findings.actual: Two `remote_publish_branch` invocations are issued and both run — the per-repo queue serialises them but does not dedupe — producing two activity entries, two success toasts and two network pushes (and, with F2, two pushes of the wrong branch).
findings.fix: Read `git.busy` in `toolbarVerbs` (`disabled: busy || …`) and pass `:busy="git.busy"` into BranchDetailPane; or guard inside `useGit.run` (`if (busy.value) return null`).
findings.testIdea: src/App.test.ts: with the git composable's `busy` true, assert the push verb model reports `disabled === true` with a reason; and src/composables/useGit.test.ts asserting a second `push()` while the first is pending issues no second `remotePublishBranch`.

notes:
CONFIRMED on every material claim; I could not find the guard the default assumed existed.

(1) `busy` is genuinely dead. src/composables/useGit.ts:26 declares it, :39 and :49 write it, :55 exports it (the finding cites :54 — off by one, immaterial). An exhaustive enumeration of every `git.` call site in App.vue yields only git.fetch/pull/push/stash/merge/rebase/continueOperation/abortOperation/resolveConflict. `git.busy` and `git.lastError` are read nowhere in the repo. Both exported refs are dead state.

(2) BranchDetailPane is never told. App.vue:1606-1609 passes only :branch, :current-branch, :can-delete. No :busy, no :push-options. Grepping `pushOptions` across all of src/ hits only BranchDetailPane.vue:28 (decl), :30 (default), :146 (bind) — App.vue never supplies it. With `busy` defaulting to false at BranchDetailPane.vue:30, all seven `:disabled="busy"` / `:busy="busy"` bindings (119, 131, 135, 145, 150, 165, 172) are inert.

(3) The toolbar model omits busy. App.vue:593-639 sets no `busy` key on any verb. The plumbing is fully built and merely unwired: ToolbarVerbModel has `busy?: boolean` at contracts.ts:372 and AppToolbar.vue:55 binds `:busy="verb.busy"` — always undefined.

(4) Guards I hunted for and eliminated:
 - SplitAction.runPrimary (SplitAction.vue:37) DOES contain `if (props.disabled || props.busy) return` — the real guard, but its `busy` input is permanently false, so it never fires. This is the one the auditor correctly identified as inert.
 - App.vue runVerb (:571-588): no guard. useGit.run: no guard.
 - Backend: RepoQueueManager::enqueue (queue.rs) is a fair per-repo tokio Mutex that serialises but never dedupes; AppState::run (state.rs) resolves the repo, enqueues, then validates INSIDE the queued turn — so the second call is never rejected for being second.
 - The only in-flight guard in the codebase is useApp.ts:73/132 (`if (inFlight) return inFlight`), which guards the app update check — unrelated.
 - No CSS pointer-events gating (only ToastHost/atmosphere), no debounce/throttle anywhere.

So double-click does issue two real remote_publish_branch invocations, two activity entries and two toasts.

SEVERITY CORRECTED major -> minor. The "actual" field overstates the outcome. Because the second invocation is serialised behind the first AND each command re-validates on its own turn, the destructive verbs self-neutralise: a double-clicked stash hits require_dirty (refs.rs:1777) and returns "There is nothing to stash"; a double-clicked merge hits require_no_integration / integration_in_progress (integrate.rs:129, merge.rs:399) or returns IntegrationOutcome::UpToDate (merge.rs:413) — never a second merge commit. Duplicate push is a redundant network round-trip that git treats as normal and idempotent. No wrong ref is written, no state corrupted, no data lost. The user-visible harm is duplicate toasts/activity rows and one spurious error toast on stash. That is a genuine defect worth fixing in one line, but it does not meet a major bar. Note the finding's parenthetical "(and, with F2, two pushes of the wrong branch)" imports another finding's severity into this one and should not count toward F9's rating.

One correction to the proposed fix, which matters: `if (busy.value) return null` inside useGit.run is wrong. run() returns ErrorPayload | null where null means SUCCESS, and runVerb (App.vue:574-586) reads a null return as success and pushes a success toast. That guard would emit a third false confirmation for work that never ran.

findings.title: A verb's post-success refresh is applied to whichever repository it was issued for, overwriting the stores after a repo switch
findings.evidence: src/composables/useGit.ts:32-34 — `refreshAll(repo)` is called with the id captured at :37, and :43 runs it after the action resolves. src/stores/branches.ts:24-39 assigns `branches.value = locals` unconditionally with no "is this still the selected repo" guard; the same shape is in src/stores/workingCopy.ts:26-34 and src/stores/history.ts:85-90. Compare the guard the compare composable does have: src/composables/useCompare.ts:115-117 uses a request token and App.vue:520-524 re-keys on repo change. The event path is guarded (src/composables/useAppEvents.ts:31,37 compare `event.payload.repo !== repos.selectedId`) but the verb path is not.
findings.repro: In repo A press 拉取 (or 推送) against a slow remote; while it is in flight, switch to repo B from the sidebar (App.vue:526-529 → repos.select); A's call resolves.
findings.expected: B's lists keep showing B.
findings.actual: `refreshAll(A)` runs after B's own refresh and the branch/working-copy/history stores end up holding A's data while B is selected. `selectedBranchInfo` (App.vue:1092) then resolves against A's branches, and any verb pressed from the pane operates on A's refs under B's identity — with F9's missing guard making the overlap easy to hit.
findings.fix: Bail out of `refreshAll` when the repo is no longer `repos.selectedId`, or key each store's data by repo id.
findings.testIdea: src/composables/useGit.test.ts: start a push for A, switch the store's selection to B, resolve the push, assert the branches store was not overwritten with A's rows.

notes:
Confirmed by full re-trace; I looked for the missing guard and it does not exist anywhere on the verb path.

useGit.ts:36-51: run() captures id = repoId() (= repos.selectedId, :28-30) at :37, awaits the action at :42, then unconditionally calls refreshAll(id) at :43. Nothing between the action resolving and the refresh re-checks selectedId.

The three stores accept any repo id unconditionally: branches.ts:24-39 assigns branches.value/remoteBranches.value straight from branchList(repo); workingCopy.ts:26-33 applies wcStatusLoad(repo); history.ts:85-95 applies historyCommitsLoad(repo). loadState.ts is a pure data holder — there is no generation counter, request token, or loadedFor marker anywhere in the store layer.

The repo switch is not gated. RepoSwitcher.vue declares a `locked` prop documented as "Disables the switcher while a blocking operation runs" (:19-23, :77), but App.vue:1417 binds `:locked="false"` hardcoded. useGit.busy (:26) is returned but never bound to the switcher — the only busy consumed is activity.running for toolbar verbs (App.vue:651). repositories.select() (stores/repos.ts:90-93) just sets selectedId and calls loadRemotes.

Ordering is the exploitable direction, not the exotic one: the switch fires the composable watchers (useBranches.ts:19-25, useWorkingCopy.ts:15-21, useHistory.ts:19-26), each doing `void store.refresh(B)`. A's refreshAll(A) starts after that, so on equal-cost IPC it typically resolves last and wins. No watcher or event re-fires afterward, so A's data persists under B until the next manual refresh.

The contrast the finding draws is accurate, not rhetorical: useCompare.ts:115-117 uses `requestToken += 1` plus a token check, App.vue:520-524 re-keys compare on activeRepoId, and useAppEvents.ts:31,37 guards with `event.payload.repo !== repos.selectedId`. The verb path is genuinely the unguarded one.

The consequence chain also checks out: selectedBranchName (App.vue:1085) is never reset on repo switch (written only at :413, :792, and by the list's own @select at :1591). selectedBranchInfo (:1089-1093) resolves that name against branches.branches, so after the overwrite it resolves against A's list while B is selected, and git.push/merge/rebase (:496, :802, :808) then send A's branch name at B.

One wording correction to the finding (does not affect the verdict): it says a follow-on verb "operates on A's refs under B's identity." It is the reverse — the command targets B with A's branch name (remotePublishBranch(B, remote, A_branch)). Still a wrong-repo write, but the description is backwards.

Severity stays major, not blocker: the window is seconds and gated on a slow remote, the wrong state is visible (A's branch names rendered under B's repo header), and any later refresh clears it. It is not minor either, because the follow-on push/merge can reach the engine with a cross-repo ref, and no refresh self-heals it without user action.

findings.title: Every list's error arm is hardcoded English in a zh-CN UI
findings.evidence: src/components/common/ListShell.vue:66 `{{ errorMessage ?? "Something went wrong." }}` and :68 `<button …>Try again</button>`; the file has no `useI18n` at all (grep finds no `t(` call). The arm is used by every list: src/components/panes/BranchListPane.vue:74-79, src/components/panes/HistoryPane.vue:154-158, src/components/panes/WorkingCopyPane.vue:164-168, src/components/panes/ComparePane.vue:118-122.
findings.repro: Make any list load fail with the UI in 简体中文 — for instance press Cmd+Shift+R, which fails by F6, or point a repo at an unreachable remote and pull.
findings.expected: A catalogue string (the project rule: the UI renders catalogue entries, src/i18n/catalog.test.ts enforces parity).
findings.actual: "Something went wrong." and "Try again" render in English. The catalogue test cannot see them because they are literals rather than keys, and the fallback also masks real errors: when the rejection is a Tauri string (F1, F6) `state.error.message` is undefined, so the panel shows this generic English line instead of anything actionable.
findings.fix: Add `shell.list.error` / `shell.list.retry` to both catalogues and render `t(...)`; keep the `??` fallback pointing at the catalogue key, not a literal.
findings.testIdea: Extend src/i18n/catalog.test.ts with a scan for ASCII-only quoted literals inside template interpolations/attributes in src/components, failing on ones with no `t(` nearby — or a targeted component test asserting ListShell's error arm renders `t('shell.list.error')` and `t('shell.list.retry')`.

notes:
CONFIRMED after line-by-line retrace; severity corrected down.

Verified in the snapshot:
- src/components/common/ListShell.vue:66 `{{ errorMessage ?? "Something went wrong." }}` and :68 `<button type="button" @click="$emit('retry')">Try again</button>` are hardcoded English literals.
- The file has zero i18n wiring. Grep for useI18n|vue-i18n|$t( returns only false positives (.ghost:hover at :167, $emit at :61/:68). Every sibling rendering copy is localized: all panes/*.vue via `const { t } = useI18n()`, AccountScreen.vue and RepositoryListScreen.vue via `$t()`. ListShell is the sole unlocalized outlier, and it is the shared chrome underneath all of them.
- The finding UNDERCOUNTS blast radius: it names 4 call sites, there are 6. It also misses src/components/screens/AccountScreen.vue:95 and src/components/screens/RepositoryListScreen.vue:280.
- No guard rescues it. globalInjection: true (src/i18n/index.ts:49) means $t is available app-wide, so nothing is structurally missing — the strings simply bypass the catalogue. src/i18n/catalog.test.ts only flattens and diffs the two catalogues; it never scans src/components, so a literal passes parity vacuously, exactly as the finding claims.
- No test covers ListShell (grep across all *.test.ts for ListShell / "Try again" / "Something went wrong" returns nothing).

Secondary claim also holds: errorState is a bare cast (src/stores/loadState.ts:19, `error as ErrorPayload`), pinned as "a cast, not a converter" by src/stores/loadState.test.ts:79-87. asErrorPayload (src/components/diff/useDiffDocument.ts:133) does normalize but only the diff path uses it; stores/workingCopy.ts and stores/history.ts pass raw rejections through. So a Tauri-string rejection leaves state.error.message undefined and the generic English fallback fires. However that masking is a SEPARATE correctness bug belonging with F1/F6 and must not inflate this finding.

Severity corrected major -> minor. The defect is real and correctly localized, but it is cosmetic copy on an error path: the error still surfaces, the retry button still works, nothing is lost or corrupted. The only genuinely functional part of the claim is the masking, which belongs to a different finding. Untranslated fallback text in an error state is minor against blocker/major/minor.

Fix correction: the proposed fix says to add shell.list.error / shell.list.retry, but suitable keys already exist and are already correctly translated — common.retry = "Retry"/"重试" (en.ts:42, zh-CN.ts:37) and errors.byCode.unclassified = "Something went wrong."/"出了点问题。" (en.ts:179, zh-CN.ts:172). common.retry is already the cross-cutting retry word, used by BlamePane.vue:136, CommitDetailPane.vue:125, ReleaseNotesPanel.vue:97. Adding new keys would create exactly the duplication the parity test exists to prevent. Because globalInjection is on, no import is needed (AccountScreen.vue:81 calls $t bare in a template), so the fix is two template lines and zero catalogue churn.

findings.title: The toolbar Push success toast omits the `{branch}` the message needs
findings.evidence: src/App.vue:672 — `runVerb(() => git.push(), t("shell.toast.pushed"))` with no interpolation params. src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:273 — `pushed: "已推送 {branch}。"`; the en catalogue has the same placeholder (src/i18n/locales/parts/en/diff.ts:293). The correct call, with the branch, is src/App.vue:498 (`t("shell.toast.pushed", { branch: name })`).
findings.repro: Press 工具栏 → 推送. Measured against the snapshot's own vue-i18n 2.x: `t('shell.toast.pushed')` returns `"已推送 。"` while `t('shell.toast.pushed',{branch:'main'})` returns `"已推送 main。"`.
findings.expected: "已推送 main。" — naming the branch that was pushed.
findings.actual: "已推送 。" — the branch name is silently dropped, leaving a broken sentence with a stray space. Combined with F2 the dropped name is also the only place the branch would have been named.
findings.fix: Pass the branch actually pushed: `t("shell.toast.pushed", { branch })`. Resolving that branch once (as F2's fix requires) makes this fall out naturally.
findings.testIdea: Extend src/i18n/catalog.test.ts: for each catalogue value containing `{x}`, scan App.vue for the corresponding `t(` call and assert an object with `x` is supplied — or at minimum assert `shell.toast.pushed` is only used with `{ branch }`.

notes:
CONFIRMED (with one factual error in the evidence and one fix correction).

Re-traced the path line by line in /tmp/meridian-baseline:
- src/App.vue:672 `case "push": await runVerb(() => git.push(), t("shell.toast.pushed")); return;` — second arg is the pre-rendered `success` string, passed straight to `shell.pushToast({kind:"success", text: success})` in `runVerb` (App.vue:575-590). No wrapper, no guard, no fallback.
- The toolbar verb is live, not dead code: `toolbarVerbs` (App.vue:593+) enables `push` whenever repo + remote + headBranch all exist — the ordinary case — and `pushReason` only disables it for no-repo/no-remote/detached-HEAD.
- `t` is the plain composition-API `useI18n().t` (App.vue:106); there is no project-level `t` wrapper that supplies defaults.
- `git.push` is `push(branchName?: string)` (src/composables/useGit.ts:75), so `git.push()` is valid, returns success, and the toast fires.
- Both catalogues carry the placeholder: zh-CN `pushed: "已推送 {branch}。"` (parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:273), en `pushed: "Pushed {branch}."` (parts/en/diff.ts:293). The correct sibling call is App.vue:498 `t("shell.toast.pushed", { branch: name })`.
- src/i18n/catalog.test.ts contains no assertion covering `pushed` or `{branch}`, so nothing catches this in CI.

Two corrections to the finding as written:
1. The repro says "vue-i18n 2.x". The snapshot pins `"vue-i18n": "^11.4.14"` (package.json) and 11.4.14 is what's in node_modules. I re-ran the repro against the snapshot's own build: `t('shell.toast.pushed')` -> "已推送 。" and `t(...,{branch:'main'})` -> "已推送 main。". Output is identical under v11, so the repro's conclusion stands — only the stated version was wrong.
2. The suggested fix says pass "the branch actually pushed", but names `{ branch }` as if `selectedBranchInfo` were it. It isn't. `selectedBranchInfo` is the branch *selected in the pane* (App.vue:1089, derived from `selectedBranchName`), while the toolbar path calls `git.push()` with no ref, i.e. it pushes HEAD. On a pane reading a non-HEAD branch those differ — so naively writing `t("shell.toast.pushed", { branch: selectedBranchInfo.value?.name })` would name the wrong branch. The toolbar toast must name `selectedRepo.value?.headBranch` (the ref actually pushed), unless F2's fix makes the toolbar push the pane's branch, in which case the one resolved name serves both.

Severity stays minor: a single success-toast string renders with a dropped noun and a stray space. No data loss, no wrong ref created by this bug (the wrong-ref problem is F2's), and the fix is one argument. It is a genuine user-visible defect, not cosmetic-only in the sense of being invisible.

findings.title: Toolbar Stash cannot include untracked files, yet its toast claims the working copy was stashed
findings.evidence: src/composables/useGit.ts:85 — `stashSave(id, {})`; src/bridges/commands.ts:361; src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:1157-1176 (opts defaulted); src-tauri/src/engine/stash.rs:45-55 (`include_untracked`/`include_ignored` default false, and `stash_flags` is the only place they are read); the toolbar verb carries no options at all (src/App.vue:631). The validator disagrees with the operation: src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:1777-1791 sets `include_untracked(true)` before deciding there is nothing to stash.
findings.repro: Repo with one modified tracked file and one untracked file; press 工具栏 → 储藏. Then repeat with only the untracked file present.
findings.expected: Either stash everything (`git stash -u`) or tell the user what was left behind.
findings.actual: The untracked file stays in the working copy while the toast says 已储藏工作区。. In the untracked-only case `require_dirty` passes but `stash::save` has nothing to stash, so the user gets the engine's raw libgit2 message (English, via src-tauri/src/engine/error.rs:33-35 `message: err.message().to_string()`) rather than a catalogue string.
findings.fix: Send `includeUntracked: true` for the toolbar verb (or expose the option), and make `require_dirty` count exactly what the operation will stash so the precondition cannot pass for a no-op.
findings.testIdea: A `#[cfg(test)]` test in src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs: with only untracked changes and default opts, assert the failure is a catalogue `ErrorPayload` (params["class"] present) rather than an unclassified libgit2 payload; and a frontend test asserting `stashSave` is called with `includeUntracked: true` from the toolbar path.

notes:
Confirmed on every link; I could not find the guard, default or handler the finding missed.

1. Frontend carries no options. `src/composables/useGit.ts:85` is `stash: () => run((id) => commands.stashSave(id, {}))`, and `src/bridges/commands.ts:361` defaults `opts` to `{}`. The toolbar verb at `src/App.vue:631` is enabled by `disabled: !hasRepo` only — no working-copy check — and `src/App.vue:675` runs `runVerb(() => git.stash(), t("shell.toast.stashed"))`. `StashSaveOptions.includeUntracked` exists in `src/bridges/bindings.ts:580` and is used by **no caller**: grepping `stashSave` across all of `src` returns exactly two hits (useGit.ts:85, commands.ts:361), and the Stashes screen (`src/App.vue:356`) is a registered nav entry with no save verb — `docs/04-ui-spec.md:225` lists the pane verbs as apply / apply+delete / delete / copy message. So the toolbar is the only save-stash entry point in the app and it can never send `-u`, despite `docs/01-product-spec.md:186` (CAP-G8-01) requiring "Save a stash, optionally including untracked files".

2. Engine default confirms the flag is what decides. `src-tauri/src/engine/stash.rs:44-58` `StashSaveOptions` is `#[serde(default)]` with `include_untracked: bool` defaulting false, and `stash_flags` (stash.rs:236-247) is the only reader — empty flags unless opts say otherwise.

3. Mixed case behaves exactly as claimed. Tracked modification + untracked file, flags empty: libgit2 stashes the tracked change, `GIT_STATUS_OPT_INCLUDE_UNTRACKED` is never set, so the untracked file stays on disk. `run()` then calls `refreshAll` and `runVerb` pushes `shell.toast.stashed` = "已储藏工作区。" / "Stashed the working copy." (`src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:274`). The toast asserts the whole working copy went away. The untracked file does stay visible in the refreshed working-copy pane, so there is no silent data loss — which is why this stays minor rather than major.

4. Untracked-only case produces the raw libgit2 message, not the catalogue string. This I checked in the actual C source rather than from memory: `libgit2-sys-0.18.8+1.9.7/libgit2/src/libgit2/stash.c:681-708` `git_stash_save_with_opts` calls `ensure_there_are_changes_to_stash(repo, opts->flags)`, whose only untracked-aware behaviour is conditional — stash.c:583-585 adds `GIT_STATUS_OPT_INCLUDE_UNTRACKED | RECURSE_UNTRACKED_DIRS` *only if* `GIT_STASH_INCLUDE_UNTRACKED` is set, and stash.c:596-597 otherwise does `create_error(GIT_ENOTFOUND, "there is nothing to stash.")`. With empty flags and only an untracked file present, that error is raised. `src-tauri/src/engine/stash.rs:121` `?`-propagates it, and `src-tauri/src/engine/error.rs:23-45` classifies `ErrorClass::Stash`/NotFound via the catch-all arm to `ErrorCode::Unclassified` with `message: err.message().to_string()` and `params: Default::default()` — i.e. no `class` param. `require_dirty` at `refs.rs:1777-1791` sets `options.include_untracked(true)` *without* `recurse_untracked_dirs`, so a top-level untracked file still yields a non-empty status list and validation passes — the precondition green-lights a guaranteed no-op. `runVerb` then shows that raw English string via `activity.finish(id, "failed", error.message)` / `reportError`, while the catalogue already has the right answer: `Violation::new(ErrorCode::InvalidRequest, "There is nothing to stash").with_param("class", "save_stash_no_changes")`, and `docs/03-command-surface.md:281` specifies that `SaveStashNoChangesError` for exactly this precondition.

So the validator and the operation genuinely disagree, and the UI cannot express the option that would reconcile them. Severity stays minor: no data loss, no corruption, the remaining untracked file is still listed in the refreshed working-copy pane, and both symptoms are cosmetic-to-mild (a misleading success toast and an untranslated engine string).

findings.title: Pull moves the refs but never invalidates the Compare pane, which keeps showing the pre-pull divergence
findings.evidence: src/composables/useGit.ts:32-34 — `refreshAll` refreshes branches, working copy and history only. The compare composable reloads only when a side's id changes (src/composables/useCompare.ts:103-145, watch at 131-141), and the only other trigger is the error-state retry button (src/components/panes/ComparePane.vue:124, bound at src/App.vue:1641). The seeding watcher returns early once a pair is chosen (src/App.vue:448-461).
findings.repro: Open the compare tab with `main` against `origin/main` (shows 落后 3), then press 工具栏 → 拉取.
findings.expected: The comparison re-reads, so the divergence shown matches the refs the pull just moved (落后 0).
findings.actual: The pane keeps showing 落后 3 under unchanged labels — the exact "last pick's numbers on screen under this pick's labels" that useCompare's own doc comment (src/composables/useCompare.ts:97-101) calls actively misleading. The same holds after a merge or rebase.
findings.fix: Add `compare.reload()` to `refreshAll` (or have useCompare watch the branches store / the refsChanged event), so a ref-moving verb invalidates the comparison.
findings.testIdea: src/composables/useCompare.test.ts: after a refs refresh that changes the tips, assert `historyCompareSummary` is re-requested for the unchanged left/right pair.

notes:
Confirmed; no guard exists on this path. Traced end to end in /tmp/meridian-baseline.

Chain: App.vue:669 (toolbar pull) -> useGit.ts:36-51 run() -> refreshAll at useGit.ts:32-34, which is exactly Promise.all([branches.refresh, workingCopy.refresh, history.refresh]). `comparison` is assigned in only two places in useCompare.ts: reload() line 147 and forRepo() line 172. reload() has exactly two callers repo-wide: the watch([left,right]) on id change (lines 178-185) and App.vue:1641 @refresh.

Checked and eliminated every candidate handler the auditor might have missed:
- forRepo is watched on activeRepoId (App.vue:520-525); a pull does not change repo id, and forRepo early-returns when repo === currentRepo (useCompare.ts:168).
- The seeding watcher App.vue:461 watch([activeTab, branches.allBranches]) DOES fire after a pull (stores/branches.ts:22 builds a fresh array, so identity changes), but seedCompareDefaults bails at line 450 on `if (compare.left.value !== null || compare.right.value !== null) return`. Independently, even if it ran, setBoth only rebuilds RefChoice objects and the useCompare watcher compares `.id`, which is unchanged, so it still would not fire. Two independent confirmations.
- App.vue:1641 @refresh reaches the pane only via ComparePane.vue:124 @retry on ListShell, and ListShell.vue:64-69 renders that button ONLY in the status === "error" arm. So in the healthy data state the Compare pane has no refresh affordance at all (Branches by contrast wires @refresh="branches.refresh()" at App.vue:1602).
- Tab round-trip does not help: RepositoryScreen.vue:85-88 uses v-if/v-else-if per slot so leaving and returning remounts ComparePane, but state lives in App.vue setup, and the activeTab watcher early-returns at line 450 for the same reason.
- The backend event path misses it too: useAppEvents.ts:30-35 handles refsChanged by refreshing only branches and history.
- Grep for reload() repo-wide returns only diff.reload and compare.reload at App.vue:1641; ports.ts:16 confirms there is no stores/compare.ts and useCompare is the only compare surface.

So 落后 3 stays under unchanged labels after pull, fetch, merge, rebase, push or commit, and does not self-heal. Real discrepancy confirmed.

Two evidence corrections that do not change the conclusion: the compare watcher is at useCompare.ts:178-185, not 131-141, and reload() spans 103-163, not 103-145. The cited test file src/composables/useCompare.test.ts does not exist (no test covers this composable), so the testIdea is a proposal, not an edit to an existing suite.

Severity stays minor: read-only display staleness, no corruption or crash, and an escape hatch exists (re-pick a side, which changes the id and reloads). It is at the top of minor because the trigger is a primary toolbar verb and there is no visible way to force a refresh, so the pane fails silently rather than looking stale.

The suggested fix cannot be applied as worded: refreshAll lives in useGit.ts, which never references `compare` (constructed in App.vue:126), so adding compare.reload() there would cross the composition boundary App.vue and layout/ports.ts deliberately keep clean.

findings.title: There is no way to choose, add or inspect a remote, and `defaultRemote` picks one by array order
findings.evidence: src/stores/repos.ts:31-34 — `origin` first, else `remotes[0]`; the list comes from `remotes_model`, which iterates libgit2's name-sorted remote list (src-tauri/src/engine/repository.rs:444-474 and 551-553). Every remote-management command is registered (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:133-146: remote_list/add/rename/delete/set_url/refspec_add/refspec_delete/set_fetch_mode/push/force_push/prune) and `branch_set_upstream/unset_upstream/track_remote/untrack` exists in refs.rs, but none has a wrapper in src/bridges/commands.ts and none is referenced anywhere in src/ (grep returns nothing). The sidebar's 远程 section lists remote-tracking *branches*, not remotes (src/App.vue:271-278, 339-346).
findings.repro: A repo whose remotes are `github` and `origin`: Push always uses `origin` with no way to change it. A repo whose only remote is `github`: Push uses `github` purely because it is first in the sorted list. A branch published through F3 can never be given an upstream.
findings.expected: docs/04 §4.1 lists "set upstream" as a Branch row option and §4.1's toolbar includes push-to and force-push; docs/03 §8 documents the whole remote_* family.
findings.actual: The push target is chosen silently by array order, there is no force-with-lease path from the UI, and no surface can set or clear upstream — which is what makes F3 permanent rather than cosmetic.
findings.fix: Wire `remote_list`/`remote_add`/`remote_set_url`/`remote_delete` and `branch_set_upstream`/`branch_unset_upstream` into a remotes surface plus a branch-row option, and let the three toolbar verbs name their remote (falling back to the tracking remote, then `origin`).
findings.testIdea: A guard in the style of src-tauri/tests/handler_completeness.rs, inverted: every `remote_*` / `branch_*upstream` command registered in lib.rs must appear in src/bridges/commands.ts, so an unreachable command cannot sit silently in the handler list.

notes:
I tried to refute it and could not; every load-bearing claim re-traces exactly.

1) The remote target is picked by order, and nothing else. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/repos.ts:31-34 is verbatim `const defaultRemote = computed<string | null>(() => { const origin = remotes.value.find(r => r.name === "origin"); return origin?.name ?? remotes.value[0]?.name ?? null; })`. All three network verbs read only that value: src/composables/useGit.ts:58 (fetch), :64 (pull), :77 (push). There is no parameter, no picker, no per-call override — `useGit()` exposes `fetch()`, `pull()`, `push(branchName?)` and nothing else.

2) The fallback really is arbitrary array order, and deterministic. The list comes from `repository_remotes_load` → `remotes_model` (src-tauri/src/engine/repository.rs:444-475), which iterates `remote_names` (repository.rs:551-553) → `string_array_names` (repository.rs:543-549) over libgit2's `repo.remotes()`. That helper copies the array verbatim and never sorts, so the order is libgit2's name-sorted list — i.e. alphabetical. So a repo whose only remote is `github` pushes to `github` purely because "g" sorts first, and a repo with `github` + `origin` always pushes to `origin` with no way to change it. Both repro cases in the finding are accurate.

3) The unreachable commands really are unreachable. lib.rs registers remote_list/add/rename/delete/set_url/refspec_add/refspec_delete/set_fetch_mode/fetch/pull/push/force_push/prune/publish_branch and branch_set_upstream/unset_upstream/track_remote/untrack (lib.rs:125-146). `grep -rn "remote_list\|remote_add\|remote_set_url\|remote_delete\|branch_set_upstream\|branch_unset_upstream\|branch_track_remote\|branch_untrack\|remote_force_push" src/` returns nothing — zero hits. src/bridges/commands.ts wraps only four remotes commands (repositoryRemotesLoad, remoteFetch, remotePull, remotePublishBranch at :287-317), and there is no generic invoke-by-name passthrough anywhere in the bridge (every `invoke` call is a literal string).

4) The sidebar section is branches, not remotes. src/App.vue:271-278 builds `remoteRows` by filtering `branches.branches.value` on `branch.isRemote` — remote-tracking refs — and renders them under the section titled `shell.sidebar.remotes` (App.vue:339-346). No remote object is ever displayed, so the user cannot even see which remote the name resolves to, let alone choose one.

5) Upstream cannot be set from the UI. `upstream` appears in components only as read-only display: BranchDetailPane.vue:47/94 and BranchListPane.vue:68/140-141. `remotePublishBranch`'s `setUpstream` defaults to `false` (commands.ts:309-312) and useGit.ts:76 passes only three args — so publish never records an upstream either. That is the mechanism by which the finding's F3 dependency becomes permanent rather than cosmetic.

6) The docs promises are real. docs/04-ui-spec.md:222 lists "set upstream" among the Branch row options; :198 lists push-to and force-push among toolbar verbs; docs/03-command-surface.md §8 "remotes" (heading at :228) documents the whole remote_* family including remote_force_push (:245) and remote_publish_branch (:250). CHANGELOG.md:42-45 advertises "Remotes — add, rename, delete, change URL, edit refspecs, fetch, pull, push, force-push, prune, and publish a branch" as shipped.

7) No guard catches this. handler_completeness.rs walks declared → registered only; its doc comment states its purpose as "Adding a command wrapper without registering it fails here," so a registered-but-unwrapped command is out of scope by construction. changelog_parity.rs checks version headings only. interactionCompleteness.test.ts checks Vue emits and buttons — Rust-side commands have no button, so it cannot see them. The auditor's inverted guard is genuinely absent.

Severity: minor is correct and I am not raising it. Nothing crashes, corrupts, or loses data; fetch/pull/push still reach a real configured remote, and `origin` is the conventional name so the common case is right. The worst case — pushing to an alphabetically-first non-`origin` remote, an outward-facing write the user never chose — requires a multi-remote repo with no `origin`, which is uncommon, and the choice at least follows git's own naming convention rather than a random one. This is a missing-surface/docs-divergence defect, not a broken path.

One precision note that does not change the verdict: the fallback is deterministic alphabetical order (libgit2 sorts in `git_remote_list`), not insertion order. That makes it a stable-but-arbitrary default, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than worth panicking about.

findings.title: `bindings.ts`'s remote types do not match the Rust wire shapes
findings.evidence: src/bridges/bindings.ts:485 declares `RemoteFetchMode` as the 4-value string union used by F1, while the Rust side has two same-named types: src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:56-65 (the options struct) and src-tauri/src/domain/repository.rs:187-196 (a two-value `All|Specified` enum, which is what `repository_remotes_load` actually serialises — as "all"/"specified"). src/bridges/bindings.ts:487-490 declares `PullOptions.mode` as `"merge"|"rebase"|"ffOnly"` while src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:136-147 renames `FastForwardOnly` to `"fastForwardOnly"`, so `"ffOnly"` is not a valid variant. src/bridges/bindings.ts:492-500 declares `fetchUrl`/`pushUrl`, while src-tauri/src/domain/repository.rs:198-208 with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` serialises `url`/`pushurl` — `RepositoryRemote.fetchUrl` is therefore `undefined` at runtime.
findings.repro: Read `repos.remotes[0].fetchUrl` (undefined), or send `remotePull(repo, remote, branch, { mode: "ffOnly" })` — serde rejects the unknown variant. Neither is reachable from the current UI, which is why the drift has gone unnoticed.
findings.expected: The typed mirror in src/bridges/bindings.ts matches the Rust structs exactly (the project rule: keep it in sync by hand until tauri-specta lands, docs/02 §1).
findings.actual: Three independent mismatches, one of which (the mode union at line 485) is the direct cause of the F1 blocker; the drift is invisible because nothing reads these fields yet.
findings.fix: Mirror the Rust shapes: `fetchUrl`→`url`, `pushUrl`→`pushurl`, `fetchMode: "all"|"specified"`, `PullOptions.mode: "merge"|"rebase"|"fastForwardOnly"`; and rename one of the two Rust `RemoteFetchMode` types so the frontend cannot confuse them.
findings.testIdea: src/bridges/bindings.test.ts: a runtime fixture of `repository_remotes_load`'s real JSON (captured from the Rust serialisation) asserted against the declared interface, plus a `expectTypeOf` check on `PullOptions['mode']`.

notes:
Two of the three claimed mismatches are real; the third — the one with the most concrete-sounding repro — is a conflation of two different Rust structs and is wrong.

CONFIRMED (claim 1, RemoteFetchMode): /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/bridges/bindings.ts:485 declares `export type RemoteFetchMode = "default" | "prune" | "tags" | "pruneTags"`. No Rust type produces those four strings. The Rust side has two distinct same-named types: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:58 is a *struct* `RemoteFetchMode { prune: bool, tags: TagFetch, depth: Option<i32> }` under `#[serde(default, rename_all = "camelCase")]` — an object, not a string; /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/domain/repository.rs:189 is a *two-value enum* `All | Specified` under `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` — serialising as `"all"`/`"specified"`. I confirmed the enum is the one actually on the wire for the command in question: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/commands/repository.rs:498 gives `repository_remotes_load` an output of `RepositoryRemotes`, whose `remotes` are `domain::repository::RepositoryRemote`, and /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/repository.rs:452-456 populates `fetch_mode` from that enum (`All` if any refspec contains `*`, else `Specified`). So `RepositoryRemote.fetchMode` (bindings.ts:498, typed by the wrong union) is `"all"`/`"specified"` at runtime — never a member of the declared union. No serde escape hatch rescues this: I grepped both Rust files for `alias`, `untagged`, and `deserialize_with` and found none.

CONFIRMED (claim 2, PullOptions.mode): bindings.ts:488 declares `mode?: "merge" | "rebase" | "ffOnly"`. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:136-147 is `enum PullMode { Merge, Rebase, FastForwardOnly }` under `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, so the wire values are `"merge"`, `"rebase"`, `"fastForwardOnly"`. `"ffOnly"` is not a variant. Latent, though — the only live call path is /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useGit.ts:66 `commands.remotePull(id, remote)`, which uses the `opts = {}` default, and /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:148-153 marks `PullOptions` `#[serde(default)]`, so no bad variant is ever sent today. The finding's own "not reachable from the current UI" caveat is accurate for this one.

REFUTED (claim 3, fetchUrl/pushUrl): the auditor attributed `engine/remotes.rs:69-77 RemoteInfo`'s field names (`url`, `pushurl`) to `domain/repository.rs:199-209 RepositoryRemote`. Those are different structs serving different commands. `RemoteInfo` is what `remote_list`/`remote_add`/`remote_set_url` return (/tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:1631-1638) — and it has no TypeScript mirror at all (grep for `RemoteInfo` in bindings.ts returns nothing), so it cannot drift against a declaration that doesn't exist. `RepositoryRemote`, the type behind `repository_remotes_load`, declares `fetch_url`/`push_url` under `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` at /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/domain/repository.rs:199-209, which serialises as exactly `fetchUrl`/`pushUrl` — precisely what bindings.ts:494-495 declares. The repro "Read `repos.remotes[0].fetchUrl` (undefined)" is false; /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/repos.ts:48 assigns that payload straight through and the field is populated correctly.

Severity stays minor, on the finding's own reasoning and independently verified: the two live remote paths are `remoteFetch` (blocked by F1) and `remotePull` with an empty `opts`, so nothing in the current UI reads the drifted fields. This is drift in a hand-maintained type mirror, which docs/02 §1 makes a project rule, plus a trap for the next caller — not a live defect.

One correction the parent must carry forward: the finding's proposed fix would *introduce* a bug by renaming `fetchUrl`→`url` and `pushUrl`→`pushurl` in `RepositoryRemote`. That would break the one pair of fields that are currently correct.

findings.title: Commit composer survives a repository switch, so the next commit amends the wrong repository's HEAD
findings.evidence: src/App.vue:935-938 declares composerSubject/composerBody/composerAmend/composerSignOff; the only place they are cleared is App.vue:1005-1007 inside commitNow() after a successful commit. The existing repository watch App.vue:520-524 (`watch(activeRepoId, (id) => compare.forRepo(id ?? null))`) resets compare but nothing resets the composer. commitNow() (App.vue:987-1014) sends whatever is in those refs to workingCopy.commit -> commitAmend/commitCreate (src/stores/workingCopy.ts:68-84) with repo = repos.selectedId, i.e. the NEW repository. The switcher is always enabled (App.vue:1417 `:locked="false"`), so the switch is reachable mid-edit.
findings.repro: Open repository A, type subject "fix parser" in the working-copy composer, tick Amend (can-amend is true because A has a HEAD). Without committing, use the sidebar RepoSwitcher to switch to repository B. Stage any file in B and press Commit. Expected: B's commit uses B's own composer (empty subject, Amend off). Actual: `commit_amend` is invoked against B with message "fix parser", rewriting B's HEAD commit.
findings.expected: Switching the selected repository resets the composer (subject, body, amend, sign-off) — no input meant for repository A can be submitted against repository B.
findings.actual: composerSubject/composerBody/composerAmend/composerSignOff are shell-level refs that outlive the repository selection, so A's message and A's amend tick are applied to B, silently rewriting an unrelated repository's HEAD commit.
findings.fix: In the existing `watch(activeRepoId, ...)` at App.vue:520-524, clear composerSubject.value = "", composerBody.value = "", composerAmend.value = false, composerSignOff.value = false (and selectedPath.value = null, conflictedOnly.value = false) whenever the id actually changes.
findings.testIdea: New src/App.test.ts: mount App with two repositories in the repos store, set the composer subject via the WorkingCopyPane `update:subject` event and tick amend, change repos.selectedId, then assert the emitted `commit` payload (or the composer props) has an empty message and amend === false.

notes:
CONFIRMED as a real defect; no missed guard, but the impact wording is overstated and the suggested fix is broken.

Trace (App.vue is the mounted root in main.ts — `createApp(App)...mount("#app")`, no RouterView, screens swapped by `v-if`/`v-else-if` on routeName, so its setup scope never tears down on a repo param change):

1. `composerSubject`/`composerBody`/`composerAmend`/`composerSignOff` are plain `ref`s at /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:935-938, created once per app lifetime.
2. The only place they are cleared is App.vue:1005-1007 inside `commitNow()` after a successful commit. (`composerSignOff` is not cleared even there — a separate one-line leak the finding did not mention.)
3. The five `watch()` calls in App.vue (461, 520, 958, 1075, 1118, 1390) — only 520 watches `activeRepoId`, and its body is `compare.forRepo(id ?? null)` only. Nothing resets the composer, `selectedPath`, or `conflictedOnly`.
4. Switch path: App.vue:1417 passes `:locked="false"` to AppSidebar; RepoSwitcher.vue:61-63 `choose()` emits `switchRepo` with no confirmation and no dirty check (the only `locked` uses are `Popover :open` / `:disabled` on the trigger button). It lands on `openRepository(id)` (App.vue:526-529) → `repositories.select(id)` + `navigate(repositoryPath(id))`. Route param changes → `activeRepoId` (App.vue:196) changes → component instance and its refs survive.
5. `commitNow()` (App.vue:987-1014) calls `workingCopy.commit({ message, amend: composerAmend.value, signOff: composerSignOff.value })`. Note the finding cites stores/workingCopy.ts:68-84 for `repo = repos.selectedId`; that resolution is actually in /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:47-52 (`activeRepo()` → `repos.selectedId`) — the store only takes `repo` as a parameter. Either way the id is read at click time, so it is B.
6. Commit button stays enabled: CommitComposer.vue:67-72 `canCommit` = `amend && canAmend && (subject !== "" || staged > 0)`, and App.vue:1482 `:can-amend="selectedRepo?.headOid != null"` re-evaluates against B. So a leftover subject + ticked amend is one click from rewriting B's HEAD.
7. Rust side offers no mitigation: engine/index.rs:603-608 only refuses an amend when HEAD is unborn; there is no cross-repo or unpushed-HEAD check (`ValidateUnpushedCommits` appears in docs/03-command-surface.md:138 but is not implemented anywhere in src-tauri).

Why severity drops from blocker to major:
- "Silently" is wrong. After the switch the composer still renders the stale subject in the input, the amend checkbox is still ticked, and CommitComposer.vue:106 swaps the header to the `commit.amendTitle` label; the staged-count chip (CommitComposer.vue:108-112) already shows B's count. The mis-targeted state is on screen before the click, not hidden.
- The non-amend create path additionally requires staging a file in B (canCommit needs `subject !== "" && staged > 0`), so it needs two deliberate acts, not one.
- Damage is recoverable: engine/index.rs:684-691 moves HEAD by hand specifically so the reflog gets a `commit (amend): <summary>` entry, so B's original HEAD survives in the object store.
- It needs an unusual sequence (leave an unsaved composer, switch repos, then commit) — not a load-time or everyday-flow failure.

The defect itself is real and worth fixing: a composer bound to no repository can be submitted against a different one, which is a data-affecting mis-targeting bug in a git GUI.

One correction to the proposed fix, which would otherwise be a startup crash: it says to clear the refs "in the existing `watch(activeRepoId, ...)` at App.vue:520-524". That watch uses `{ immediate: true }` (App.vue:523), and Vue invokes an immediate watcher synchronously during `watch()` — but `composerSubject` is a `const` declared 415 lines later at App.vue:935.
