Touching `composerSubject.value` in that callback throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'composerSubject' before initialization` on every app start.

findings.title: HEAD is never re-read after a checkout, so the toolbar's Push and Commit & Push publish the wrong branch
findings.evidence: RepoInfo (headBranch/headOid/state) is only written by repos.upsert, which is called solely from open/init/clone (src/stores/repos.ts:36-43, 61, 78, 124). branches.checkout (src/stores/branches.ts:60-70) runs branch_checkout then refresh() of the branch list only — it never updates RepoInfo, and useGit.refreshAll (src/composables/useGit.ts:32-34) refreshes branches/working-copy/history only. The engine command that would fix this, `repository_refresh` (src-tauri/src/commands/repository.rs:259-302, registered at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:69), has NO bridge in src/bridges/commands.ts and no entry in src/bridges/bindings.ts, so nothing in the UI can call it. Consumers of the stale value: windowSubtitle (App.vue:220-227, renders "On {branch}"), RepoSwitcher head label (src/layout/RepoSwitcher.vue:85), toolbar pushReason/detachedHead (App.vue:604-610), can-amend (App.vue:1483). git.push() with no name reads repos.selected?.headBranch (src/composables/useGit.ts:75-84) and the engine pushes that named ref: engine/remotes.rs:982 builds refspec `refs/heads/{branch}:refs/heads/{branch}`.
findings.repro: In repository R on branch main, use the branch pane to check out feature (or `git switch -c feature` in a terminal). Press Push on the toolbar (or Commit & Push on the commit split button, App.vue:1022). Expected: `feature` is published. Actual: headBranch is still "main", so remote_publish_branch is called with branch="main" and refs/heads/main is pushed; feature's commits never reach the remote and the success toast fires anyway. Established with the git CLI in /tmp/audit-shell/gitlab: with HEAD on `feature`, `git push origin main:main` leaves origin at refs/heads/main=3f2a300 (the pre-feature commit) and pushes nothing of feature.
findings.expected: After a checkout (in-app or external) the shell's repository model reflects the new HEAD, so the window subtitle, the switcher and every push path name the branch that is actually checked out.
findings.actual: headBranch/headOid/state are frozen at open time; after a checkout the subtitle still reads "On main", and the toolbar Push / Commit & Push publish `main` while the user is on `feature` — a silent wrong-ref push to a remote, reported as success.
findings.fix: Add a `repositoryRefresh(repo)` bridge for the already-registered `repository_refresh` and call it (or re-read RepoInfo via it) after every command that can move HEAD: branch checkout/create/rename/delete, commit/amend, merge/rebase/continue/abort, fetch/pull/push, discard. Alternatively have useGit.run refresh the RepoInfo of the repo it acted on and upsert it.
findings.testIdea: New src/stores/repos.test.ts: with a fake commands module, call branches.checkout(repo,'feature') and assert repos.selected.headBranch === 'feature' after the flow settles (currently fails); plus a unit assertion that useGit.push() passes the post-checkout headBranch.

notes:
I could not refute it; every link in the chain checks out in /tmp/meridian-baseline.

(1) RepoInfo (src/bridges/bindings.ts:70-80) is written only by repos.upsert, which is called only from open/init/clone (src/stores/repos.ts:61,78,124). `grep -rn "upsert" src/` returns exactly those three plus the definition — no other writer.
(2) branches.checkout/checkoutRemote/create/rename/remove (src/stores/branches.ts:48-110) each do `await refresh(repo)`, which only re-reads the branch list via branchList.
(3) useGit.refreshAll (src/composables/useGit.ts:32-34) touches branches/workingCopy/history only; run() (36-51) calls nothing else.
(4) The event bus is not a missed back door: useAppEvents (src/composables/useAppEvents.ts:24-42) refreshes branches+history on refsChanged and workingCopy on workingCopyChanged, and the reposChanged case is an explicit no-op with the comment "The store that ran the command already updated itself". RefsChanged is emitted only from in-app commands (commands/{branches,commit,integrate,refs}.rs); there is no .git/HEAD watcher in src-tauri.
(5) repository_refresh is registered (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:69) and returns a fresh RepoInfo via engine::repository::reopen+info (commands/repository.rs:259-302), but `grep repositoryRefresh src/` is empty and commands.ts exposes only repositoryOpen/Init/Clone/CloneDestination/Discover/RemotesLoad — so nothing in the UI can call it.
(6) The wrong-ref write is real: toolbar Push (App.vue:671-672) and Commit & Push (App.vue:1022) both call `git.push()` with no name, which reads `repos.selected?.headBranch` (useGit.ts:79); the engine builds `refs/heads/{branch}:refs/heads/{branch}` from that name and then sets tracking config for it (engine/remotes.rs:982,1002) with no HEAD fallback. Confirmed by reading publish_branch directly.
(7) The toast cannot warn the user: `shell.toast.pushed` is "Pushed {branch}." (i18n/locales/parts/en/diff.ts:293) but the toolbar passes no branch param, so it never names what was pushed.

Additional consequence the finding understates: App.vue:773 `renameBranchFlow` falls back to `selectedRepo.headBranch` when the pane has no selection, and the toolbar Branch > Rename menu (App.vue:668) invokes it with no preset — so Rename pre-fills, and on confirm renames, the branch the user is NOT on. So this is a silent wrong-target *write*, not only a wrong push.

Severity corrected blocker -> major. Why not blocker: the push is non-forced (`refs/heads/x:refs/heads/x`, no `+`), so it cannot destroy remote history or clobber a diverged branch; in the common `git switch -c feature` case main is already in sync with origin and the push is a silent no-op that costs the user a false success and an unpublished feature branch, both recoverable. Actually publishing unintended commits requires the extra precondition that the stale branch is ahead of its remote (realistic when a user walks away from a WIP branch — that variant is genuinely bad and needs a remote history rewrite). Likewise the rename is local and reversible with `git branch -m`. That is severe, silent, and hits the most-used toolbar verbs, but it is not irreversible corruption, so major is the right grade; I would escalate to blocker only if the push path were force-capable.

Scope note on the proposed fix: it only covers HEAD moves made in-app. Since no watcher on .git/HEAD exists and RefsChanged is not emitted for external changes, the repro's external `git switch` half stays broken even after that fix. The push path must resolve HEAD just-in-time, not from a cached field.

findings.title: Activity entries are labelled with the raw i18n key shell.activity.genericOperation, which exists in neither catalogue
findings.evidence: App.vue:575-589 runVerb has `labelKey = "shell.activity.genericOperation"` (App.vue:578) as its default, and all fourteen call sites (App.vue:399, 496, 666, 669, 672, 675, 802, 808, 1022, 1027, 1464, 1465, 1509, 1510) omit the third argument, so that is the only key ever recorded. ActivityScreen.labelOf renders `entry.label ?? t(entry.labelKey)` (src/components/screens/ActivityScreen.vue:30-32, 76). The `shell.activity` block (src/i18n/locales/parts/en/diff.ts:333-349, src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:313-329) contains title/subtitle/running/idle/state/clear/nothingToClear/empty/emptyCaption/privacy and no genericOperation. Verified against the catalogues by walking both message trees (650 leaf keys each, identical sets) and against the installed vue-i18n 11.4.14: a missing key resolves to the key string itself.
findings.repro: Open a repository and press Fetch (or Pull/Push/Stash). Open the toolbar activity chip. Expected: each row names the operation ("Fetch"). Actual: every row's name renders literally as `shell.activity.genericOperation`, in both zh-CN and en.
findings.expected: Each activity row shows a human name for the operation; a missing catalogue entry is caught before shipping.
findings.actual: t('shell.activity.genericOperation') returns the key verbatim, so the Activity screen lists every operation under the literal string `shell.activity.genericOperation`.
findings.fix: Add `genericOperation` to the `shell.activity` block in both catalogue slices, and give each runVerb call site its own key (shell.activity.fetch, .pull, .push, …) so the list is actually informative.
findings.testIdea: Extend src/i18n/catalog.test.ts with a scan of src/**/*.{ts,vue} for labelKey defaults and t() literals, asserting i18n.global.te(key, 'zh-CN') && te(key,'en') for each; that test currently fails on shell.activity.genericOperation, shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle and shell.dialogue.compareTargetTitle.

notes:
CONFIRMED. I tried to refute it via every override I could find and there is no guard.

Path traced line by line against /tmp/meridian-baseline:
1. App.vue:575-579 — `async function runVerb(action, success, labelKey = "shell.activity.genericOperation")`. `grep -rn genericOperation src` returns exactly one hit in the whole tree (App.vue:578); the key exists nowhere else in code.
2. All 15 call sites (399, 496-499, 666, 669, 672, 675, 802, 808, 1022, 1027, 1464, 1465, 1509, 1510 plus the multi-line one at 496) pass exactly two arguments. None passes a labelKey, so the default is the only key ever recorded.
3. The override the auditor could have missed is real but does not help: ActivityScreen.vue:30-32 is `entry.label ?? t(entry.labelKey)`. `entry.label` is only set by `useActivity.start(labelKey, label?)` (useActivity.ts:45-58), and `activity.start(labelKey)` at App.vue:580 is the ONLY `start()` call in the repo (`grep -rn "activity\.start(" src` → one hit) — no caller supplies the second argument, so `entry.label` is always `undefined` and the `??` always falls through to `t()`.
4. No runtime rescue: src/i18n/index.ts:47-56 creates the i18n instance with no `missing` handler, no postTranslation transform, and `missingWarn`/`fallbackWarn` gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV`, so a missing key is silent in release.
5. Key genuinely absent from both catalogues. I loaded the real runtime objects (copied the locale tree to /tmp/shell03-probe/i18n/ with `.ts` import specifiers fixed, imported through node's type-stripping) rather than trusting the source text: 650 leaf keys per locale, key sets identical (only-in-en: [], only-in-zh: []), and `shell.activity.genericOperation` resolves to `undefined` in both. NOTE on a near-miss I chased and dismissed: `parts/en/diff.ts:333` prints `activity: {` at 2-space indent and looks like a top-level sibling of `shell`, while zh-CN's is at `parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:313` at 4-space — that would have been an en/zh path asymmetry. It is not: an indentation-only difference, both are nested inside `shell` (`en.shell` and `zh.shell` both list `activity` last). No asymmetry.
6. Against the installed vue-i18n 11.4.14 with the project's own config (legacy:false, locale zh-CN, fallbackLocale en): `te('shell.activity.genericOperation')` → false and `t(...)` → the string `"shell.activity.genericOperation"` verbatim, in BOTH zh-CN and en. So the repro is exact: every row of the Activity screen renders the raw key.
7. Reachability confirmed end to end: `src/router/routes.ts:32` declares `{ name: "activity", path: "/activity" }`, App.vue:1403 passes `:activity="activitySummary"` to the toolbar, `onToolbarRun` handles `"activity"` at App.vue:692, and App.vue:1709-1713 renders `<ActivityScreen :entries="activity.entries.value" :running="...">`. Not dead code.
8. Why CI is green: src/i18n/catalog.test.ts only diffs en against zh-CN key paths and byte-identical values. It never checks a key against a call site, and the `zh-CN.ts: Catalog` type annotation only catches en↔zh drift — a key missing from BOTH catalogues is invisible to both guards.

Two corroborations beyond the finding as written:
- The doc comment at App.vue:567-573 states the labelKey contract ("passed rather than the rendered text so the entry re-labels itself when the language changes") — the plumbing was built and documented, then no caller ever used the third argument. The signature of shipped-but-unwired.
- The same missing-key class exists at `shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle` and `shell.dialogue.compareTargetTitle` (App.vue:470-471). I confirmed both are absent from both catalogues. So this is a three-instance pattern, not a one-off.

Severity: major stands. A primary, reachable screen renders an internal i18n key to the user in every locale for every operation recorded, and the feature's entire purpose (an informative operation log) is defeated — but nothing crashes, no data is lost, and the rows still carry state, timestamps and error text, so the list remains usable. That is above minor (a visible defect on a shipped screen) and short of blocker (no functional loss, no security or correctness consequence).

findings.title: About screen: "Check for updates" is permanently disabled and the panel says "Checking…" forever when auto-check is off or the build cannot self-update
findings.evidence: check starts as {status:'loading'} (src/composables/useApp.ts:52). start() (useApp.ts:157-164) returns before checkForUpdates() when `!autoCheck.value || !canSelfUpdate.value`, leaving check at 'loading' forever. canSelfUpdate requires app_info.canSelfUpdate (useApp.ts:90-92), which Rust sets to `configured && profile == BuildProfile::Release` (src-tauri/src/commands/app.rs:111-113) — false for every `pnpm tauri dev` build and any build without an update endpoint. AboutScreen's updateSummary maps status 'loading' to {kind:'loading'} (src/components/screens/AboutScreen.vue:109) and the Check button is `:disabled="updateSummary.kind === 'loading' || ..."` (AboutScreen.vue:243-250).
findings.repro: Settings → About → turn off "Check automatically on launch" (or run the debug build). Navigate away and back to About. Expected: the panel offers "Check for updates" and the user can press it. Actual: the card shows "Checking…" / "Asking the project's release page for the newest version." next to "Never checked.", and the Check button stays disabled with no way to trigger a check or learn why.
findings.expected: A check that was deliberately skipped (auto-check off, or a build that cannot act on the answer) leaves the panel in a settled state where "Check for updates" is clickable and the unavailable/debug-build explanation is shown.
findings.actual: The initial 'loading' state is never replaced, so the UI reports a check that is not happening and permanently disables the only control that could start one.
findings.fix: In start(), when the check is skipped set check.value = { status: 'empty' } (or a new 'skipped' kind) instead of leaving 'loading'; keep the button disabled only while a real request is in flight, and surface the notConfigured/debugBuild reason from a fresh checkForUpdates() call.
findings.testIdea: src/components/screens/AboutScreen.test.ts (exists): add a case rendering with `check: {status:'empty'}` and assert the Check button is not disabled; and a useApp test asserting start() with autoCheck=false leaves check.status !== 'loading'.

notes:
Confirmed by re-trace and by mounting the component under the repo's own vitest.

Chain verified: useApp.ts:52 initialises `check` to `{status:'loading'}`; start() (useApp.ts:157-164) returns early when `!autoCheck || !canSelfUpdate` and `checkForUpdates()` is the only writer of `check` (setAutoCheck at useApp.ts:234-241 does not re-trigger it), so the ref is stuck on `loading` until a full app restart. canSelfUpdate (useApp.ts:90-92) is `configured && profile == BuildProfile::Release` (src-tauri/src/commands/app.rs:113), so debug builds are stuck too. AboutScreen.vue:109 maps loading -> {kind:'loading'} and AboutScreen.vue:246 disables the button for kinds 'loading'/'unavailable'. Empirically: mounting with check {status:'loading'} renders `disabled=""`, label "Checking…", body "Asking the project's release page for the newest version." next to "Never checked.", and a synthetic click emits no 'check' event. Not dev-only: build.rs derives MERIDIAN_REPO_SLUG from origin, so a real release build has canSelfUpdate=true and the sole trigger is the user-facing "Check automatically on launch" switch.

Two errors in the finding's fix section, not in its diagnosis:
1. The proposed `check.value = {status:'empty'}` does not work — AboutScreen.vue:112 also maps empty to loading (`if (state.status === "empty") return { kind: "loading" }`). Verified: check {status:'empty'} renders the identical DISABLED / "Checking…" panel, so the suggested test would fail against the snapshot as written.
2. The expectation "the panel offers Check for updates" is wrong for builds that cannot self-update: when the check does run and Rust returns NotConfigured/UnsupportedInDebugBuild, kind is 'unavailable' and the button is disabled by design (verified: notConfigured => DISABLED | Check for updates). The correct expectation there is the already-shipped debug/not-configured explanation, not an enabled button.

Severity stays major: user-visible false state plus a permanently dead control with no in-app recovery, but no data loss or security impact, and confined to the About panel.

findings.title: "Refresh repository" refreshes three stores and skips the compare pane and the remotes list
findings.evidence: The ⌘⇧R binding (App.vue:1374) and the palette's `action:refresh` handler (App.vue:1340-1346) both run only `Promise.all([workingCopy.refresh(), branches.refresh(), history.refresh()])`. Compare only reloads when left/right ids change (src/composables/useCompare.ts:178-185) or via the pane's own @refresh (App.vue:1641); repos.remotes is loaded only by open/init/clone/select (src/stores/repos.ts:45-54, 92) and never by the refresh action. seedCompareDefaults (App.vue:448-459) returns early once left/right are set, so a branch deletion does not clear them.
findings.repro: On the Compare tab pick base main / target feature, note the ahead/behind counts. In a terminal run `git branch -D feature` in that repository. Press ⌘⇧R (or ⌘⇧P → "Refresh repository"). Expected: the comparison reflects the new ref set (or is cleared, since a side no longer exists). Actual: the pane keeps the old merge base and counts, and its pickers still name the deleted ref, with no indication the data is stale. Same for remotes: add a remote in a terminal and ⌘⇧R will not show it, so the toolbar's defaultRemote and the fetch/pull/push enablement stay wrong.
findings.expected: "Refresh repository" reloads everything the shell displays for the selected repository, including the compare inputs and the remotes model (the Rust `repository_refresh` command exists for exactly this and emits RefsChanged + WorkingCopyChanged).
findings.actual: Two of the repository's displayed models (compare, remotes) keep pre-refresh data, and no error or hint is shown.
findings.fix: Have the refresh action call the engine's repository_refresh (add the missing bridge), then repos.loadRemotes(id) and compare.reload(); or at minimum re-derive compare's inputs from the freshly loaded branch list and drop sides whose ref no longer exists.
findings.testIdea: New src/composables/useCompare.test.ts: set left/right to refs, delete one from the injected branch list, invoke the shell refresh path, and assert compare.reload() ran (or comparison was cleared) — currently no reload is triggered.

notes:
Confirmed; every citation verified against /tmp/meridian-baseline, and I found no guard the auditor missed.

(1) App.vue:1374 (the ⌘⇧R binding) and App.vue:1340-1346 (palette `action:refresh`) are identical three-call bodies: `Promise.all([workingCopy.refresh(), branches.refresh(), history.refresh()])`. Neither touches compare, neither calls repos.loadRemotes, neither invokes repository_refresh.

(2) useCompare.ts:178-185 — the sole watcher fires only when `nextLeft?.id !== previousLeft?.id || nextRight?.id !== previousRight?.id`. Re-picking the *same* ref is a no-op. compare.reload() has exactly one caller: App.vue:1641, the ComparePane `@refresh`.

(3) seedCompareDefaults (App.vue:449-450) returns early when either side is non-null, so the `watch([activeTab, () => branches.allBranches.value], seedCompareDefaults)` at App.vue:461 fires on a branch deletion and does nothing. Confirmed.

(4) stores/repos.ts: `loadRemotes` is invoked only from open(:63), init(:80), select(:92), clone(:126). No refresh path. Confirmed.

(5) useAppEvents.ts:30-40 routes `refsChanged` to branches.refresh + history.refresh only; compare and remotes are not subscribers. No setInterval, no visibilitychange, no fs-watcher anywhere in src/ to compensate. Confirmed.

Three things strengthen the finding beyond what was reported:

(a) The compare pane has NO manual escape hatch. ComparePane's only `emit('refresh')` is ListShell's `@retry` (ComparePane.vue:124), and ListShell renders that button solely inside `v-else-if="status === 'error'"` (ListShell.vue:64-70). In the normal data state the user cannot force a compare reload at all short of switching repositories — so "press the pane's own refresh" is not an available workaround.

(b) The hole is not limited to the terminal-`git branch -D` repro. The in-app delete path has it too: App.vue:827 deleteBranch → branches.remove → store.refresh → branch_delete emits RefsChanged (src-tauri/src/commands/branches.rs:129) → useAppEvents refreshes branches + history, never compare. Likewise a plain `git fetch` from a terminal, an extremely common workflow, leaves the compare pane's origin/main ahead/behind stale with no error.

(c) The Rust `repository_refresh` command exists (registered src-tauri/src/lib.rs:69, implemented src-tauri/src/commands/repository.rs:296, emits RefsChanged + WorkingCopyChanged) and is required by docs/03-command-surface.md:78 and docs/04-ui-spec.md:252 (S2 shell) — but `grep repositoryRefresh src/` returns nothing. It has zero TypeScript callers. That is why every refresh reads through the long-lived `git2::Repository` handle in state.rs's registry, never re-opened via engine::repository::reopen, so even the branch list can read stale refdb state after an external packed-refs change. The auditor's "add the missing bridge" is literally correct.

Severity stays major rather than dropping to minor: nothing is corrupted on disk and there is no crash, but the pane displays wrong ahead/behind counts under labels naming a ref set the user can no longer act on — the exact "mislabelled view" the composable's own header comment says reload exists to prevent — with no error surfaced and no in-pane recovery. Not a blocker: no data loss, no security impact, and recovery is possible by switching repositories and back.

findings.title: Global shortcuts fire while a modal dialogue is open, queueing an invisible second dialogue
findings.evidence: useKeyboardShortcuts (src/layout/useShell.ts:159-176) has no modal/context test; its only guard is `if (!binding.allowInInput && isTextTarget(event.target)) continue` (useShell.ts:167, isTextTarget at 148-153 tests INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT/contentEditable only). None of the five bindings sets allowInInput (App.vue:1370-1376). DialogueShell focuses either [data-autofocus] or focusables()[0] (src/components/dialogues/DialogueShell.vue:71-77); ConfirmDialog marks a *button* as autofocus (src/components/dialogues/ConfirmDialog.vue:67-74) and ChooseBranchDialog has no data-autofocus, so focusables()[0] is DialogueShell's close <button> (ChooseBranchDialog.vue:86). A focused button is not a text target, so every shortcut still runs while those modals are up.
findings.repro: Open a repository and use the branch pane → Check out branch… (ChooseBranchDialog open, focus on a button). Press ⌘⇧B. Expected: the shortcut is ignored while a modal owns the window. Actual: newBranchFlow() runs, askDialogue pushes a second request behind the visible one, and the New-branch prompt appears out of nowhere once the picker is resolved/cancelled. Pressing ⌘, in the same state navigates the app to Settings while the modal stays on top.
findings.expected: While a modal dialogue is open (or the palette is open), global shortcuts do nothing — the modal owns the keyboard.
findings.actual: ⌘K/⌘⇧P/⌘,/⌘⇧R/⌘⇧B all run with a dialogue on screen; ⌘⇧B silently queues a dialogue that the user never asked to open, and ⌘, navigates under the modal.
findings.fix: In the shell's keydown handler, skip when `shell.activeDialogue.value !== null` (and when paletteMode !== null); or gate registration on there being no active modal, which is also what makes the shortcut table testable.
findings.testIdea: New src/layout/useShell.test.ts: register a binding, call askDialogue(...) to make activeDialogue non-null, dispatch a keydown for the bound key on a focused button, and assert binding.run was not called.

notes:
Confirmed by full re-read plus a passing reproduction; I found no guard the auditor missed.

Path trace: useKeyboardShortcuts's onKeydown (src/layout/useShell.ts:160-172) has exactly one skip — `if (!binding.allowInInput && isTextTarget(event.target)) continue` (line 167) — and isTextTarget (148-153) only tests INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT/contentEditable. None of the five bindings in App.vue:1370-1376 sets allowInInput. The listener is registered on document in the BUBBLE phase (useShell.ts:174). DialogueShell registers its own document keydown in the CAPTURE phase (DialogueShell.vue:73) but calls stopPropagation() only for Escape (DialogueShell.vue:44) and otherwise only intercepts Tab; every other key therefore continues to the bubble-phase shell handler. I enumerated every keydown registration in the app — useShell.ts:174, DialogueShell.vue:73, Popover.vue:38, BlamePane.vue:81, CommandPalette.vue:77 and :114 — and none swallows command chords.

Focus claims verified: data-autofocus appears only at ConfirmDialog.vue:67/74 (a <button>) and PromptDialog.vue:95 (an <input>). ChooseBranchDialog.vue has none, so DialogueShell.vue:75-76 falls back to focusables()[0], which is the header close <button> at DialogueShell.vue:102-110. Neither tag is a text target.

Targets have no guards either: newBranchFlow (App.vue:713) calls askDialogue unconditionally, openPalette (App.vue:1264) is a bare assignment, and navigate (src/router/index.ts:79) has no context check. askDialogue (useShell.ts:114-118) unconditionally appends to the queue; activeDialogue is queue[0] (useShell.ts:112) and DialogueHost renders exactly that (App.vue:1753-1758), so once the visible dialogue settles the queued request becomes active and pops. "Invisible" is literal — queuedDialogues (useShell.ts:191) is computed but referenced nowhere else in src/.

Empirical: in a scratch copy of the snapshot (/tmp/sh06-verify, src/sh06.repro.test.ts) both tests pass. (1) Unit, the test the finding proposes: register {key:"b",meta,shift}, call askDialogue, dispatch keydown on a focused <button> — run() fires once. (2) Integration: mount the real ChooseBranchDialog with the app's i18n, stub offsetParent (jsdom implements no layout, so focusables() would otherwise return []), dispatch ⌘⇧B — activeElement is BUTTON and run() fires.

Exposure is narrower than the finding implies but not absent: PromptDialog autofocuses an input, so the five shortcuts are already suppressed there (accidentally, via isTextTarget). The confirmed gap is ConfirmDialog (autofocus on a button — Cancel when danger, Confirm otherwise) and ChooseBranchDialog.

Two accuracy corrections that do not refute: (a) the "race" category is wrong — there is no timing dependence, the bug is 100% reproducible and is a missing precedence/keyboard-context guard; (b) the fix's testability claim understates a real obstacle — useShell.ts calls window.matchMedia(...).addEventListener(...) at module scope (line 23), so a new src/layout/useShell.test.ts fails at import under jsdom with "window.matchMedia is not a function" unless the stub is installed before the import rather than in beforeAll (I hit this). Separately, paletteMode is a local ref in App.vue:1261, not shell state, so the palette half of the guard cannot live inside useShell.ts as the fix is worded.

Severity stays major: no destructive shortcut misfires (⌘⇧R only refreshes, ⌘⇧B only queues a prompt), so it is not a blocker, but it is reachable through ordinary use, injects app state the user never requested, and the stray prompt appears on its own once the visible dialogue resolves.

findings.title: Repository can be switched mid-operation (locked hard-coded false, useGit.busy unread) and the in-flight result is applied to the new repository
findings.evidence: App.vue:1417 passes `:locked="false"` to AppSidebar, whose RepoSwitcher documents the prop as "Disables the switcher while a blocking operation runs" (src/layout/RepoSwitcher.vue:19-22, 72, 77). useGit exposes `busy` (src/composables/useGit.ts:26) and it is read nowhere in the app (grep finds only its declaration). useGit.run captures the id but then calls refreshAll(id) (useGit.ts:36-51), and each store refresh writes shared state with no check that the repo it was issued for is still selected: src/stores/branches.ts:24-39, src/stores/workingCopy.ts:26-33, src/stores/history.ts:85-95. The event path does guard — useAppEvents.ts:31-39 returns unless `event.payload.repo === repos.selectedId` — so the two paths disagree about the hazard.
findings.repro: Open repositories A and B. Select A and press Fetch against a slow/large remote (or clone a large repository and switch away while it runs). Switch to B via the RepoSwitcher. B's lists load. When A's request resolves, refreshAll(A) overwrites branches/working-copy/history with A's data while the route, window title and switcher all say B. Selecting a file in that stale working-copy list then calls wc_stage_paths(B, [A's path]).
findings.expected: A response for repository A must never be written into state that is displaying repository B; the switcher should be disabled (with a reason) while a blocking operation runs.
findings.actual: The response is applied unconditionally, so the sidebar, working-copy list and history show the previous repository's contents under the new repository's title, and a subsequent action derived from that list targets the wrong repository.
findings.fix: Guard every store write with the repo it was issued for (drop the response when `repo !== repos.selectedId`), and pass `:locked="git.busy || repositories.busy || activity.running.length > 0"` to AppSidebar so the switcher stops claiming it is fine to switch.
findings.testIdea: New src/stores/branches.test.ts: make branchList resolve for A after B, call refresh(A) then refresh(B), await both, and assert store.branches holds B's branches (currently holds A's).

notes:
CONFIRMED — every cited location is accurate and no guard exists anywhere on this path.

Traced in order: (1) App.vue:1417 passes the literal `:locked="false"` to AppSidebar, which forwards it verbatim to RepoSwitcher (AppSidebar.vue:42). RepoSwitcher.vue:21 documents the prop as "Disables the switcher while a blocking operation runs" and both the trigger button (`:disabled="locked"`) and the popover (`:open="open && !locked"`) honour it — the guard is built and deliberately never engaged. (2) `useGit.busy` really is dead: grep for "busy" across src returns only useGit.ts:26/39/49/55 (decl, two assignments, return); App.vue:131 calls git.push/fetch/pull/stash/merge/rebase/continueOperation/abortOperation/resolveConflict and never reads git.busy. (3) useGit.run (useGit.ts:36-51) captures id = repos.selectedId, awaits the action, then unconditionally calls refreshAll(id) -> branches/workingCopy/history .refresh(A). (4) All three writes are unguarded: branches.ts:24-39 assigns `branches.value = locals` / `remoteBranches.value = remotes`; workingCopy.ts:26-33 calls apply() unconditionally; history.ts:85-95 calls apply() then loadGraph(repo). No `repo !== repos.selectedId` check, no request token, no $reset, and no clear-on-switch anywhere in the stores. (5) The switch is reachable: openRepository (App.vue:526-529) calls repositories.select(id), a bare `selectedId.value = id` + loadRemotes (repos.ts:89-92), then navigates. There is no router beforeEach/beforeEnter/beforeResolve guard in src/router or src/main.ts. Switching fires refresh(B) through the selectedId watchers in useBranches.ts:19-25, useWorkingCopy.ts:15-21 and useHistory.ts:21-27, so B loads first and A's in-flight response lands last and wins. (6) The downstream wrong-repo action is real: useWorkingCopy.stage (useWorkingCopy.ts:26-30) takes the target from activeRepo() = current selectedId while the path comes from the now-stale rendered list, so wc_stage_paths(B, [A's path]) is exactly what fires.

The decisive internal contrast holds: the codebase already solves this hazard twice elsewhere and not here. useCompare keeps a monotonic requestToken bumped per load and checks it before every write (useCompare.ts:120-121, 149, 160, 171), with App.vue:519-524 stating "Compare is repository-scoped: it must not answer for the previous repo." useAppEvents.ts:31-39 guards on `event.payload.repo !== repos.selectedId`. So two of the three request paths guard; the store path — the one fed by both the selection watcher and every git verb — does not.

Severity stays major, not blocker: discardEntry (App.vue:907-920) is behind a confirm dialogue so there is no silent data loss, and the display self-corrects on the next refresh. But staging/committing B's index with A's paths is a silent wrong-repository action in a tool whose documented promise is "not surprising anyone", and the switcher actively asserts it is fine to switch.

One inaccuracy in the repro that does not affect the finding: cloning is NOT a repro path — repos.clone() (repos.ts:100-133) sets selectedId itself and never goes through useGit.run, so it issues no refreshAll. The fetch/pull half of the repro is accurate and sufficient on its own. No existing test covers this (src has only loadState.test.ts, catalog.test.ts, AboutScreen/changelog/templateCompiles/interactionCompleteness tests; none touch selectedId).

findings.title: Every error surface shows the raw English engine message although a complete localised catalogue and errorText() exist
findings.evidence: errorText() is defined at src/i18n/index.ts:159-168 and referenced nowhere in src (grep: only its definition). Its header comment states the backend does not localise and that `errors.byCode` covers every ErrorCode (src/i18n/locales/en.ts:159-181, matching block in zh-CN.ts). The shell instead renders payload.message directly: reportError (App.vue:548-554) pushes `String(error.message)` as a danger toast; the launch screen banner binds `:error-message="repositories.lastError.value?.message"` (App.vue:1440, rendered at RepositoryListScreen.vue:201-205); activity entries store `error.message` (App.vue:583, rendered at ActivityScreen.vue:78).
findings.repro: With the UI in zh-CN, type a path that does not exist on the launch screen and press Open. Expected: the catalogue sentence for the code (errors.byCode.io = "文件操作失败。"). Actual: the banner and the toast show the Rust sentence, e.g. "Path does not exist: /nope", in English.
findings.expected: User-facing error text comes from the catalogue via errorText(payload), interpolating params; the Rust message is a developer-facing fallback only.
findings.actual: All shell error output is the untranslated English Rust message, so the zh-CN UI mixes languages for exactly the failures the owner is complaining about.
findings.fix: Route reportError, the launch-screen banner, the activity entry error and the ListShell error props through errorText() from src/i18n (it already handles the missing-key fallback), keeping payload.detail for logs.
findings.testIdea: New src/i18n/index.test.ts: assert errorText({code:'io'}) equals the zh-CN catalogue string and not payload.message; plus a source scan asserting no component renders `.error.message` for display.

notes: CONFIRMED — no guard, default, or handler rescues this. Every step of the repro re-traces exactly as the finding describes. (1) errorText is dead code. `grep -rn "errorText" src/ src-tauri/` returns exactly one hit: its own definition at src/i18n/index.ts:159. No component, store, composable, or bridge calls it. (2) The catalogue is complete and build-enforced, so errorText's fallback branch is unreachable. en.ts byCode is `satisfies Record`; zh-CN.ts is annotated `: Catalog` (the shape of en.ts). Both define `io`. (3) Repro verified end to end. repository_open calls validate_open_path (src-tauri/src/validation/repository.rs:8-16), which returns `Violation::new(ErrorCode::Io, format!("Path does not exist: {}", path.display())).with_param("path", ...)`. That crosses to repos.ts:66 (`lastError.value = error as ErrorPayload`), binds at App.vue:1440 (`:error-message="repositories.lastError.value?.message ?? null"`), and renders verbatim at RepositoryListScreen.vue:203 (`{{ errorMessage }}`). The zh-CN user sees the English Rust sentence. No locale is sent to the backend for errors — the only command taking a `locale` arg is app_release_notes_load (commands.ts:379) — and bridges/commands.ts is a bare typed wrapper with no interception layer. reportError (App.vue:548-554) and the activity entry (App.vue:583) have the same shape. (4) Extra corroboration the auditor missed, which strengthens the finding: reportError's `fallback` argument is only used when the error object has no `message`, and ErrorPayload.message is a non-optional `String` (domain/error.rs:32, no serde skip). So the `t("shell.toast.checkoutFailed")` / `commitFailed` / `branchDeleteFailed` / `actionFailed` strings passed at all 11 reportError call sites (App.vue:511, 584, 736, 795, 829, 866, 877, 903, 920, 1011) are unreachable dead arguments. The localisation layer was built and then never wired at any level. (5) Scope is wider than the four sites named: AccountScreen.vue:101, WorkingCopyPane.vue:168, HistoryPane.vue:158, ComparePane.vue:122, BranchListPane.vue:79, BlamePane.vue:135, CommitDetailPane.vue:124 and 229, SettingsScreen.vue:149, AboutScreen.vue:111 and 218, ReleaseNotesPanel.vue:96, RepositoryListScreen.vue:229 and 286. Severity kept at major. Against a stated owner constraint that the app "ships Simplified Chinese and English, Chinese by default", every failure path in the app renders in the wrong language in the default locale — that is a defect users hit routinely, not an edge case, and it renders a complete dead subsystem (a 14-entry x 2-locale catalogue plus a purpose-built function) as unused code. It is not a blocker: nothing crashes, corrupts, or blocks work, and the English text is still readable and accurate. One correction to the proposed fix, which would otherwise cause a regression: routing `io` through errorText() alone LOSES information. The `io` catalogue entry has no `{path}` placeholder ("文件操作失败。" / "A file operation failed."), so the path the user just typed vanishes from the banner — strictly worse than today. Only 4 of the 14 entries interpolate params (unknown_revision {revision}, invalid_reference_name {name}, reference_exists {name}, reference_not_found {name}); the other 10 are parameterless, even though the Rust side populates params via with_param in 193 places across 27 files.

findings.title: Compare ref picker titles render the raw key shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle / compareTargetTitle (missing from both catalogues)
findings.evidence: App.vue:465-480 (pickCompareRef) builds the ChooseBranchDialog title as `t("shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle")` (line 470) or `t("shell.dialogue.compareTargetTitle")` (line 471). Walking both message trees (650 leaf keys, identical key sets in en and zh-CN) shows neither key exists; the only hits for those strings in the tree are App.vue:470-471. Verified with vue-i18n 11.4.14: t() on a missing key returns the key itself.
findings.repro: Open a repository, go to the Compare tab, click the base-side picker. Expected: a dialog titled "Comparison base" / "比较基准". Actual: the dialog's h2 and its aria-label read `shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle` (same for the target side).
findings.expected: Both titles resolve to translated copy like every other dialogue title.
findings.actual: The literal key is shown as the dialog title in both locales.
findings.fix: Add `compareBaseTitle` and `compareTargetTitle` to the `shell.dialogue` block in src/i18n/locales/parts/en/diff.ts and zh-CN/diff.ts.
findings.testIdea: The catalogue/literal scan described in SHELL-03 (extend src/i18n/catalog.test.ts) fails today on exactly these two keys.

notes:
CONFIRMED — I re-traced every step and found no guard, default, or handler that rescues the key. Path: `/tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:464-480` (`pickCompareRef`) builds the ChooseBranchDialog request with `title: side === "left" ? t("shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle") : t("shell.dialogue.compareTargetTitle")` (lines 470-471, exactly as reported). The picker that fires it is always live: `ComparePane.vue:65-97` renders both `.ref-picker` buttons with `@click="emit('chooseRef', 'left'|'right')"`, and `App.vue:1631` passes `:unavailable="null"`, so they are never disabled. Propagation has no fallback at any hop: `layout/DialogueHost.vue:81` passes `:title="branchRequest.title"` straight through → `ChooseBranchDialog.vue` passes it to `DialogueShell` → `DialogueShell.vue:94,101` renders it as both `

{{ title }}

` and `:aria-label="title"` on the `role="dialog"` panel. So the raw key is both visible and announced by a screen reader. Catalogue gap: `grep -rn "compareBaseTitle\|compareTargetTitle"` over the whole `src` tree returns **only** App.vue:470-471 — zero hits in any locale file. `shell.dialogue` exists in both `locales/parts/en/diff.ts:260-278` and `locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:241-258` with 17 keys each (newBranchTitle … discardConfirm), and neither includes the compare titles. I also enumerated every other `shell.dialogue.*` reference in `src` (19 call sites in App.vue:470-914) — all resolve to existing keys, so this is an isolated omission, not a systemic one. No escape hatch exists: `createI18n` in `src/i18n/index.ts:44-53` sets no `missing` handler (only `missingWarn`/`fallbackWarn`, DEV-only), and nothing calls `mergeLocaleMessage`/`setLocaleMessage` at runtime (grep across `src` returns nothing) — the messages object is the plain spread of the three slices. `fallbackLocale: "en"` cannot help because the key is missing from en too. Empirically confirmed on the project's own vue-i18n 11.4.14 (from `/tmp/meridian-baseline/node_modules`): `t("shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle")` returns the literal string `"shell.dialogue.compareBaseTitle"` under both `zh-CN` and `en`, with a control key (`shell.dialogue.checkoutTitle`) resolving correctly to `签出分支` / `Check out branch` in the same instance. Why it escaped: I ran the existing `src/i18n/catalog.test.ts` in the baseline — 4/4 pass. That test checks en/zh mutual parity and untranslated duplicates, but nothing checks that keys *referenced by components* exist, so a component-side typo is invisible to both it and to `vue-tsc` (`zh-CN.ts` is typed `Catalog`, which only catches drift between the two catalogues). The auditor's test idea is the right durable fix. Severity: major stands. It is user-visible in both locales on a normal Compare interaction, not a cosmetic-only nit (a raw i18n key is the app's internal dotted path shown in a modal heading and in its accessible name), but it is also not functional breakage — the picker still opens, filters, and returns the chosen ref, and no data or state is affected. That is exactly the major band, not blocker, and not minor. Note on scope: this was read-only verification against `/tmp/meridian-baseline`; I made zero edits. `git status` in `~/dev/CortexOS` is clean and in sync with `origin/main`, so there is no half-finished change here to commit — the two entries in `git stash list` are dated, hand-labelled WIP and I left them alone.

findings.title: Escape with the palette open over a dialogue closes both, because both handlers are capture-phase listeners on the same node
findings.evidence: DialogueShell registers its handler with `document.addEventListener("keydown", onKeydown, true)` (src/components/dialogues/DialogueShell.vue:73) and calls event.stopPropagation() on Escape (DialogueShell.vue:41-47). CommandPalette does the same (src/components/palettes/CommandPalette.vue:77, 114) and also stops propagation on Escape (CommandPalette.vue:86-89). stopPropagation does not prevent other listeners already registered on the same target from running (only stopImmediatePropagation does), and both listeners are on `document` in the capture phase, so both fire for one Escape.
findings.repro: Open the checkout picker (branch pane → Check out branch…), then press ⌘K (the shortcut matcher's only guard is isTextTarget, and focus is on a button, see SHELL-06). The palette paints above the dialogue because both use z-index var(--md-z-dialog) and the palette is later in DOM order (App.vue:1750-1775). Press Escape once. Expected: only the palette closes, leaving the picker. Actual: the palette and the picker both close.
findings.expected: One Escape dismisses exactly the topmost layer.
findings.actual: Two layers close from one keystroke, so the user loses the dialogue they were working in.
findings.fix: Give the palette and DialogueHost a single owner of the keydown handler (one host component, or a shared modal stack), or use stopImmediatePropagation while checking that no other modal is stacked above.
findings.testIdea: New src/components/palettes/CommandPalette.test.ts (jsdom): render DialogueShell + CommandPalette, dispatch one Escape on document, assert exactly one close emitted.

notes:
Confirmed on re-trace; no guard, default, or ordering fact the auditor missed.

Mechanism verified in source: DialogueShell.vue:73 registers `document.addEventListener("keydown", onKeydown, true)` and DialogueShell.vue:44 calls `event.stopPropagation()` before `emit("close")`. CommandPalette.vue:77 (watch on `open`) and CommandPalette.vue:114 (onMounted) register the same capture-phase listener on the same node, and CommandPalette.vue:86-89 does `stopPropagation()` + `emit("close")`. Two listeners on the same target in the same phase: `stopPropagation` only halts propagation to *further* nodes, so both run. `stopImmediatePropagation` is never called anywhere in src (grepped).

Empirically reproduced with the real components under jsdom + @vue/test-utils (scratch dir, since no palette/dialogue test exists — the finding's testIdea is a real gap): one `new KeyboardEvent("keydown", {key:"Escape", bubbles:true})` dispatched on `document` emitted closes in order `["dialogue.close","palette.close"]`; both `.dialogue-backdrop` and `.palette-backdrop` were removed from the DOM.

Repro precondition independently verified rather than assumed: ChooseBranchDialog.vue carries no `data-autofocus` (only ConfirmDialog.vue:67/74 and PromptDialog.vue:95 do), so DialogueShell.vue:75 falls through to `focusables()[0]`. DOM-order inspection of the mounted panel gives `BUTTON.dialogue-close | INPUT | BUTTON.branch-row | BUTTON.btn` — the first focusable is a button, not a text field, so `isTextTarget` (useShell.ts:148) is false and the `⌘K` binding at App.vue:1371 runs `openPalette("open")` with the picker already open. Z-order claim also holds: both backdrops use `z-index: var(--md-z-dialog)` (80, tokens.css:303) and both Teleport to body, with the palette landing second (`body` children `["DIV","dialogue-backdrop","palette-backdrop"]`), so it paints above the picker — the topmost layer really is the one that survives visually.

One correction to the proposed fix, not to the finding: `stopImmediatePropagation` is offered as an alternative but is wrong as a standalone remedy. Measured listener order is `["dialogue.close","palette.close"]` — DialogueShell mounts and registers first, so adding `stopImmediatePropagation` there would close the *bottom* layer and leave the topmost palette open, the inverse of the intent. The ownership/shared-stack half of the fix is the correct half.

Severity minor is correct and I am not raising it: one keystroke, fully recoverable by reopening the picker, no persisted state lost. Category nit: `race` is a misnomer — the behaviour is deterministic listener layering on one node, not a timing race — but that does not change the verdict.

findings.title: A failed repository scan is reported as "Nothing found nearby", and its retry affordance is unreachable
findings.evidence: discoverNearby's catch sets nearby.value = [] and nearbyState.value = "empty" (src/stores/repos.ts:145-156) while stashing the payload in lastError. App.vue:1226-1235 maps every nearbyState that is not 'scanning' or 'done' to { status: 'empty' }, so the ListShell error branch and its @retry (RepositoryListScreen.vue:286-287, 280-288) can never fire; repos.nearbyState has no 'error' member at all (repos.ts:143).
findings.repro: Click "Scan again" and choose a folder whose contents cannot be read (permissions). Expected: the nearby section reports the failure and offers Retry. Actual: the section renders its empty state "Nothing found nearby" / "你已授权的文件夹里的仓库会显示在这里。" while a separate error banner appears above the recents list.
findings.expected: A scan that failed is distinguishable from a scan that found nothing, and offers a retry that re-runs the scan.
findings.actual: The failure is reported as an empty result and the retry path is dead code.
findings.fix: Add an 'error' member to nearbyState, set it in the catch, and map it to { status: 'error', error } in App.vue so ListShell renders the message and its retry.
findings.testIdea: New src/stores/repos.test.ts: mock repositoryDiscover to reject and assert nearbyState === 'error' (currently 'empty').

notes:
Traced end to end; the finding holds. repos.ts:143 types nearbyState as "idle" | "scanning" | "done" | "empty" — no 'error' member — and the catch at 151-155 sets it to "empty" while stashing the payload in lastError. useRepositories.ts:86-87,105 is a pure passthrough, so there is no second path. App.vue:1226-1235 switches on "scanning"->loading and "done"->data with `default:`->{status:"empty"}, so both "empty" and "idle" (and any future value) land on empty; 'error' can never be produced. That flows through RepositoryListScreen.vue:281 into ListShell, whose error arm (ListShell.vue:64-69, including the "Try again" button) requires status === 'error', so the arm never renders and @retry on line 287 is dead code. The failure is reachable: repository.rs:223-236 calls validate_discover_root, which returns "Cannot read {path}" for an unreadable directory (lines 586-590) — precisely the repro.

Two overstatements that keep this at minor rather than changing the verdict. First, the "silent-failure" category is inaccurate: the catch sets lastError, bound at App.vue:1440-1441 to :error-message/:error-detail, which renders the role="alert" banner at RepositoryListScreen.vue:201-205 — the finding's own repro concedes this banner appears, so the failure is announced, not hidden. Second, "its retry affordance is unreachable" is true only of the ListShell "Try again" button; a working retry is already on screen in the same section header at RepositoryListScreen.vue:269-278 ("Scan again"), never disabled on this route because App.vue:1442 passes :unavailable="null", emitting the identical refreshNearby -> scanNearby() -> discoverNearby. The user is never stranded. The real defect is narrower: the nearby section asserts a false negative ("Nothing found nearby" / "附近没有找到仓库") on the same screen where the banner above says the scan failed — two contradictory statements — plus genuinely dead error-arm code.

Supporting evidence the finding did not cite: ListShell.vue:6-11 documents a contract ("Every asynchronous list renders exactly four states... no list can forget a state") and every other consumer honors it. history.ts:31, workingCopy.ts:15, useApp.ts:110-140 and useCompare.ts:159 hold a LoadState in the store and set errorState(error) in the catch, then pass state.status straight to ListShell (HistoryPane.vue:154-159, BranchListPane.vue:74-79, ComparePane.vue:118-122, WorkingCopyPane.vue:164-169). RepositoryListScreen.vue:281 is the sole outlier — the only ListShell consumer fed by a hand-rolled switch with no error arm, and the only one omitting :error-detail. So the deviation is real and the fix is a return to the house pattern.

Severity stays minor: not major, because there is no data loss, the error is announced with role="alert", and a working retry button exists; not a no-op, because a self-contradicting false empty state plus dead code against a documented contract is a genuine defect.

findings.title: "Scan again" re-opens the folder picker instead of rescanning the folder that was already granted
findings.evidence: RepositoryListScreen emits refreshNearby from the "Scan again" button (src/components/screens/RepositoryListScreen.vue:269-278) and from ListShell's retry (line 287); App.vue binds `@refresh-nearby="scanNearby"` (App.vue:1448) and scanNearby unconditionally calls pickDirectory() before discoverNearby (App.vue:1244-1247). The last scanned root is never stored (repos.discoverNearby takes a root and keeps no record, src/stores/repos.ts:145).
findings.repro: On the launch screen click "Scan again" and pick a folder; the nearby list populates. Click "Scan again" a second time. Expected: the same folder is rescanned (a refresh). Actual: a folder-chooser dialog opens again, so a one-click refresh costs a modal file dialog and the user must remember the same path.
findings.expected: Refresh re-runs the last scan; only a first-time scan (or an explicit "Choose a folder") asks for a directory.
findings.actual: Every refresh re-prompts for a folder, and the button's label ("Scan again" / "重新扫描") does not mention a picker.
findings.fix: Store the last scanned root in the repos store; scanNearby uses it when present and only calls pickDirectory() when it is null (or when the user explicitly chooses a new folder).
findings.testIdea: New src/components/screens/RepositoryListScreen.test.ts: with a remembered root, assert the refresh emits a rescan event rather than a browse event.

notes:
CONFIRMED — re-traced line by line in /tmp/meridian-baseline, and I looked hard for the guard the finding might have missed. None exists.

1. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/screens/RepositoryListScreen.vue:265-278 — the `<section v-if="showNearby" class="launch-nearby">` header holds the "Scan again" button. Its only guard is `:disabled="!!unavailable?.nearby"` (line 272), and App.vue:1440 passes `:unavailable="null"`, so the button is always live. `showNearby` defaults to `true` (line 55) and App.vue never passes it, so the section renders unconditionally — the button is even visible before any scan has happened.
2. Click → `emit('refreshNearby')` (line 274). The second site the auditor cites (line 287, `ListShell @retry`) is a real emit but is DEAD CODE: App.vue's `nearbyState` computed (App.vue:1226-1235) only ever returns 'loading' | 'data' | 'empty' — never 'error' — so ListShell never renders the error/retry state. That is an evidence inaccuracy in the finding, but it does not touch the primary claim, which rests on the button path.
3. App.vue:1448 `@refresh-nearby="scanNearby"`.
4. App.vue:1244-1247, verbatim:
     async function scanNearby(): Promise<void> {
       const root = await pickDirectory();
       if (root) await repositories.discoverNearby(root);
     }
   Unconditional picker, no memo, no branch on prior state. Its doc comment only justifies picking instead of walking $HOME; it says nothing about refresh.
5. src/stores/repos.ts:145-156 — `discoverNearby(root)` sets `nearbyState`/`nearby` and keeps no record of `root`. Nothing else in the store writes one.
6. No other layer holds it: no localStorage/sessionStorage/persist plugin anywhere under src/stores or src/main.ts; `useRepositories.ts` only re-exports `store.discoverNearby` (line 105) and its `nearbyState`/`nearby` computeds (86-87); the Rust side is stateless per call — `repository_discover` (src-tauri/src/commands/repository.rs:223) takes `root` in its args and returns roots, `engine::discovery` "has no state of its own", and `app_pick_directory` (commands/app.rs:320-345) sets only a title, no remembered default path.

So the repro is real: after one scan, a second "Scan again" opens a fresh modal folder panel. Severity stays minor — it is a UX/label mismatch ("Scan again" does not say it opens a picker), not a correctness defect: no data loss, no wrong state, cancel resolves to null and is silently ignored (correctly — the Rust doc at app.rs:308-310 explicitly wants cancel-as-non-error). One mitigation worth noting for the fix's sake: the macOS native panel reopens at the last-visited folder, so the cost is "one modal + a click", not "recall the path" — the finding slightly overstates the pain.

The proposed fix direction is right but the test idea is aimed at the wrong layer: the screen emits `refreshNearby` unconditionally and cannot distinguish refresh from choose-folder, so a `RepositoryListScreen.test.ts` asserting "a rescan event rather than a browse event" cannot fail until the component itself grows a second emit. The assertion belongs on the store/composable (root remembered after `discoverNearby`, reused on the next refresh) or on App.vue's `scanNearby`.

findings.title: Sidebar filter makes sections claim they are empty ("No branches") when they are merely filtered out
findings.evidence: sidebarSections applies `keep` to branch names and to the translated History title (App.vue:250-364; branchRows filter at 255-257, remoteRows at 271-272, the history row's guard at 316-317) but each section keeps its `emptyCaption` ("No branches" / "没有分支", "No commits", "No remote branches"). SidebarSection renders that caption whenever the row list is empty (src/layout/SidebarSection.vue:64), and the filter field lives in the sidebar footer (src/layout/AppSidebar.vue:61-68) with no indication that it is what emptied the sections above it.
findings.repro: Open a repository with several branches and type a Chinese word such as 分支 into the sidebar filter (or any string that matches no branch name). Expected: a "no matches" state, or the filter not applying to branch names at all. Actual: the Branches section shows "No branches" while the repository plainly has branches, and the History section does the same for commits.
findings.expected: An empty section caused by the filter is distinguishable from a genuinely empty section (different caption), or the filter only filters what it can meaningfully match.
findings.actual: The same caption is reused for both states, so filtering misinforms the user about the repository's contents.
findings.fix: Track whether a needle is active and pass a distinct caption (e.g. a new shell.sidebar.noMatch key) when rows were filtered out rather than absent; the working-copy row and the unconditional sections should follow the same rule.
findings.testIdea: Extract the section-building logic into a testable function (or new src/composables/useSidebar.test.ts) and assert that with a non-matching filter the branches section reports a filter-miss caption rather than emptyBranches.

notes:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every link in the auditor's chain checks out, and no guard, default, or handler exists that distinguishes "empty" from "filtered empty".

Re-trace (all line numbers in /tmp/meridian-baseline):
1. App.vue:251-253 — `needle = sidebarFilter.value.trim().toLowerCase()`, `keep = needle === "" || label.includes(needle)`. `keep` is applied in exactly three places: branch names (256), remote names (272), and the translated History *title* (317). Nothing else in the file consumes `needle`.
2. App.vue:280-363 — every section carries an unconditional `emptyCaption`: `emptyWorkingCopy`, `emptyHistory`, `emptyBranches`, `emptyRemotes`, `emptyTags`, `emptyStashes`. None is conditional on `needle`. `sectionsWithCollapse` (368-373) only overrides `collapsed`, never the caption.
3. App.vue:1411-1426 passes `sectionsWithCollapse` straight to `AppSidebar`; there is no pre-filter or no-match banner anywhere between the computed and the DOM. Grep for `sidebarSections|sectionsWithCollapse|sidebarFilter` returns only those definitions plus this one binding — no other consumer.
4. SidebarSection.vue:64 — `v-if="section.rows.length === 0"` renders `section.emptyCaption`. That is the only empty-state render path in the component.
5. AppSidebar.vue:61-68 — the `SearchField` sits in `.sidebar-footer`, below `.sidebar-sections` (which is `flex: 1`, line 80-85), so it is visually disconnected from the sections it empties. No clear button, no result count.

So: filter to a string matching no branch name → `branchRows` is `[]` → Branches renders "No branches" while `branches.branches.value` is non-empty. Confirmed as described.

Three things strengthen the finding beyond what was written:

(a) The type contract already says filtered-empty is its own state. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/contracts.ts:425-426 documents `emptyCaption` as "Rendered when the section has no rows (the filtered-empty state)." The author designed the field for the filtered-empty case and then filled it with the genuinely-empty copy. This is an unimplemented intent, not a stylistic choice.

(b) The UI spec enumerates it as a distinct state. /tmp/meridian-baseline/docs/04-ui-spec.md:440 lists `<SidebarSection>` states as "collapsed, filtered-empty, normal, selected" — filtered-empty is called out separately from the empty/normal cases.

(c) The sibling screen already implements the recommended fix, so the sidebar is the inconsistent one. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/screens/SettingsScreen.vue:292 and :298 use dedicated `screens.settings.noMatchingGroup` ("No matching settings." / "没有匹配的设置。") and `noMatchingTitle` keys for the filtered-empty state, instead of reusing the empty copy. The exact pattern the finding proposes already exists one screen over.

Two corrections to the evidence, neither of which weakens it:
- The Chinese captions are 尚无分支 / 尚无提交 / 尚无远程分支 (src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:172-174), not "没有分支" as quoted. This is worse, not better: 尚无 means "there are none *yet*", so in Chinese the sidebar actively tells the user the repository has no branches yet — a forward-looking claim the code cannot support.
- The History section's `keep` (line 317) tests the localized section *title*, never commit subjects. So History can never be found by searching for anything a user would look for in it; typing any commit-related word silently empties it into "No commits". The comment at 314-315 shows this was deliberate (to make a Chinese needle match the Chinese title), so the history row is searchable only by its own name.

Scope check on severity: the caption only renders inside `v-if="!section.collapsed"` (SidebarSection.vue:53). Branches and History are `collapsed: false` by default (App.vue:312, 335), so they are visible on load and the wrong text appears immediately. Remotes/Tags/Stashes default to collapsed, so their wrong captions are latent. Recovery is trivial — the field the user just typed in is right below. No data loss, no crash, no persistence, no security impact; it is a false statement about repository state confined to one pane and one keystroke to undo. "minor" is the right grade and I found nothing to raise or lower it.

One nuance in the repro as written: typing 分支 is a valid needle that matches nothing because branch names are ASCII in practice — the repro is correct in effect, but any non-matching string demonstrates the same thing, including in English. The auditor already allowed for this.

findings.title: Settings' empty tabs show "Nothing matches """ instead of the intended "nothing to configure yet"
findings.evidence: The document hard-codes three tabs with `groups: []` and source 'schema' (App.vue:1190-1212: general, services, advanced). SettingsScreen's fallback empty state is gated on `!active` (SettingsScreen.vue:154-159) — reachable only for an unknown tab id — while the filtered-empty state at SettingsScreen.vue:295-301 fires for any tab other than appearance, using screens.settings.noMatchingTitle / nothingMatches with `{ query: search }`, and search is '' when the user merely switched tabs. The catalogue's screens.settings.emptyTitle/emptyCaption ("Nothing to configure yet" / "Settings become available as the backend commands land.") are therefore unreachable in normal use.
findings.repro: Settings → click the General (or Services, Advanced) tab. Expected: "Nothing to configure yet" with the note that these arrive with the backend. Actual: an empty state titled "No matching settings" whose caption reads "Nothing matches ""." in en and "没有与「」匹配的项。" in zh-CN, as though a search were in effect.
findings.expected: A tab with no rows and an empty query shows the "nothing to configure" copy; the "nothing matches" copy appears only when a search is actually filtering.
findings.actual: The wrong empty state is chosen and it interpolates an empty query.
findings.fix: Choose the empty state on `active.groups.length === 0 && search.trim() === ''` (emptyTitle/emptyCaption) versus a non-empty query (noMatchingTitle/nothingMatches).
findings.testIdea: New src/components/screens/SettingsScreen.test.ts: render with the real document and active-tab 'general', assert the rendered title is screens.settings.emptyTitle.

notes:
Confirmed — I re-traced every hop and then mounted the component to check, and could not find the guard.

Path, line by line (all paths under /tmp/meridian-baseline):

1. The document is built in App.vue:1139 `settingsDocument = computed<SettingsDocument>(() => ({ version: 1, tabs: [...] }))`. `tabs` is a plain array literal — no `.filter()`, no normalization, no derived state. Lines 1187-1212 hold three placeholder tabs verbatim: `id: "general" / "services" / "advanced"`, each `source: "schema"`, each `groups: []`.
2. App.vue:1254 `settingsState` wraps it as `{ status: "data", data: settingsDocument.value }` — so `document.status` is never `loading`/`error` here and the first two EmptyState arms are dead in the real shell.
3. App.vue:1214 `settingsTab = computed(() => route.value.query.section ?? "appearance")`; the tab button handler is `@update:active-tab="navigate(settingsPath($event))"` (App.vue:1697), and `settingsPath` (router/routes.ts:81) only encodes the section — no validation, no fallback to a known-good tab. Clicking General therefore yields `activeTab === "general"`.
4. SettingsScreen.vue:56 `tabs = document.status === "data" ? document.data.tabs : []`, and :58 `active = tabs.find(t => t.id === props.activeTab) ?? null`. `"general"` IS in the array, so `active` is non-null — the fallback arm at :154-159 (`v-else-if="!active"` → emptyTitle/emptyCaption) is unreachable for every tab a user can actually click. The auditor's claim about that gate is exactly right.
5. SettingsScreen.vue:60-71 `filteredGroups`: `if (!active) return []`, then `needle = search.trim().toLowerCase()`; needle === "" returns `active.value.groups` unchanged, i.e. `[]` for these three tabs. `App.vue:1215 settingsSearch = ref("")` and is only ever written by the search input, so it is "" on a plain tab switch.
6. SettingsScreen.vue:295-301: the only remaining EmptyState is `v-if="filteredGroups.length === 0 && active.id !== 'appearance'"`. `[] === 0` is true and `'general' !== 'appearance'`, so it renders `noMatchingTitle` and `nothingMatches` with `{ query: search }` where `search` is `""`. EmptyState.vue:35 renders the caption whenever `caption` is truthy — and the interpolated string is truthy — so the malformed caption is not swallowed.

Empirical check (scratch copy at /tmp, node_modules symlinked from the snapshot, since a mount is the only thing that settles a v-if chain). Mounting `<SettingsScreen>` with the exact tab set from App.vue, locale `en`, `search=""`:

  [general]   titles=["No matching settings"] captions=["Nothing matches “”."]
  [services]  titles=["No matching settings"] captions=["Nothing matches “”."]
  [advanced]  titles=["No matching settings"] captions=["Nothing matches “”."]
  [unknown]   titles=["Nothing to configure yet"] captions=["Settings become available as the backend commands land."]

So the copy the catalogue reserves for an unknown tab id is the only place it appears, and the three tabs a user can click all get the search copy with an interpolated empty query. zh-CN is the same defect with "没有与「」匹配的项。" (i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/shell.ts:86).

What I could not use as a defence: no doc pins this. `docs/04-ui-spec.md` has no §S12 for Settings (its S12 is the Activity window), and grepping all of docs/ for "Nothing to configure" / "No matching" returns nothing, so there is no spec clause making "No matching settings" the intended state for an unpopulated tab. There is also no SettingsScreen test at all (only i18n/catalog.test.ts and components/about/changelog.test.ts touch settings strings), and src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts only scans emits and button wiring, so nothing guards this.

Two things the auditor got slightly wrong or missed, neither of which rescues the code:
- The `active.id !== 'appearance'` half of the guard is deliberate, not a bug: the two shell-owned sections (Theme, Language) render unconditionally on the appearance tab, so a zero-row filter there still shows real controls. Confirmed empirically — appearance + query "zzz" yields zero empty states, i.e. no blank panel, just no hint. Fixing the guard must not touch that half.
- The test idea says "render with the real document", but `settingsDocument` is a local const inside App.vue's setup block (App.vue:1139) and is not exported; nothing in src/bridges or elsewhere builds a SettingsDocument fixture. The test has to hand-build the tab list (or the document has to be extracted into a module first).

Severity stays minor, and I checked it is not lower: it is a visible, reproducible wrong-string defect on 3 of the 5 tabs in a shipped screen, with a second-order symptom that `emptyTitle`/`emptyCaption` are dead catalogue entries in both locales — the kind of rot that reads as an unfinished build. It is not major because nothing fails functionally: no crash, no data loss, no action is blocked, and every control on the tab still works.

findings.title: Toolbar Push toast interpolates a branch it was never given ("Pushed .")
findings.evidence: App.vue:672 calls `t("shell.toast.pushed")` with no params, while the catalogue entry is `pushed: "Pushed {branch}."` (en) / "推送了 {branch}。" (zh-CN, src/i18n/locales/parts/en/diff.ts:290-296 and the zh slice). The branch-pane path does pass it (App.vue:496-499), which is what makes the omission visible. Verified with vue-i18n 11.4.14: t('pushed') with no argument renders "推送了 。" / "Pushed .".
findings.repro: Press Push on the toolbar with a repository open. Expected: "Pushed main." Actual: "Pushed ." / "推送了 。"
findings.expected: The success toast names the branch that was pushed (which also matters because the pushed branch may not be the one the user expects — see SHELL-02).
findings.actual: A dangling placeholder is shown.
findings.fix: Pass the branch: t("shell.toast.pushed", { branch: repos.selected?.headBranch ?? "" }) — and once SHELL-02 is fixed, the same value the command actually used.
findings.testIdea: Extend src/i18n/catalog.test.ts (or a new toast test) with a check that every catalogue string containing a named placeholder is invoked with a params object at its call site.

notes:
Confirmed by direct re-trace, with the runtime behavior reproduced against the snapshot's own dependency.

DISCREPANCY: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:672 reads `await runVerb(() => git.push(), t("shell.toast.pushed"));` — no params object — while the catalogue leaf is `pushed: "Pushed {branch}."` (en) at src/i18n/locales/parts/en/diff.ts:293 and `pushed: "已推送 {branch}。"` (zh-CN) at src/i18n/locales/parts/zh-CN/diff.ts:273. `runVerb` (App.vue:575-589) forwards that pre-rendered string straight to `shell.pushToast`, so the toast body is fixed at call time.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: ran the snapshot's own node_modules/vue-i18n (11.4.14) with the exact catalogue strings — t("shell.toast.pushed") renders "Pushed ." / "已推送 。", confirming the dangling placeholder.

GUARDS SEARCHED FOR, NONE FOUND:
- Key clobbering: en/shell.ts:70 also has a `toast:` block, which looked like a collision candidate, but it lives under that file's `screens` namespace (en/shell.ts:51) and the file exports top-level toolbar/sidebar/screens/dialogues/palette — not `shell`. The spread order in locales/en.ts (...diffEn, ...panesEn, ...shellEn) therefore cannot shadow `shell.toast`, which exists only in diff.ts (namespace opens at line 174, toast at 283).
- Missing-param handling: src/i18n/index.ts configures only fallbackLocale, missingWarn and fallbackWarn (both DEV-gated). No `missing` handler and no `messageResolver` that could substitute a value.
- Render-time cleanup: ToastHost.vue:31 renders `{{ toast.text }}` verbatim.
- Reachability: the `push` verb is enabled whenever hasRepo && hasRemote && hasHead (App.vue:596-610, 628) and SplitAction.runPrimary only short-circuits on `disabled || busy`, so line 672 executes in the ordinary case — not dead code.
- Test coverage: catalog.test.ts checks key-path parity and untranslated-duplicate values only; nothing asserts placeholder/call-site agreement. No test references onToolbarRun, toolbarVerbs, or shell.toast.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE FINDING: the proposed fix `t("shell.toast.pushed", { branch: repos.selected?.headBranch ?? "" })` does not compile in App.vue — the bindings there are `repositories` (App.vue:124) and the computed `selectedRepo` (App.vue:201). Substantively the intent is right and the value is exactly correct: useGit.push resolves `branchName ?? repos.selected?.headBranch` (src/composables/useGit.ts:77), so the toolbar's bare git.push() publishes precisely selectedRepo.value.headBranch. Note also that SHELL-02's wrong-branch concern does not bear on this call site — the toolbar pushes HEAD, and the branch-pane path (App.vue:492-500) is the one with the wrong-ref hazard.

Severity minor is correct: a cosmetic defect in a success toast. No data loss, no incorrect git operation, and it is immediately visible and self-clearing.

findings.title: Editor font size min/max are declared in the schema but never enforced on write or read
findings.evidence: The row declares min: 10 / max: 22 (App.vue:1152-1162) and the component only forwards them as <input> attributes (SettingsScreen.vue:214-223); onNumber emits the raw Number() of the field (SettingsScreen.vue:93-97); setSetting stores it verbatim (App.vue:1126-1130) and settingValue performs a typeof check but no range check (App.vue:1110-1113). editorFontSize then feeds the CSS variable (App.vue:1115-1124), which is consumed by the diff and blame views (src/components/diff/DiffViewer.vue:563, src/components/panes/BlamePane.vue:361).
findings.repro: Settings → Appearance → Editor font size → type 999 and blur (or hand-edit meridian.settings in localStorage to {"shell.editorFontSize":999} and reload). Expected: the value is clamped to 10–22. Actual: --md-font-size-editor becomes 999px and every diff/blame line is unreadable; the row's own min/max attributes do not block typed values.
findings.expected: The schema's min/max are enforced wherever the value is written or read, so no out-of-range value can reach the stylesheet.
findings.actual: Only the number input's spinner honours the bounds; typed and stored values pass through unchecked.
findings.fix: Clamp in setSetting (and when reading, in settingValue) against the row's declared min/max, and re-render the input from the clamped value so the UI cannot disagree with what was stored.
findings.testIdea: New src/components/screens/SettingsScreen.test.ts: emit an int row value of 999 and assert the emitted value is 22; plus a store-level test that a stored 999 yields editorFontSize 22.

notes:
CONFIRMED. I re-traced every hop and found no guard the auditor missed.

1. App.vue:1153-1162 declares min:10/max:22 on the row. SettingRowModel (src/components/contracts.ts:278-279) carries min/max, but grep for row.min|row.max shows the ONLY consumer is the template attribute forwarding in SettingsScreen.vue:222-223. The bounds are declared and never read by any logic.
2. SettingsScreen.vue:214-223 renders <input type="number" :min="row.max" @change="onNumber">. HTML numeric min/max constrain spinner stepping and the constraint-validation API only; they do not reject typed values. The file contains no <form>, no required, no checkValidity()/reportValidity() (grep: zero hits), so nothing turns the constraint into a block. The auditor is right that only the spinner honours the bounds.
3. SettingsScreen.vue:93-97 onNumber emits Number(input.value) after only a Number.isNaN guard. That guard also misses a MORE reachable trigger than the reported one: clearing the field gives Number("")===0, which is not NaN, so emptying the input emits 0 -> --md-font-size-editor:0px -> diff and blame lines disappear entirely. Same root cause, broader trigger, and it strengthens rather than weakens the finding.
4. App.vue:1126-1130 setSetting stores the value verbatim into storedSettings and localStorage.
5. App.vue:1110-1113 settingValue does a typeof check only; typeof 999 === "number" === typeof 13, so the hand-edited-localStorage repro ({"shell.editorFontSize":999}) passes validation and reaches the computed.
6. App.vue:1115-1124 editorFontSize feeds the CSS variable unconditionally, which is consumed raw at src/components/diff/DiffViewer.vue:563 (font-size) and :571 (min-height: calc(var(--md-font-size-editor) * var(--md-editor-leading))) and src/components/panes/BlamePane.vue:361. grep for clamp across src/ hits only MasterDetail.vue and VirtualCommitList.vue, unrelated; neither consumer uses CSS min()/max().

One inaccuracy in the finding, minor: the fix's clause "re-render the input from the clamped value so the UI cannot disagree with what was stored" describes a divergence that does not exist today -- :value="row.value as number" faithfully renders 999, so UI and storage currently agree on the wrong number. It is a correct requirement for the fix, not a description of the present defect. No test file in src/ currently covers this path.

Severity stays minor: the trigger is entirely self-inflicted (type it, or clear the field), there is no crash, no data loss and no security surface, and the row already renders a one-click Reset button (SettingsScreen.vue:281, condition defaultValue !== undefined && value !== defaultValue) that restores 13. It degrades two views; it does not break the app.

findings.title: Enter on a highlighted disabled palette item does nothing and says nothing
findings.evidence: CommandPalette.run returns silently for a disabled item (src/components/palettes/CommandPalette.vue:104-107, called from the Enter branch at 98-101); `active` starts at 0 (lines 47, 67, 75) and ArrowUp/Down move onto disabled items (lines 90-97) with no skip. The reason is only in the item's `title` (line 155), i.e. hover-only.
findings.repro: With no repository open, press ⌘⇧P (Quick actions). The first three items (New branch…, Check out branch…, Refresh repository) are disabled and the highlight is on the first of them.
