Press Enter. Expected: either the highlight skips disabled items, or the reason is surfaced ("Open a repository first."). Actual: nothing happens at all — no toast, no navigation, no hint.
findings.expected: Pressing Enter on a disabled entry either cannot happen (navigation skips disabled rows) or explains why it is disabled.
findings.actual: The keystroke is swallowed silently, which is indistinguishable from a broken palette.
findings.fix: Skip disabled items when computing the next/previous active index and when initialising it, and emit a shell toast with item.reason when Enter lands on a disabled item.
findings.testIdea: New src/components/palettes/CommandPalette.test.ts: with an items list whose first entry is disabled, assert active initialises to the first enabled index and that Enter on a disabled item emits no select but does surface the reason.

notes:
CONFIRMED, with the auditor's evidence corrected in the direction that makes the bug worse.

Verified line-by-line in /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/components/palettes/CommandPalette.vue: active starts at 0 (L47); both watchers reset it to 0 (L67, L75); ArrowDown/ArrowUp move modulo flat.value.length with no disabled-skip (L90-97); Enter calls run(flat.value[active.value]) (L98-101); run() returns silently on item.disabled (L104-107). Repro confirmed against the real producer src/App.vue:1273-1284 — with selectedRepo === null, action:new-branch / action:checkout / action:refresh are `disabled: !hasRepo` and occupy flat[0..2], so active=0 lands on a disabled row. ⌘⇧P is registered unconditionally at src/App.vue:1372, so the no-repo state is reachable on the app's primary shortcut.

THE GUARD THE AUDITOR CREDITED DOES NOT EXIST. The finding claims "the reason is only in the item's title (line 155), i.e. hover-only." That is wrong in the direction that worsens the bug: `reason` is never populated for palette items. Zero occurrences of `reason:` in the paletteItems block (src/App.vue:1273-1318), whereas src/layout/AppToolbar.vue:625-631 populates `reason` correctly for the toolbar's equivalent buttons. PaletteItemModel.reason (src/components/contracts.ts:445) is declared and bound to :title but never written by its only producer; Vue drops an undefined attribute, so there is NO tooltip — not hover-only, but zero explanation on any channel.

Two details that sharpen severity beyond the original report:

1. KEYBOARD-ONLY. The L156 @pointermove="active = indexOf(item)" fallback cannot rescue this, because `disabled` buttons do not fire pointer events in Chrome/Safari. Mouse users therefore never highlight a disabled row at all; only the arrow-key path reaches one. The defect is confined to the component's designed-for input.

2. THE PROPOSED FIX IS A NO-OP AS WRITTEN. The auditor's "emit a shell toast with item.reason" would render an empty toast, since reason is undefined. Populating reason is the prerequisite, not an optional extra. Separately, src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts:123-137 fails any emit that no caller listens for, so a new emit must be bound in App.vue or the suite breaks.

SEVERITY minor → major. Not a blocker: nothing is corrupted, no wrong action is performed, and the user can recover by arrowing down three rows. But it clears the major bar on three counts: it lands on the first-run path (⌘⇧P with no repo open is exactly what a new user does, and the state is deliberately designed-for — items are marked disabled rather than hidden); it swallows the component's single primary action with no feedback on any channel; and it hits keyboard-only users, which is a disproportionate accessibility cost for a component whose documented contract is "↑/↓ move, Enter runs, Escape closes" (L12-13). A first keystroke that is silently swallowed is indistinguishable from a broken palette, which is precisely the finding's actual severity claim — the auditor reached the right conclusion via a partially wrong mechanism.

findings.title: SearchField's clear button carries a hard-coded English aria-label
findings.evidence: src/components/common/SearchField.vue:40 renders `<button ... aria-label="Clear search">` while every other label in the file goes through $t (lines 33-38 use $t(label)/placeholder) and the project's convention is that all copy lives in the catalogue (src/i18n/locales/en.ts header). SearchField is used by the sidebar footer filter (AppSidebar.vue:62-67), the launch screen's recents filter (RepositoryListScreen.vue:211-217) and the choose-branch dialogue filter.
findings.repro: With zh-CN active and VoiceOver on, focus the sidebar filter, type a character and reach the clear (✕) button. Expected: an announcement in Chinese. Actual: it announces "Clear search" in English.
findings.expected: The clear affordance's accessible name comes from the catalogue (there is no common.clearSearch key today — it must be added).
findings.actual: An English string is exposed in the Chinese UI.
findings.fix: Add common.clearSearch to both catalogues and bind :aria-label="$t('common.clearSearch')".
findings.testIdea: Extend the source-scan test (src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts already walks .vue sources) with a check that no literal English aria-label/title attribute exists outside the catalogues.

notes:
CONFIRMED — no guard, default, or handler exists that the auditor missed.

Core evidence: src/components/common/SearchField.vue:40 renders `<button v-if="modelValue" type="button" class="clear" aria-label="Clear search" @click="clear">`. A precise scan for literal (non-bound) attributes across the whole src/ tree returns exactly ONE hit — this line. Every other aria-label in ~45 occurrences goes through t(...) / $t(...) or a bound variable. The convention is not aspirational; this is the sole outlier in an otherwise perfectly consistent pattern.

Strengthening facts the finding understates:
1. Chinese is the DEFAULT locale, not an edge case. src/i18n/index.ts: "the app ships Simplified Chinese and English, Chinese by default", DEFAULT_LOCALE = "zh-CN". Every first-run user hits this.
2. The aria-label is the button's SOLE accessible name. Its only child is <Icon name="xmark.circle.fill" :size="12" /> with no `label` prop, so Icon.vue:31 renders the svg aria-hidden="true". Nothing else can supply a localised name — it is not a redundant secondary label.
3. Blast radius is 5 call sites, not 3: AppSidebar.vue:62, RepositoryListScreen.vue:211, ChooseBranchDialog.vue:77, HistoryPane.vue:165, BranchListPane.vue:101.

Two factual errors in the evidence that weaken the presentation but NOT the claim:
- It says "lines 33-38 use $t(label)/placeholder". False — SearchField.vue contains no $t at all. Lines 34-35 are plain prop bindings (:placeholder="placeholder", :aria-label="label"), which is correct for a presentational component.
- It names 3 call sites; there are 5.

That the omission is unintentional (not a deliberate language-neutral design) is proven by all five callers carefully localising :label and :placeholder while the component still emits one raw string. common.search: "搜索" already exists in zh-CN.ts, so common.clearSearch is the natural sibling. No test guards this: interactionCompleteness.test.ts walks .vue sources with an allowlist but only checks @click bindings; no test scans literal template attributes. The proposed source-scan check is sound and idiomatic. Bonus guard worth knowing: catalog.test.ts fails when a zh-CN value is a byte-for-byte copy of the English, so a lazy fix of clearSearch: "Clear search" would be caught.

Severity minor confirmed (not raised). No crash, no functional breakage, and @keydown.escape="clear" is a working keyboard alternative. It is an a11y-consistency defect in a low-traffic affordance, fixed by one line plus two catalogue entries — not release-blocking. "major" would overstate it since no user is functionally blocked.

Adjacent note, outside this finding: SearchField.vue:14 defaults `placeholder` to the literal "Search". Unreachable today (all five callers pass an explicit translated placeholder) but the same class of latent drift.

refuted.title: Right-click on a branch row is inert and suppresses the OS context menu

verifiers.reasoning:
I re-traced every hop and found no missed handler, no guard, and no default that the auditor overlooked — the mechanical trace is accurate. What breaks the finding is that the "missing" capability is not missing.

VERIFIED AS STATED (all line numbers exact in /tmp/meridian-baseline):
- src/components/panes/BranchListPane.vue:126 does bind `@contextmenu.prevent="emit('contextmenu', filtered[index].fullName, $event)"`, and line 36 does declare the emit.
- src/App.vue:1593 does bind `@contextmenu="() => {}"` — payload dropped.
- src/layout/SidebarRow.vue:39 `@contextmenu.prevent="onContextMenu"` -> line 28 emit -> src/layout/AppSidebar.vue:57 `rowContextmenu` -> src/App.vue:1424 `@row-contextmenu="() => {}"`. Chain confirmed end to end.
- BranchListPane declares checkout/merge/rebase/delete/rename at lines 38-42; App.vue:1595-1599 wires all five to real handlers (checkoutFlow, mergeBranch, rebaseBranch, deleteBranch, renameBranchFlow); the template emits only refresh/create/update:filter/update:search/select/activate/contextmenu. The five are indeed never fired.

WHY IT IS NOT A BUG:

1. Every verb the finding says is unreachable is reachable, right next to the list. App.vue:1606-1621 renders BranchDetailPane in the adjacent #detail slot of the same MasterDetail, always mounted for the selected branch, with real buttons: @checkout, @merge-into-current, @rebase-onto, @push/@pull, @rename, @remove. So "nothing happens at all" is false for the user's goal — the verbs exist as discoverable UI. Row dblclick -> activate -> checkoutFlow (App.vue:1592) also works, as the finding itself notes.

2. The context-menu feature was never in scope, so the empty handler is a deliberate stub, not a broken wire. Corroborating evidence, all checked:
   - src/i18n/locales/ contains ZERO menu strings (grep -i "menu" over src/i18n/ returns nothing). A designed menu would have labels.
   - There is no menu component anywhere in the tree — the only match for *menu*.vue is src/components/common/FilterMenu.vue, which is the per-pane view-settings Popover, unrelated.
   - No native Tauri menu: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json has no menu config, src-tauri/src/lib.rs has no menu setup. SenderTag::SidebarContextMenu in src-tauri/src/domain/sender.rs:12 is an unused enum variant, not a handler.
   - No spec section requires it: the only mention of "context menus" in docs/ is docs/04-ui-spec.md:385, which describes the *reference app's* quick-actions palette, not a requirement for Meridian.
   - No global contextmenu listener exists (grepped every addEventListener in src/).
   This is a 0.1.0 skeleton (package/product version 0.1.0, 6 test files total), and App.vue carries 15 `() => {}` stubs — @contextmenu x2, @file-contextmenu x2, @hunk-action x2, @annotate, @select-line, @close-popover, @open-commit, @follow-rename, @retry x3. Same pattern at App.vue:1492 (WorkingCopyPane), :1560 and :1655 (CommitDetailPane). The auditor reported one instance of a project-wide placeholder pattern and read it as a defect.

3. `.prevent` is doing the right thing here, not hiding a failure. In a Tauri v2 app the webview is WKWebView; right-click would otherwise surface the webview's own Reload / Inspect Element menu. Suppressing that in a desktop shell is standard practice. So dropping `.prevent` (the finding's proposed fallback) would make things worse, not better.

4. The sidebar half is partly redundant anyway. Local branch rows set hasOptions: true (App.vue:267), which renders the hover-revealed `.row-options` ellipsis (SidebarRow.vue:58-66) wired through @options -> AppSidebar:55 -> App.vue:1422 `@row-options="checkoutFlow(...)"`. That is a discoverable, keyboard-focusable equivalent of the right-click intent. Only remote-branch rows (App.vue:270-278) lack the ellipsis — and for those, the row still selects on click and the full verb set lives in the Branches tab.

The residue worth keeping is code hygiene, not a defect: BranchListPane.vue:38-42 declares five emits that no code path can fire, and App.vue:1593/1424 leave two component contracts permanently unsubscribed. That is dead wiring in a scaffold, worth a TODO or a delete — but it is not a silent failure of shipped behavior, so "not-a-bug" is the honest classification.

No files were modified; the working tree is clean and /tmp/meridian-baseline is not a git repo, so there is nothing half-applied to commit.

refuted.title: Every `xxx.refresh()` call without a repository sends `repo: undefined`, so those refreshes always fail

verifiers.reasoning:
REFUTED — the finding conflates the composable's `refresh()` with the store's `refresh(repo)`, two different functions that share a name.

`src/App.vue:127-129` binds `workingCopy = useWorkingCopy()`, `branches = useBranches()`, `history = useHistory()` — composables imported at App.vue:40/44/46. App.vue contains zero imports from `./stores` (verified by grep), so these identifiers can never be rebound to a store instance; the auditor's premise that a bare `.refresh()` reaches `commands.branchList` directly is impossible.

Each composable exposes a zero-argument `refresh()` that resolves the repository itself and guards the empty case:
- src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:26-29 — `const id = activeRepo(); if (id) await store.refresh(id);`
- src/composables/useBranches.ts:28-31 — `if (id) await store.refresh(id, search.value);`
- src/composables/useHistory.ts:31-34 — `if (id) await store.refresh(id);`

`repos.selectedId` is a real RepoId on the repro path — it is set when a repository is opened (src/stores/repos.ts:62, 79, 91, 125), which is the precondition of the stated repro ("Open a repo, press Cmd+Shift+R").

The store signatures the auditor cites as proof of breakage (src/stores/workingCopy.ts:26, src/stores/branches.ts:24, src/stores/history.ts:85) are the *deeper* layer, invoked only by the composables, which always hand it a resolved id. So `repo` is never `undefined` at src/bridges/commands.ts:139 and serde never sees a missing field. All cited call sites are correct as written: App.vue:976 (onHunkAction), 1342-1344 (palette), 1374 (Cmd+Shift+R), 1490/1545/1602 (pane @refresh), 1664-1665 (@diff-retry / @diff-show-anyway). src/composables/useGit.ts:32-34 is the only place holding stores directly, and it correctly passes `repo`.

The finding's own test idea (scan App.vue for `\.refresh\(\)` and fail on no argument) would be a guaranteed false positive against correct code.

Note on the session mismatch: the relayed user request was "你老是改一半为啥不提交" (why do you keep changing halfway without committing), which is unrelated to this audit and cannot be expressed in this schema. The parent should address that question directly in its own thread; the snapshot at /tmp/meridian-baseline is read-only and was not modified.

refuted.title: `selectedBranchName` survives a repository switch, so the branch pane and Push can address another repository's branch

verifiers.reasoning:
The premise is right but the conclusion does not follow. `selectedBranchName` (src/App.vue:1085) does survive a repo switch — none of the six watchers (461, 520, 958, 1075, 1118, 1390) reset it, and `repositories.select` (src/stores/repos.ts:90-93) only sets `selectedId`. But four things the auditor missed defeat the stated harm.

(1) The branch pane is not on screen at the moment of the switch. `openRepository` (App.vue:526-529) navigates to `repositoryPath(id)` with no `tab` query; `activeTab` (App.vue:196-198) then falls back to `working-copy`, and RepositoryScreen only renders the `branches` slot when `tab === 'branches'`. So the user cannot press 推送 while looking at A's branch.

(2) Once the user clicks the Branches tab, `selectedBranchInfo` (App.vue:1089-1094) resolves against `branches.branches.value`, which `useBranches`' watcher (useBranches.ts:20-26) has already refreshed to B's list. BranchDetailPane then renders B's data in full — name, `branch.oid.slice(0,7)`, `branch.tipSummary`, `upstream`, `ahead`/`behind` (BranchDetailPane.vue:74-113). The pane is describing B's branch with B's own commit, so what the user reads is what Push publishes.

(3) The id and the name derive from the same selection, so they cannot diverge. `useGit.repoId()` returns `repos.selectedId` (useGit.ts:28-30) = B, and the branch list was refreshed for that same B. The finding presents this as the defect ("the name is consumed with the *new* repo's id and remote"); it is in fact the invariant that holds. The codebase already holds selections to their owning repo elsewhere — `reconcileSelection` in stores/history.ts:61-69 drops a selection absent from the loaded set, and `compare.forRepo` (App.vue:520-524) resets on repo change.

(4) The destructive verbs cannot reach a null-branch fallback. `?? selectedBranchName` at App.vue:1611-1617 only evaluates when `selectedBranchInfo` is null, and every one of those buttons sits inside `<template v-else>` of `v-if="!branch"` (BranchDetailPane.vue:66-75), so the pane renders an EmptyState instead. Delete additionally passes through a confirm dialogue that prints the branch name (App.vue:815-828).

What genuinely remains is a stale selection that can auto-resolve onto a same-named branch in the new repo, so B's pane opens with a row already highlighted rather than empty — a real inconsistency with the compare pane's explicit reset, worth fixing, but not a silent cross-repository publish. Two adjacent things I found while checking, neither being the reported bug: `useBranches` watches `repos.selectedId` while `activeRepoId` prefers `route.params.repoId`, so a browser Back between two `?tab=branches` routes changes the header repo without refreshing the list; and `refresh` assigns `branches.value` only after its `await` (stores/branches.ts:27-38), so the detail pane — a sibling of the loading-guarded list — can briefly show the previous repo's oid and tip summary under the new repo's header.

crossCutting: The only guard against dead controls is structurally blind to exactly this failure mode. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts proves that 'every emitted event is listened for' by regexing event NAMES across all sources and asserting each name appears somewhere — so binding `@contextmenu="() => {}"` in App.vue satisfies it. Fifteen such bindings exist in App.vue alone (lines 1424, 1492, 1560, 1568, 1593, 1655, 1663, 1679-1682, 1686-1687, 1705, 1747). Every one of them renders a translated, enabled, screen-reader-announced control. Fix once, not per finding: make the check reject empty arrow bodies (and no-op identifiers), or delete the controls.

One `LoadState` type serves two different jobs — 'what should I render' and 'did the last action work' — and each store picks its own failure convention. branches turns throws into `null`/`false` plus a shared `lastError` (stores/branches.ts:46-95); history nulls the graph and swallows (stores/history.ts:79-84); repos empties `remotes` on failure (stores/repos.ts:49-51); workingCopy lets a mutation error replace the entire tab. The result is that 'failed' and 'there is none' are pixel-identical in every surface, and the message the user sees depends on which store the verb happened to go through. Fix once: one result type carrying the `ErrorPayload`, one reporting path, and mutation errors that never overwrite list state.

There is no in-flight guard and no cancellation anywhere in the app. `useGit.busy` is set and read by nobody; the only guard in the codebase is the `inFlight` promise in useApp.ts; the Rust queue serialises per repository but the UI neither shows nor blocks queued work. Every verb is double-clickable, fetch/push/clone/install cannot be abandoned, and every async store load (history query, branch list, remotes) is last-response-wins with no generation counter, so a slow earlier response can overwrite a faster later one. Fix once: a per-repo operation registry (start / settle / cancel + request token) that every verb goes through and that simultaneously drives the disabled state and the activity chip.

Selection and query state is duplicated between shell refs and the stores that own the data, and the copies silently drift. `branchSearch`/`branchFilter` (App.vue:1086-1087) never reach `useBranches.search`, so the engine-side `search` argument of `branch_list` is always empty; `historySearch`/`historyView` are shell refs that re-drive the store through an undebounced watcher (App.vue:1075); `selectedBranchName`, `selectedSidebarId`, `paletteQuery` are all shell-local. Fix once: one owner per piece of state, in the store, with the shell holding only view state that has no server meaning.

Limits and capacities are decided ad hoc per surface and mostly fail silently: diffs truncate at 40k lines, history pages at 250, branches load everything and filter locally, the activity list caps at 50, remotes load all. Each surface decides on its own whether truncation is visible, which is why the working-copy findings about silent diff truncation and about rows that can never appear are two instances of one missing contract. Fix once: a `Paginated`/`Truncated` field on `LoadState` that every load must state, rendered by one component.

Error presentation is decided at the call site, not at a boundary: raw engine English, a shell toast, or a ListShell error arm, chosen per verb; the i18n `errors.byCode` catalogue is bypassed. `useAppEvents` is the only place with a systematic rule (ignore events for another repo) and it does not extend to the stores' own awaits. Fix once: a single error-to-catalogue mapping at the reporting boundary, plus the repo-id check on every async store result.

Nothing re-reads state that changed outside the app's own commands. Refreshes come only from `refsChanged`/`workingCopyChanged` events and the explicit ⌘⇧R / palette refresh — no window-focus refresh, no file watcher — and even the manual refresh skips `compare` and the remotes list. An edit made in a terminal leaves the entire window stale until the user remembers the shortcut.

All state is global singleton state: one `repos.selectedId`, one history selection, one branch selection, one toast list, one dialogue queue, one activity list — with no per-window isolation and no request tagging. Every cross-repo correctness question in the findings (a status delta from the previous repo, an event arriving after a switch, a queue entry outliving its operation) is an instance of this one structural choice.
